text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
And the earth was waste and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters.
And God said: “Let there be light,” and there was light.
And God saw the light that it was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.
And God said: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters.”
And God made the firmament and separated the waters that were under the firmament from the waters that were above the firmament. And it was so.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.
And God said: “Let the waters under the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so.
And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
And God said: “Let the earth put forth vegetation, plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind, upon the earth.” And it was so.
And the earth brought forth vegetation, plants yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.

And God said: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth and to separate the day from the night, and let them be for signs and for seasons and for days and years,
and let them be for lights in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
And God set them in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.
And God said: “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures and let fowl fly above the earth across the firmament of the heavens.”
And God created the great sea monsters and every living creature that creeps, with which the waters swarmed, after their kinds, and every winged fowl after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
And God blessed them, saying: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply on the earth.”
And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.
And God said: “Let the earth bring forth living creatures after their kind, cattle and creeping things and the beast of the earth after their kind.” And it was so.
And God made the beast of the earth after their kind and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing upon the ground after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

And God said: “Let us make man in our image, and after our likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God created man in his image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

And God blessed them, and God said to them: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the fowl of the heavens and over every living thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God said: “Behold, I have given you every plant seeded with seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which there is fruit seeded with seed; you shall have them for food.

And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to every creeping creature upon the earth, in which there is a living soul, [I have given] every green plant for food.” And it was so.
And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
And God finished on the sixth day his work that he had done, and he rested on the seventh day from all his work that he had done.
And God blessed the seventh day and hallowed it, because on it he rested from all his work that God had done in creation.
These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that Shema God made heaven and earth.
And no bush of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for Shema God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground,
but there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.
Then Shema God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and Adam became a living soul.
And Shema God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and there he put the man whom he had formed.

And out of the ground Shema God made to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food . And also in the midst of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
And a river went out of Eden to water the garden, and there it parted and became four heads.
The name of the first is Fishon. It is the one which flows around the whole land of Ābbila, where the gold is,
and the gold of that land is very good; the bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
And the name of the second river is Giyyon. It is the one which flows around the whole land of Kosh.
And the name of the third river is Addeqel. It is the one which flows east of Ashor. And the fourth river is Farat.
And Shema God took the man and put him into the garden of Eden to till it and to keep it.
And Shema God commanded the man, saying: “Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat,
but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for on the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.”
And Shema God said: “It is not good that the man should be alone. I will make a helper fit for him.”

And Shema God formed again out of the ground every beast of the field, and every fowl of the heavens, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them, and whatever the man would call every living creature, that was to be its name.
And the man gave names to all the cattle, and to the fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper fit for him.
And Shema God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept, and he took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
And the rib, which Shema God had taken from the man, he made a woman, and brought her to the man.
And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of her man.”
Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and shall cleave to his wife, and of both of them shall become one flesh.
And they were both naked, Adam and his wife, and were not ashamed.
And the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field that Shema God had made. And he said to the woman: “Did God really say ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
And the woman said to the serpent: “Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat,
but of the fruit of this tree that is in the midst of the garden, God said ‘You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.’”
And the serpent said to the woman: “You shall not surely die,
for God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be as God, knowing good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took of its fruits, and ate, and she also gave to her husband, who was with her, and they ate.
And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves aprons.
And they heard the sound of Shema God walking in the garden during the day. And Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Shema God among the trees of the garden.
And Shema God called to the man and said to him: “How [are you]?”
And he said: “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.”
And he said: “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten of the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”
And the man said: “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.”
And Shema God said to the woman: “What is this that you have done?” And the woman said: “The serpent beguiled me, and I ate.”

And Shema God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and above all beasts of the field; upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.”
And to the woman he said: “I will greatly multiply your pain and your childbearing; in pain you shall bring forth children. And your return shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you.”

And to Adam he said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you, saying: ‘You shall not eat of it,’ cursed is the ground for your sake; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
Thorns also and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to your dust you shall return.”
And the man called his wife’s name Abba, because she was the mother of all those who are alive.
And Shema God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them.
And Shema God said: “Behold, the man has become as one of us, to know good and evil, and now, lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life and eat, and live forever.”
Therefore Shema God sent him out from the garden of Eden to till the ground from which he was taken.
He drove out the man, and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the whirling sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.
And the man knew Abba his wife, and she conceived and bore Qen, and said: “I have gotten a man from Shema.”
And again, she bore his brother Ebel. Now Ebel was a keeper of sheep, and Qen was a tiller of the ground.
Now in the course of time Qen brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to Shema,
and Ebel too brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fattest of them. And Shema had regard for Ebel and for his offering,
but to Qen and to his offering he had no regard. And Qen was very angry, and his face fell.
And Shema said to Qen: “Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
Behold, if you do well, you will be forgiven, and if you do not do well, at the door of sin crouch! And to you is its return, but you can rule over it.”
And Qen said to Ebel his brother: “Let us go out to the field.” And when they were in the field, Qen set upon his brother Ebel and killed him.
And Shema said to Qen: “Where is Ebel your brother?” And he said: “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
And he said: “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood is crying to me from the ground.
And now you are cursed more than the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the ground, it shall no longer yield to you its strength. A fugitive and a wanderer you shall be on the earth.”
And Qen said to Shema: “My punishment is too great to bear.
Behold, you have driven me out this day from the face of the ground, and from your face I shall be hidden, and I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
And Shema said to him: “Therefore whoever kills Qen, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” And Shema set a sign on Qen, lest anyone who finds him should kill him.
And Qen went away from the presence of Shema, and dwelt in the land, wandering east of Eden.
And Qen knew his wife, and she conceived, and bore Inok. And he built a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son Inok.
And to Inok was born Irad, and Irad begot Miyyaʾel, and Miyyaʾel begot Metushaʾel, and Metushaʾel begot Lemek.
And Lemek took to himself two wives. The name of the one was ʿAda, and the name of the other Ṣala.
And ʿAda bore Yabal. He was the father of those who dwell in tents and [have] cattle.
And his brother’s name was Yubal. He was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe.
And Ṣala, she also bore Tubal-qen, the forger of all instruments of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-qen was Nēmma.
And Lemek said to his wives: “ʿAda and Ṣala, hear my voice; you wives of Lemek, listen to my speech. I have killed a man for my wound, and a young man for my bruising.
If Qen is avenged sevenfold, then Lemek seventy-seven-fold.”
And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son, and he called his name Shat, for [he said]: “God has appointed for me another offspring instead of Ebel, for Qen killed him.”
And as to Shat, he also begot a son, and he called his name Enosh. At that time he began to invoke the name of Shema.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day God created man, he made him in the likeness of God.
Male and female he created them, and he blessed them and named them Man when they were created.
And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot [a son] in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Shat.
The days of Adam after he begot Shat were eight hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
And Shat lived one hundred and five years, and begot Enosh.
Shat lived after he begot Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Shat were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And Enosh lived ninety years, and begot Qinan.
Enosh lived after he begot Qinan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
And Qinan lived seventy years, and begot Māllelel.
Qinan lived after he begot Māllelel eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Qinan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died
And Māllelel lived sixty-five years, and begot Yarad.
Māllelel lived after he begot Yarad eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Māllelel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
And Yarad lived sixty-two years, and begot Inok.
Yarad lived after he begot Inok seven hundred and eighty- five years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Yarad were eight hundred and forty-seven years, and he died.
And Inok lived sixty-five years, and begot Metushala.
Inok walked with God after he begot Metushala three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Inok were three hundred and sixty-five years.
Inok walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
And Metushala had lived sixty- seven years, and begot Lemek.
Metu- shala lived after he begot Lemek six hundred and fifty-three years, and be- got sons and daughters.
All the days of Metushala were seven hundred and twenty years, and he died.
And Lemek lived fifty-three years, and begot a son,
and called his name Na, saying: “Out of the ground which Shema has cursed this one shall comfort us from our deeds and from the toil of our hands.”
Lemek lived after the birth of Na six hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
All the days of Lemek were six hundred and fifty-three years, and he died.
Na was five hundred years old, and begot Shem, Ām, and Yefet.
And when men began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were fair. And they took them for wives, of all that they chose.
And Shema said: “My spirit shall not strive with man forever, because he is also flesh. Yet his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”

And the Nefilem were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of God came into the daughters of men, and they begot children with them. These were the mighty men that were of old, the men of renown.
And Shema saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the time.
And Shema regretted that he had made the man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
And Shema said: “I will blot out the man, whom I have created, from the face of the ground, from man to beast, to creeping thing, to fowl of the heavens, for I regret that I have made them.”
But Na found favour in the eyes of Shema.
These are the generations of Na. Na was a righteous man and perfect in his generations. Na walked with God.
And Na begot three sons: Shem, Ām and Yefet.
And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
And God saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way upon the earth.
And God said to Na: “The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence through them. And, behold, I will destroy them from the earth.
Make yourself an ark of gopher wood; you shall make rooms in the ark, and shall pitch it within and without with pitch.
And this is how you shall make it: The length of the ark three hundred cubits, and fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
A light you shall make to the ark, and to a cubit you shall finish it upward. And the door of the ark you shall set in its side; with lower, second, and third [decks] you shall make [it].
And I, behold, I do bring the flood, waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under heaven; everything that is in the earth shall perish.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons, and your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
And of every beast and of all the flesh, two of every [kind] you shall bring into the ark, to keep them alive with you, male and female. And it will be
of the fowl after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, and of everything that creeps on the ground after their kinds, two of every [kind] shall come in to you, to keep them alive.
And you, take with you of all food that is eaten, and gather it to you, and it shall be for you and for them as food.”
And Na did according to all that God commanded him; so he did.
And God said to Na: “Come you and all your household, into the ark, for you [alone] I have seen righteous before me in this generation.
Of every clean beast you shall take to you seven and seven, male and female, and of the beasts that are not clean two and two, male and female.
And also of the fowl of the heavens, the clean ones, seven and seven, male and female, to keep offspring alive upon the face of all the earth.
For in seven days, I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every living thing that I have made from the face of the earth.”
And Na did according to all that Shema commanded him.
And Na was six hundred years old when the flood was, waters upon the earth.
And Na and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives, went in with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
Of the clean beasts, and of the beasts that are not clean, and of the fowl, and of all that creeps upon the ground,
two and two came to Na into the ark, male and female, as Shema commanded Na.
And after the seven days, the waters of the flood were upon the earth,

in the six hundredth year of Na’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
On the very same day Na, Shem, Ām, and Yefet, the sons of Na, and Na’s wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, entered the ark.

They, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird, every winged thing.
And they came to Na into the ark, two and two of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
And they that entered, male and female, male and female of all flesh went in, as God commanded him, and Shema shut him in.
And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and bore up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth.
And the waters prevailed, and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark went upon the face of the waters.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and they covered all the high mountains under the whole heavens.
Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail, and they covered the mountains.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth perished, both fowl, and cattle, and beast, and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and every man.
All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was on the dry land, died.

And every living thing which was upon the face of the ground was blotted out, from man to cattle, to creeping thing, to fowl of the heavens, and they were blotted out from the earth. And Na only was left, and those that were with him in the ark.
And the waters prevailed upon the earth one hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Na, and every living thing, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark. And God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
And the fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were stopped, and [God] ceased the rain from the heavens.
And the waters receded from off the earth continually. And the waters decreased at the end of one hundred and fifty days.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Araraṭ.
And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
And at the end of forty days, Na opened the window of the ark which he had made.
And he sent out a raven, and it went to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth.
And he sent out a dove from him to see if the waters were abated from the face of the ground.

But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him, to the ark, for the waters were on the face of the whole earth. So he put out his hand, and took her, and brought her in to him into the ark.
And he waited another seven days, and again he sent out the dove out of the ark.
And the dove came in to him in the evening, and lo, a plucked olive leaf was in her mouth. So Na knew that the waters were abated from the earth.
And he waited another seven days, and sent out the dove. And she did not again return to him any more.

And in the six hundred and first year, in the first [month], on the first [day] of the month, the waters had dried up from the earth. And Na removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dried.
And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
And God spoke to Na, saying:
“Go out from the ark, you, and your wife, and your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.

And every living thing that is with you of all flesh, both fowl, and cattle, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth bring out with you, that they may swarm on the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.”
And Na went out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him,
and every beast, and every fowl and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, after their families, went out of the ark.
And Na built an altar to Shema, and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burned offerings on the altar.

And Shema smelled the sweet savour. And Shema said in his heart: “I will never again curse the ground any more for man’s sake, for the inner thoughts of man’s heart are evil from his youth, neither will I ever again destroy every living thing, as I have done.
As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, by day and night shall not cease.”
And God blessed Na and his sons, and said to them: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the heavens, and upon everything with which the ground teems, and upon all the fish of the sea, into your hand I have delivered it.
Every creeping thing that lives shall be food for you; as the green plants I have given you all.
But flesh with its life, [which is] its blood, you shall not eat.
And your blood of your lives I will require; at the hand of every living [thing] I will require it; at the hand of the man, at the hand of man and his brother, I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds man’s blood, by man his blood shall be shed, for in the image of God he made the man.
And you, be fruitful, and multiply and swarm upon the earth, and multiply upon it.”
And God said to Na and to his sons with him, saying:
“And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
and with every living creature that is with you, the fowl and the cattle, and every beast of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ark, every beast of the earth.
And I will establish my covenant with you, that never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.”
And God said: “This is the sign of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
I set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
And when I bring clouds over the earth, and the bow is seen in the clouds,
I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature that is with you of all flesh, and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bow shall be in the cloud, and you will see [it], as a reminder of an everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.”
And God said to Na: “This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.”
And the sons of Na that went out from the ark, were Shem, Ām, and Yefet. And Ām is the father of Kaˈnan.
These three were the sons of Na, [and] of these the whole earth was overspread.
And Na the tiller of the soil began to plant a vineyard.
And he drank of the wine and got drunk, and he uncovered himself in his tent.
And Ām, the father of Kaˈnan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.

And Shem and Yefet took the garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father, and their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
And Na awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
And he said: “Cursed be Kaˈnan, a servant of servants he shall be to his brothers.”
And he said: “Blessed be Shema, the God of Shem, and let Kaˈnan be their servant.
May God embellish Yefet, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem, and let Kaˈnan be their servant.”
And Na lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
And all the days of Na were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
Now these are the generations of the sons of Na: Shem, Ām and Yefet. And they begot sons after the flood.
The sons of Yefet: Gamar, and Magog, Madi, and Yaban, Tubal, and Mushak, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gamar: Ashkenaz, Rifat, and Tagrema.
And the sons of Yaban: Illesh, and Tarshesh, Kittem, and Rudanem.
Of these were the foundations of the nations separated in their lands, everyone after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
And the sons of Ām: Kosh, and Miṣrem, Foṭ, and Kaˈnan.
And the sons of Kosh: Saba, and Ābbila, Sabta, and Rēmma, and Sabbitka. And the sons of Rēmma: Shaba and Dadan.
And Kosh begot Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before Shema; therefore it is said: “Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before Shema.”
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Arek, and Ikkad, and all of them were in the land of Shinniyyar.
Out of that land he went to Ashor, and built Ninabe and Rabot-īr, and Kalla,
and Rissan between Ninabe and Kalla, that is the great city.
And Miṣrem begot Lāddem, and Inamem, and Lābbem, and Naftaʾem,
and Fitrasem, and Kaslaʾem—from whence came the Philistines—and Kaftarrem.
And Kaˈnan begot Ṣidon his first-born and At,
and the Yebusite, and the Emarite, and the Girgeshite,
and the Ibbite, and the ʿAroqite, and the Senite,
and the Arbaddite, and the Ṣamrite, and the Ametite, and afterward the family of the Kaˈnanite was spread abroad.
And the territory of the Kaˈnanite was from the river of Miṣrem to the great river, the river Farat, and to the western sea.
These are the sons of Ām, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
And as to Shem—the father of all the children of Ebar, the elder brother of Yefet—he also begot.
The sons of Shem: Ilam, and Ashor, and Arfakshad, and Led, and Aram.
And the sons of Aram: Ūṣ, and Ābbel, Gatar, and Masha.
And Arfakshad begot Shala, and Shala begot Ebar.
And to Ebar were born two sons. The name of the one was Falag, for in his days was the earth divided, and his brother’s name was Yiqṭan.
And Yiqṭan begot Ilmudad, and Shalef, and Iṣrimot, and Yara,
and Eduram, and Izal, and Daqle,
and Ibal, and Abimaʾel, and Shaba,
and Afar, and Ābbila, and Yubab. All these were the sons of Yiqṭan.
And their dwelling was from Masha, as you go toward Sifra, to the mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Na, after their generations, in their nations. Of these were divided the foundations of the nations in the earth after the flood.
And the whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
And as they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinniyyar and they dwelt there.
And they said one to another: “Come, let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” And they had the brick for stone, and the bitumen they had for mortar.
And they said: “Come, let us build us a city and a tower, with its top in heavens, and let us make for ourselves a reputation, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.”
And Shema came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men had built.
And Shema said: “Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language, and this is what they have begun to do; and now nothing will be withheld from them, which they will purpose to do.
Come, let us go down, and spoil lips there, that no man may understand another’s speech.”
And Shema scattered them abroad from there upon the face of all the earth, and they left off building the city and the tower.
Therefore its name was called Babel, because there Shema did confound the language of all the earth; and from there did Shema scatter them upon the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem. Shem was one hundred years old, and begot Arfakshad two years after the flood.
And Shem lived after he begot Arfakshad five hundred years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Shem were six hundred years, and he died.
And Arfakshad lived one hundred and thirty-five years, and begot Shala.
And Arfakshad lived after he begot Shala three hundred and three years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Arfakshad were four hundred and thirty-eight years, and he died.
And Shala lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Ebar.
And Shala lived after he begot Ebar three hundred and three years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Shala were four hundred and thirty-three years, and he died.
And Ebar lived one hundred and thirty-four years, and begot Falag.
And Ebar lived after he begot Falag two hundred and seventy years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Ebar were four hundred and four years, and he died.
And Falag lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Reʾu.
And Falag lived after he begot Reʾu one hundred and nine years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Falag were two hundred and thirty-nine years, and he died.
And Reʾu lived one hundred and thirty-two years, and begot Sharog.
And Reʾu lived after he begot Sharog one hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Reʾu were two hundred and thirty-nine years, and he died.
And Sharog lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Naʾor.
And Sharog lived after he begot Naʾor one hundred years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Sharog were two hundred and thirty years, and he died.
And Naʾor lived seventy-nine years, and begot Tara.
And Naʾor lived after he begot Tara sixty-nine years, and begot sons and daughters. And all the days of Naʾor were one hundred and forty-eight years, and he died.
And Tara lived seventy years, and begot Abram, Naʾor, and Arran.
These are the generations of Tara. Tara begot Abram, Naʾor, and Arran; and Arran begot Loṭ.
And Arran died in the presence of his father Tara in the land of his birth, in Or-kishdem.
And Abram and Naʾor took for themselves wives; the name of Abram’s wife was Sharri, and the name of Naʾor’s wife, Milka, the daughter of Arran, the father of Milka, and the father of Yiska.
And Sharri was barren; she had no child.

And Tara took Abram his son and Loṭ the son of Arran, his son’s son, and Sharri and Milka his two daughters-in-law, his son Abram’s wife and Naʾor, his sons, and he brought them from Orkishdem to go into the land of Kaˈnan; and they came to Arran and dwelt there.
And the days of Tara were one hundred and forty-five years; and Tara died in Arran.
And Shema said to Abram: “Go forth from your country and from your kindred and from your father’s house to the land that I will show you.
And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great, and you shall be a blessing.
And I will bless those who bless you, and those who curse you, them I will curse; and by you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”
And Abram went, as Shema had told him; and Loṭ went with him; and Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Arran.

And Abram took Sharri his wife, and Loṭ his brother’s son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Arran; and they went forth to go into the land of Kaˈnan; and they came to the land of Kaˈnan.
And Abram passed through the land to the place of Ashkem, to Alon-mura. And the Kaˈnanite was then in the land.
And Shema appeared to Abram, and said to him: “To your offspring I will give this land.” And he built there an altar to Shema, who had appeared to him.

And he moved from there to the mountain on the east of Bit-el, and pitched his tent, having Bit-el on the west and Aˈʾi on the east, and he built there an altar to Shema and invoked the name of Shema.
And Abram journeyed, still going toward the south.
And there was famine in the land, and Abram went down to Miṣrem to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.
And when he was about to enter Miṣrem, he said to Sharri his wife: “Behold, I know that you are a fair woman to look upon.
And when the Egyptians see you, they will say ‘This is his wife,’ and they will kill me, but you they will keep alive.
Say, I pray you, you are my sister, that it may go well with me for your sake, and that my soul may live because of you.”
And when Abram came into Miṣrem, the Egyptians saw the woman that she was very fair.
And the princes of Faru saw her, and praised her to Faru. And the woman was taken into Faru’s house.
And Abram was well treated for her sake; and he had sheep, and oxen, a lot of cattle, men-servants, and maid-servants, asses, and she-asses, and camels.
And Shema plagued Faru and his house with great plagues because of Sharri, Abram’s wife.
And Faru called Abram, and said: “What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
And why did you say ‘She is my sister’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife, take her, and be gone.”
And Faru gave men orders concerning him; and they sent him away, with his wife and all that he had, and Loṭ with him.
And Abram went up out of Miṣrem, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Loṭ with him, into the south.
And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
And he went on his journeys from the south as far as Bit-el, to the place where his tent had been at first, between Bit-el and Aˈʾi,
to the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first; and Abram called there on the name of Shema.
And Loṭ, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
And the land could not bear them, that they might dwell together, for their possessions were great, so that they could not dwell together.
And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s cattle and the herdsmen of Loṭ’s cattle. And the Kaˈnanite and the Ferizzite dwelt then in the land.
And Abram said to Loṭ: “Let there be no strife, I pray you, between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen; for we are kinsmen.
Behold, the whole land is before you! Separate yourself, I pray you, from me. If you [take] the left hand, [I will go] to the right; or if you [take] the right hand, [I will go] to the left.”

And Loṭ lifted up his eyes and saw all the plain of the Yardan, that all of it was well watered, before Shema destroyed Sadem and Emirra, like the garden of Shema, like the land of Miṣrem, as you go to Ṣār.
And Loṭ chose for himself all the plain of the Yardan, and Loṭ journeyed from the east, and they separated themselves the one from the other.
Abram dwelt in the land of Kaˈnan, and Loṭ dwelt in the cities of the plain, and pitched tent as far as Sadem.
And the men of Sadem were wicked and sinners against Shema exceedingly.
And Shema said to Abram, after Loṭ had separated from him: “Lift up now your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward;
for all the land which you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
And I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth; so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring shall also be counted.
Arise, walk through the land, in the length of it and in the breadth of it, for I will give it to you.”
And Abram began [his journey], and came and dwelt by Aluni-mamri, which is in Ibron, and built there an altar to Shema.
And in the days of Amrafel king of Shinniyyar, and Aryabok king of Alasar, Kadar-lamar king of Ilam, and Teˈdal king of Guwwem,
they made war with Bara king of Sadem, and with Birsha king of Emirra, and Shaˈnab king of Idma, and Shamʾabbad king of Ṣabuwwem, and the king of Bala—that is, Ṣār.
All these joined together in the Valley of Shiddem—that is, the Salt Sea.
Twelve years they served Kadar-lamar, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year came Kadar-lamar and the kings that were with him, and defeated the Refaʾem in Ishtarot-qarnem, and the Zuzaʾem in Ām, and the Imem in Shebi-qaryatem,
and the Arrites in the Mountains of Shaʾer, as far as Il-farran, which is by the wilderness.
And they turned back, and came to In-mashfaṭ—that is, Qadesh—and defeated all the country of the ʿAmaleqites, and also the Emarites, that dwelt in Aṣaṣon-tamar.

And there went out the king of Sadem, and the king of Emirra, and the king of Idma, and the king of Ṣabuwwem, and the king of Bala—that is, Ṣār—and they set battle against them in the Valley of Shiddem
against Kadar-lamar king of Ilam, and Teˈdal king of Guwwem, Amrafel king of Shinniyyar, and Aryabok king of Alasar, four kings against the five.
And the Valley of Shiddem was full of bitumen pits; and the king of Sadem and the king of Emirra fled, and they fell there, and those that remained fled to the mountain.
And they took all the goods of Sadem and Emirra, and all their provisions, and went their way.
And they took Loṭ, the son of Abram’s brother, and all his goods, and he departed, and he was dwelling in Sadem.
And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew, who was dwelling by Aluni-mamri the Emarite, brother of Ishkol and brother of Inniram; and these were the allies of Abram.
And Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, and he equipped his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
And he divided [his forces] against them by night, he and his servants, and defeated them, and pursued them to Uba, which is north of Damsheq.
And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother Loṭ, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.
And the king of Sadem went out to meet him, after his return from the defeat of Kadar-lamar and the kings that were with him, at the Valley of Shebi—that is, the King’s Valley.
And Malki-ṣedeq king of Shalem brought out bread and wine; and he was priest of God Most High.
And he blessed Abram, and said: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth;
and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” And he gave him a tenth of everything.
And the king of Sadem said to Abram: “Give me the persons, and take the goods for yourself.”
And Abram said to the king of Sadem: “I have lifted up my hand to God, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,
[that I will not take] a thread nor a sandal-thong nor will I take anything that is yours, lest you should say ‘I have made Abram rich.’
Save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men which went with me: Inniram, and Ishkol, and Mamri; let them take their portion.”
After these things the word of Shema came to Abram in a vision, saying: “Do not fear, Abram, I am your shield, and your reward I shall increase greatly.”
And Abram said: “O Lord Shema, what will you give me, and I walk childless, and he that is in charge with my house is Eliyyazar of Damsheq?”
And Abram said: “Behold, you have given me no offspring, and, lo, one born in my house will be my heir.”
And, behold, Shema spoke to him, saying: “This one shall not be your heir, but he that shall come forth out of your own bowels shall be your heir.”
And he brought him out, and said: “Look toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” And he said to him: “So shall your offspring be.”
And he believed in Shema, and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.
And he said to him: “I am Shema that brought you out of Or-kishdem, to give you this land to inherit it.”
And he said: “O my Lord Shema, how shall I know that I shall inherit it?”
And he said to him: “Bring me a heifer three years old, and a female goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
And he brought him all these, and surely divided them, and laid each half over against the other; but the birds he did not divide.
And the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, and Abram turned them back.
And as the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and lo, a dread, a great darkness, fell upon him.
And it was said to Abram: “Know for certain that your offspring shall be a sojourner in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them, and they shall afflict them four hundred years;
and also the nation, that will enslave them, I will judge; and afterward they shall come out with great possessions.
And you shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.
And the fourth generation shall come back here; for the iniquity of the Emarite is not yet full.”
And the sun went down and there was thick darkness, and behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
On that day Shema made a covenant with Abram, saying: “To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Miṣrem to the great river, the river Farat,
the Qenite, and the Qenazite, and the Qadamonite,
and the Atite, and the Ferizzite, and the Refaʾem,
and the Emarite, and the Kaˈnanite, and the Girgeshite, and the Ibbite, and the Yebusite.”
And Sharri, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. And she had a handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Agar.

And Sharri said to Abram: “Behold now, Shema has restrained me from bearing children; go in, I pray you, to my hand-maid; it may be that I shall obtain children through her.” And Abram heeded the voice of Sharri.
And Sharri, Abram’s wife, took Agar the Egyptian, her handmaid, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Kaˈnan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.
And he went in to Agar, and she conceived; and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
And Sharri said to Abram: “My wrong be upon you. I gave my handmaid to your embrace, and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes. May Shema judge between me and you.”
But Abram said to Sharri: “Behold, your maid is in your hand. Do to her that which is good in your eyes.” And Sharri dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her.
And the angel of Shema found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain on the way to Shor.
And he said: “Agar, Sharri’s hand-maid, Woe! Where have you come from and where are you going?” And she said: “I flee from my mistress Sharri.”
And the angel of Shema said to her: “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hand.”
And the angel of Shema said to her: “I will greatly multiply your offspring, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.”
And the angel of Shema said to her: “Behold, you are with child, and shall bear a son; and you shall call his name Yishmaʾel, because Shema has heard your affliction.
And he shall be a prolific man, his hand shall be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell over against all his kinsmen.”
And she called the name of Shema that spoke to her “You are a God who sees,” for she said: “Here too I have seen [God] after seeing [him]!”
Therefore she called the well Bir-laʾi-raʾi; behold, it is between Qadesh and Barad.
And Agar bore Abram a son; and Abram called the name of his son, whom Agar bore, Yishmaʾel.
And Abram was eighty-six years old, when Agar bore Yishmaʾel to Abram.
And Abram was ninety-nine years old, and Shema appeared to Abram, and said to him: “I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be perfect.
And I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
And Abram fell on his face; and God talked with him, saying:
“And as for me, behold, my covenant is with you, and you shall be the father of a multitude of nations.
No longer shall your name be called Abram any more, but your name shall be Abˈram, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
And I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come out of you.
And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your offspring after you.
And I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land of your sojourning, all the land of Kaˈnan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.”
And God said to Abˈram: “And as for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.
This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you. Behold, circumcise every male among you.
And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between me and you.

And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any foreigner, that is not of your offspring.
Behold, one circumcised shall circumcise those born in your house, and those bought with your money, and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
And any uncircumcised male who will not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.”
And God said to Abˈram: “As for Sharri your wife, you shall not call her name Sharri, but Sharra shall be her name.
And I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her; and will bless him, and she shall be [a mother of] nations; and kings of peoples shall come from her.”
Then Abˈram fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart: “At the age of one hundred years shall I beget? Or Sharra, at ninety years, shall she bear?”
And Abˈram said to God: “Oh that Yishmaʾel might live before You!”

And God said: “But behold, Sharra your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yeˈṣaq; and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant and for his offspring after him.
And as for Yishmaʾel, I have heard you. Behold, I will bless him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.
And my covenant I will establish with Yeˈṣaq, whom Sharra shall bear to you at this set time in the next year.”
And he finished talking with him. And God went up from Abˈram,

and Abˈram took Yishmaʾel his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abˈram’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, as God had said to him.
And Abˈram was ninety-nine years old, at the circumcision of the flesh of his foreskin.
And Yishmaʾel his son was thirteen years old, at the circumcision of the flesh of his foreskin.
On that very day Abˈram and Yishmaʾel his son were circumcised.
And all the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money of a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
And Shema appeared to him by Aluni-mamri, as he sat at the tent door in the heat of the day.
And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood in front of him. And when he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them, and bowed down to the earth,
and said: “My lord, if now I have found favour in your sight, do not pass by your servant.
Let now a little water be fetched, and wash your feet, and recline yourselves under the tree.
And I will fetch a morsel of bread, and strengthen your heart. And after that you shall pass on, since you have come to your servant.” And they said: “Do as you have said.”
And Abˈram hurried into the tent to Sharra, and said: “Quickly knead three measures of fine meal, and make cakes.”
And Abˈram ran to the herd, and fetched a calf tender and good, and gave it to the servant, and he hurried to dress it.
And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them. And he stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
And they said to him: “Where is Sharra your wife?” And he said: “Behold, in the tent.”
And he said: “I will surely return to you according to the time of life, and, lo, Sharra your wife shall have a son.” And Sharra was listening at the tent door, and she was behind him.
Now Abˈram and Sharra were old, advanced in age. It had ceased to be with Sharra after the manner of women.
And Sharra wondered within herself, saying: “After I have withered, shall I have pleasure, my lord being old?”
And Shema said to Abˈram: “Why did Sharra wonder, saying: ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, and I am old?’
Is anything too hard for Shema? At the set time I will return to you, according to the time of life, and Sharra shall have a son.”
Then Sharra denied, saying: “I did not wonder,” for she was afraid. And he said to her: “But you did wonder.”
And the men rose from there, and looked toward Sadem. And Abˈram went with them to set them on the way.
And Shema said: “Shall I hide from Abˈram what I am about to do,
seeing that Abˈram shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I have known that Abˈram may command his children and his house-hold after him, that they may keep the way of Shema, to do righteousness and justice, so that Shema may bring upon Abˈram that which he has spoken of him.”
And Shema said: “[Because] the outcry of Sadem and Emirra is great, and because their sin is very grievous,
I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry of it, that has come to me. And if not, I will know.”
And the men turned from there, and went toward Sadem, but Abˈram stood still before Shema.
And Abˈram drew near, and said: “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?
Perhaps there are fifty righteous within the city; will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are there?

Far be it from you to do such a thing, to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked. Far be it from you. Behold! The Judge of all the earth shall not do right!”
And Shema said: “If I find in Sadem fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
And Abˈram answered and said: “Behold now, I have taken upon myself to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes.
Perhaps there are five of the fifty righteous lacking. Will you destroy the whole city for lack of five?” And he said: “I will not destroy it, if I find there forty-five.”
And he yet again spoke to him, and said to him: “Perhaps there are forty there.” And he said: “I will not destroy it for the sake of forty.”
And he said: “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak. Perhaps there are thirty there.” And he said: “I will not destroy it, if I find thirty there.”
And he said: “Behold now, I have taken upon myself to speak to the Lord. Perhaps there are twenty there.” And he said: “I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”
And he said: “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once. Perhaps there are ten there.” And he said: “I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.”
And Shema went his way, as soon as he had finished talking with Abˈram, and Abˈram returned to his place.
And the two angels came to Sadem in the evening, and Loṭ was sitting in the gate of Sadem. When Loṭ saw them, he rose to meet them, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.

And he said: “Behold now, my lords, turn aside, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and spend the night, and wash your feet, and you shall rise up early, and go on your way.” And they said: “No, we will spend the night in the square.”
And he urged them strongly. And they turned in to him, and entered his house. And he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sadem, both young and old, all the people from every quarter, surrounded the house.
And they called to Loṭ, and said to him: “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them.”
And Loṭ went out to them to the door, and they shut the door after him.
And he said: “I pray you, my brothers, do not act so wickedly.

Behold now, I have two daughters that have not known man. Let me, I pray you, bring them out to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes. Only to these men do nothing, for they came under the shadow of my roof.”

And they said: “Stand back.” And they said: “This one came in to sojourn, and he will also act as judge. Now we will deal worse with you, than with them.” And they pressed hard upon the man Loṭ, and drew near to break the door.
But the men put out their hand, and brought Loṭ into the house to them, and shut the door.
And they struck the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.
And the angels said to Loṭ: “Have you anyone else here? Son-in-law, your sons, and your daughters, and anyone you have in the city, bring them out of this place.
For we will destroy this place, because their outcry has become great before Shema, and Shema has sent us to destroy it.”
And Loṭ went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who married his daughters, and said: “Up, get out of this place, for Shema will destroy the city.” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.
And when the morning dawned, the angels hastened Loṭ, saying: “Rise, take your wife, and your two daughters that are here, lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city,”

and he lingered. And the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters, in Shema’s mercy on him, and they brought him out, and set him outside the city.
And when they had brought them out outside, one said: “Escape for your life. Do not look behind you, nor stay in all the plain. Escape to the mountain, lest you be consumed.”
And Loṭ said to them: “Oh, no, my lord.

Behold now, your servant has found favour in your sight, and you have magnified your kindness, which you have showed to me in saving my life. But I cannot escape to the mountains, lest evil overtake me, and I die.
Behold now, this city is near to flee to, and it is small. Oh let me escape there for it is small, and my soul shall live.”
And he said to him: “Behold, I have granted you this request also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
Hurry! Escape there, for I cannot do anything until you come there.” Therefore the name of the city was called Ṣār.
The sun had risen upon the earth when Loṭ came to Ṣār.
Then Shema caused it to rain upon Sadem and upon Emirra brimstone and fire from Shema out of heaven.
And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and the vegetation of the ground.
And his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abˈram went early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Shema.
And he looked toward Sadem and Emirra, and toward the face of all the land of the plain, and beheld, and, lo, the smoke of the land rose like the smoke of a furnace.
So it was that, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abˈram, and sent Loṭ out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Loṭ dwelt.
And Loṭ went up from Ṣār and dwelt in the mountains with his two daughters, for he feared to dwell in Ṣār. And he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters with him.
And the first-born said to the younger: “Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father.”
And they made their father drink wine that night. And the first-born went in, and lay with her father. And he did not know when she lay down, nor when she rose.

And on the next day the first-born said to the younger: “Behold, I lay last night with my father. Let us make him drink wine tonight also; then you go in, and lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father.”
And they made their father drink wine that night also. And the younger rose, and lay with him. And he did not know when she lay down, nor when she rose.
Thus both the daughters of Loṭ became pregnant by their father.
And the first-born bore a son, and called his name Muwwab; he is the father of the Muwwabites to this day.
And the younger, she also bore a son, and called his name Ban-ʿammi; he is the father of the children of ʿAmmon to this day.
And Abˈram journeyed from there toward the land of the south, and dwelt between Qadesh and Shor. And he sojourned in Gerar.
And Abˈram said of Sharra his wife: “She is my sister.” And Abimelek king of Gerar sent, and took Sharra.
But God came to Abimelek in a dream of the night, and said to him: “Behold, you are about to die, on account of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man’s wife.”
So Abimelek had not come near her. And he said: “Lord, will you slay even a righteous nation?
Behold, he himself said to me ‘She is my sister’! And she even said ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.”
And God said to him in the dream: “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also withheld you from sin against me. Therefore, I did not let you touch her.
And now restore the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for you, and you shall live. But if you don’t restore [her], know that you shall surely die, you and all that are yours.”
And Abimelek rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their hearing. And all the men were very much afraid.

And Abimelek called Abˈram, and said to him: “What have you done to us? And what is my sin against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done.”
And Abimelek said to Abˈram: “What were you thinking that you have done this thing?”
And Abˈram said: “Because I was afraid, because I thought ‘Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
And indeed she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother. And she became my wife.

And when God caused me to wander from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, I said to her ‘This is your kindness which you shall do to me. At every place to which we come, say of me ‘He is my brother.’’”
And Abimelek took one thousand pieces of silver, and sheep, and oxen, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and gave them to Abˈram, and restored Sharra his wife to him.
And Abimelek said: “Behold, my land is before you. Dwell where it pleases you.”
And to Sharra he said: “Behold, I have given your brother one thousand pieces of silver. Behold, it is for you a vindication and to all that are with you. And in respect of all you are justified.”
And Abˈram prayed to God. And God healed Abimelek, and his wife, and his maid-servants, so that they bore children.
For God had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelek, because of Sharra, Abˈram’s wife.
And Shema visited Sharra as he had said, and Shema did to Sharra as he had spoken.
And Sharra conceived, and bore Abˈram a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
And Abˈram called the name of his son that was born to him, whom Sharra bore to him, Yeˈṣaq.
And Abˈram circumcised his son Yeˈṣaq when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
And Abˈram was one hundred years old, when his son Yeˈṣaq was born to him.
And Sharra said: “God has made laughter for me. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
And she said: “Who would have said to Abˈram, that, behold, Sharra would suckle children? Yet I have borne to him a son in his old age.”
And the child grew, and was weaned. And Abˈram made a great feast on the day that Yeˈṣaq his son was weaned.
And Sharra saw the son of Agar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abˈram, mocking.
And she said to Abˈram: “Cast out this handmaid and her son. For the son of this handmaid shall not be heir with my son, with Yeˈṣaq.”
And the thing was very grievous in Abˈram’s sight on account of his son.

And God said to Abˈram: “Let it not be grievous in your sight because of the lad and because of your handmaid. In all that Sharra said to you, listen to her voice. For in Yeˈṣaq shall your offspring be called.
And also of the son of this handmaid will I make a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

And Abˈram rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and gave it to Agar, putting it on her shoulder, along with the child, and sent her away. And she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Bir-shaba.
And the water in the skin was spent, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

And she went, and sat down over against [him]; she got far about the distance of a bowshot, for she said: “Let me not look upon the death of the child.” And she sat over against [him], and lifted up her voice, and wept.
And God heard the voice of the lad. And the angel of God called to Agar from heaven, and said to her: “What troubles you, Agar? Do not fear, for God has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
Rise, lift up the lad, and hold him in your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”
And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad drink.
And God was with the lad, and he grew. And he dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer lad.
And he dwelt in the wilderness of Farran. And his mother took him a wife from the land of Miṣrem.
And at that time Abimelek and Fi-kal the captain of his host said to Abˈram, saying: “God is with you in all that you do.

Now therefore swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my offspring, nor with him who is in front of me. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land within which you have sojourned.”
And Abˈram said: “I will swear.”
And Abˈram complained to Abimelek about the well of water, which Abimelek’s servants had seized.
And Abimelek said: “I do not know who has done this thing; neither did you tell me, neither had I heard of it until today.”
And Abˈram took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelek, and the two of them made a covenant.
And Abˈram set seven ewe lambs of flock by themselves.
And Abimelek said to Abˈram: “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?”
And Abˈram said: “Indeed, the seven ewe lambs you shall take of my hand, that it may be a witness to me that I have dug this well.”
Therefore he called that place Bir-shaba, because there they swore both of them.
So they made a covenant at Bir-shaba. And Abimelek rose, and Fi-kal the captain of his host, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
And Abˈram planted a tamarisk tree in Bir-shaba, and invoked there the name of Shema, the Everlasting God.
And Abˈram sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
And after these things God tested Abˈram, and said to him: “Abˈram.” And he said: “Here I am.”
And he said: “Take now your son, your only son, whom you love, Yeˈṣaq, and go to the land of Muriyya, and offer him there as a burned offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell you.”

And Abˈram rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Yeˈṣaq his son. And he cut the wood for the burned offering, and arose, and went to the place of which God had told him
on the third day. And Abˈram lifted up his eyes, and saw the place from afar.
And Abˈram said to his young men: “Stay here with the ass, and I and the lad will go over there and we will worship, and come back to you.”
And Abˈram took the wood of the burned offering, and laid it on Yeˈṣaq his son. And he took in his hand the fire and the knife. And they went both of them together.
And Yeˈṣaq spoke to Abˈram his father, and said: “My father.” And he said: “Here I am, my son.” And he said: “Behold, the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb for a burned offering?”
And Abˈram said: “God will provide the lamb for a burned offering himself, my son.” And they went both of them together.
And they came to the place of which God had told him. And Abˈram built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Yeˈṣaq his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood.
And Abˈram stretched out his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
And the angel of Shema called to him from heaven, and said: “Abˈram, Abˈram.” And he said: “Here I am.”
And he said: “Do not lay your hand upon the lad or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”

And Abˈram lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, there was one ram caught in the thicket by his horns. And Abˈram went and took the ram, and offered him up [as] a burned offering instead of his son.
And Abˈram called the name of that place Shema-yērēʾi. As it is said to this day: “On the mountain Shema shall be seen.” >— —
And the angel of Shema called to Abˈram a second time from heaven,
and said: “By myself I have sworn, says Shema, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son, from me,
I will surely bless you, and I will greatly multiply your offspring as the stars of the heavens and as the sand that is upon the sea-shore. And your offspring shall possess the cities of his enemies.
And in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice.”
And Abˈram returned to his young men, and they rose and went together to Bir-shaba. And Abˈram dwelt in Bir-shaba.
And after these things it was told to Abˈram, saying: “Behold, Milka, she also has borne children to your brother Naʾor.
Oṣ his first-born, and Boz his brother, and Qamuwwel the father of Aram,
and Kashad, and Ezu, and Fildash, and Yidlaf, and Aftuwwel.”
And Aftuwwel begot Rubqa. These eight did Milka bear to Naʾor, Abˈram’s brother.
And his concubine, whose name was Ruma, she also bore Ṭaba, and Gām, and Tāsh, and Mākke.
And the life of Sharra was one hundred and twenty-seven years. [These were] the years of the life of Sharra.
And Sharra died in Qaryat-aʾarba at the vale—that is, Ibron, in the land of Kaˈnan, and Abˈram came to lament for Sharra, and to mourn for her.
And Abˈram rose up from before his dead woman, and spoke to the children of At, saying:
“I am a stranger and a sojourner with you. Give me a possession of a burying place with you, that I may bury my dead woman out of my sight.”
And the children of At answered Abˈram, saying: "Not so.
Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. In the choicest of our sepulchers bury your dead woman. None of us shall withhold his sepulcher from you, from burying your dead woman.”
And Abˈram rose, and bowed down to the people of the land, the children of At.
And he spoke with them, saying: “If it pleases your mind that I should bury my dead woman out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me Ifron the son of Ṣār the Atite,
that he may give me the cave of Makfela, which he has, which is at the end of his field. For the full price let him give it to me in the midst of you for a possession of a burial place.”
Now Ifron was sitting in the midst of the children of At. And Ifron the Atite answered Abˈram in the hearing of the children of At, all that went in at the gate of his city, saying:
“No, my lord, hear me. The field I give you, and the cave that is in it I give it to you. In the presence of the children of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead woman.”
And Abˈram bowed down before the people of the land.
And he spoke to Ifron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying: “But if you are with me, hear me. I will give the price of the field. Take it of me, and I will bury my dead woman there.”
And Ifron answered Abˈram, saying: “No,
my lord, listen to me. A piece of land [worth] four hundred shekels of silver, what is that between me and you? Bury therefore your dead woman.”
And Abˈram listened to Ifron. And Abˈram weighed out for Ifron the silver which he had named in the hearing of the children of At, four hundred shekels of silver, current among the merchants.

So the field of Ifron, which was in Makfela, which was before Mamri, the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were throughout its whole area, were made over
to Abˈram for a possession in the presence of the children of At, before all that went in at the gate of his city.
And after this, Abˈram buried Sharra his wife in the cave of the field of Makfela before Mamri—that is, Ibron—in the land of Kaˈnan.
And the field, and the cave that is in it, were made over to Abˈram for a possession of a burying place by the children of At.
And Abˈram was old, and well advanced in age. And Shema had blessed Abˈram in all things.
And Abˈram said to his servant, the elder of his house, that ruled over all that he had: “Put, I pray you, your hand under my thigh,
and I will make you swear by Shema, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Kaˈnanites, among whom I dwell.
But you shall go to my country and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Yeˈṣaq.”
And the servant said to him: “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I then bring your son back to the land from which you came?”
And Abˈram said to him: “Beware not to bring my son back there.

Shema, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying: ‘To your offspring I will give this land,’ he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath of mine. Only you shall not bring my son back there.”
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abˈram his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels, from his master’s camels, and departed, having all his master’s goodly things in his hand. And he rose, and went to Aram-naram, to the city of Naʾor.
And he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.
And he said: “O Shema, the God of my master Abˈram, I pray you, grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abˈram.
Behold, I am standing by the fountain of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

And let the maiden to whom I shall say ‘Let down your jug, I pray you, that I may drink.’ And she shall say ‘Drink, and I will give your camels drink also’—let her be the same that you have appointed for your servant Yeˈṣaq. And thereby I shall know that you have shown kindness to my master Abˈram.”
And before he had finished speaking in his heart, behold, Rubqa who was born to Aftuwwel the son of Milka, the wife of Naʾor, Abˈram’s brother, came out with her jug upon her shoulder.
And the maiden was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her. And she went down to the fountain, and filled her jug, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said: “Let me drink, I pray you, a little water from your jug.”
And she said: “Drink, my lord.” And she quickly let down her jug upon her hand, and gave him drink.
And when she had done giving him drink, she said: “I will draw for your camels also, until they have done drinking.”
And she hurried, and she let down her jug to the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
And the man gazed at her and held his peace, to know whether Shema had made his journey a success or not.
And as the camels had done drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight and put it upon her nose, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
and said: “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, I pray you, is there room in your father’s house for us to lodge?”
And she said to him: “I am the daughter of Aftuwwel, the son of Milka, whom she bore to Naʾor.”
And she said to him: “We also have enough straw and fodder, and also room to lodge.”
And the man bowed down, and worshipped before Shema.

And he said: “Blessed be Shema, the God of my master Abˈram, who has not forsaken his lovingkindness and his truth toward my master Abˈram. As for me, Shema has led me in the way to the house of my master’s kinsman.”
And the maiden ran, and told her mother’s house about these things.
And Rubqa had a brother, and his name was Laban; and Laban ran out to the man, to the fountain.

And it was when he saw the ring, and the bracelets upon his sister’s arms, and when he heard the words of Rubqa his sister, saying: “Thus the man spoke to me,” he came to the man. And, behold, he was standing by the camels at the fountain.
And he said: “Come in, O blessed of Shema. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
And the man came into the house, and he ungirded the camels, and gave straw and fodder for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men that were with him.
And there was set food before him to eat, but he said: “I will not eat, until I have told my errand. And they said: “Speak on.”
And he said: “I am Abˈram’s servant.
And Shema has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great, and he has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, men-servants and maid-servants, and camels and asses.
And Sharra my master’s wife bore a son to my master when he was old, and he has given him all that he has.
Now my master made me swear, saying: ‘you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Kaˈnanites, in whose land I dwell.
But you shall go to my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.’
And I said to my master ‘Perhaps the woman will not follow me.’
And he said to me ‘Shema, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and make your journey a success, and you shall take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house.
Then you shall be clear from my oath, when you come to my kindred. And if they will not give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
And I came to the fountain today, and said ‘O Shema, the God of my master Abˈram, if only you make the journey on which I go successful.
Behold, I am standing by the fountain of water, and let the maiden that comes out to draw, to whom I shall say ‘Give me, I pray you, a little water from your jug to drink,’
and who shall say to me ‘Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,’ let her be the woman whom Shema has appointed for my master’s son.’

And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rubqa came out with her jug on her shoulder, and she went down to the fountain, and drew. And I said to her ‘Let me drink, I pray you, a little water from your jug.’
And she hurried, and let down her jug from her shoulder, and said ‘Drink, and I will give your camels drink also.’ So I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
And I asked her, and said ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said ‘The daughter of Aftuwwel, Naʾor’s son, whom Milka bore to him.’ And I put the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her arms.
And I bowed down, and worshipped before Shema, and blessed Shema, the God of my master Abˈram, who had led me in the right way to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
And now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”
Then Laban and Aftuwwel answered and said: “The thing proceeds from Shema. We cannot speak to you bad and good.
Behold, Rubqa is before you; take her, and go, and let her be the wife of your master’s son, as Shema has spoken.”
