And when Abˈram’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself to the earth to Shema.
And the servant brought out jewelry of silver, and jewelry of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rubqa. He also gave precious things to her brothers and to her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night. When they rose in the morning, he said: “Send me away to my master.”
And her brothers and her mother said: “Let the maiden stay with us for a few days, or a month. And after that she shall go.”
And he said to them: “Do not hinder me, now that Shema has made my journey a success. Send me away that I may go to my master.”
And they said: “We will call the maiden, and inquire at her mouth.”
And they called Rubqa, and said to her: “Will you go with this man?” And she said: “I will go.”
So they sent away Rubqa their sister, and her nurse, and Abˈram’s servant, and his men.
And they blessed Rubqa, and said to her: “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring possess the gate of his enemies.”
And Rubqa and her maidens rose, and they rode on the camels, and followed the man. Thus the servant took Rubqa, and went on his way.
And Yeˈṣaq came in the desert of Bir-laʾi-raʾi, for he dwelt in the land of the south.
And Yeˈṣaq went out to meditate in the field in the evening. And he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
And Rubqa lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Yeˈṣaq, she dismounted from the camel.
And she said to the servant: “What man is this that walks in the field to meet us?” And the servant said: “It is my master.” And she took her veil, and covered herself.
And the servant told Yeˈṣaq all the things that he had done.
And Yeˈṣaq brought her into the tent of Sharra his mother, and took Rubqa, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Yeˈṣaq was comforted after his mother’s [death].
And Abˈram took another wife, and her name was Qiṭṭura.
And she bore him Zimron, and Yiqshan, and Maddan, and Madyan, and Yishbaq, and Shu.
And Yiqshan begot Shaba, and Dadan. And the sons of Dadan were Ashurem, and Laṭṭashem, and Lāmmem.
And the sons of Madyan were Ifa, and Afar, Inok, and Abida, and Ilˈda. All these were the children of Qiṭṭura.
And Abˈram gave all that he had to Yeˈṣaq his son.
But to the sons of the concubines that Abˈram had, Abˈram gave gifts, and he sent them away from Yeˈṣaq his son, while he was still living, eastward, to the east country.
And these are the days of the years of Abˈram’s life which he lived, one hundred and seventy-five years.
And Abˈram expired, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of days, and was gathered to his peo- ple.
And Yeˈṣaq and Yishmaʾel his sons buried him in the cave of Mak-fela, in the field of Ifron the son of Ṣār the Atite, which is before Mamri,
the field which Abˈram purchased from the children of At. There Abˈram is buried, and Sharra his wife.
And after the death of Abˈram, God blessed Yeˈṣaq his son. And Yeˈṣaq dwelt by Bir-laʾiraʾi.
Now these are the generations of Yishmaʾel, Abˈram’s son, whom Agar the Egyptian, Sharra’s handmaid, bore to Abˈram.
And these are the names of the sons of Yishmaʾel, by their names, according to their generations: The first-born of Yishmaʾel Nabaʾot, and Qadad, and Adˈbil, and Mabasham,
and Mashma, and Duma, and Masha,
Adad, and Tima, Yeṭor, and Nefesh, and Qadama.
These are the sons of Yishmaʾel, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of the life of Yishmaʾel: one hundred and thirty-seven years. And he expired and died, and was gathered to his people.
And they dwelt from Ābbila to Shor, that is before Miṣrem, as you go toward Ashor. He settled over against all his brothers.
And these are the generations of Yeˈṣaq, Abˈram’s son. Abˈram begot Yeˈṣaq.
And Yeˈṣaq was forty years old when he took Rubqa, the daughter of Aftuwwel the Aramean of Faddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
And Yeˈṣaq entreated Shema for his wife, because she was barren. And Shema was entreated by him, and Rubqa his wife conceived.
And the children struggled together within her, and she said: “If so, why do I [live]?” And she went to seek after Shema.

And Shema said to her: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your bowels. And the one people shall be stronger than the other people, and the elder shall serve the younger.”
And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And the first came out red all over like a hairy garment, and they called his name Ishab.
And after that came out his brother, and his hand held on to Ishab’s heel, so they called his name Yāqob. And Yeˈṣaq was sixty years old when she bore them.
And the boys grew. And Ishab was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Yāqob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.
Now Yeˈṣaq loved Ishab, because he ate of his game, but Rubqa loved Yāqob.
And Yāqob boiled stew. And Ishab came in from the field, and he was faint.
And Ishab said to Yāqob: “Feed me, I pray you, with that same red stew, for I am faint.” Therefore was his name called Edom.
And Yāqob said: “Sell me first your birthright.”
And Ishab said: “Behold, I am about to die, so of what use is a birthright to me?”
And Yāqob said: “Swear to me first.” And he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Yāqob.
And Yāqob gave Ishab bread and stew until satiation, and he ate and drank, and rose, and went on his way. So Ishab despised the birthright.
And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abˈram. And Yeˈṣaq went to Abimelek king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
And Shema appeared to him, and said: “Don’t go down to Miṣrem. Dwell in the land of which I shall tell you.
Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you, for to you, and to your offspring, I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abˈram your father.
And I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven, and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.
Because Abˈram, your father, obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
And Yeˈṣaq dwelt in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked [him] about his wife. And he said: “She is my sister,” for he feared to say “She is my wife.” “Lest,” [said he], “the men of the place should kill me for Rubqa, because she was fair to look upon.”
And when he had been there a long time, Abimelek king of the Philistines looked out of a window, and saw, and, behold, Yeˈṣaq was fondling Rubqa his wife.
And Abimelek called Yeˈṣaq, and said: “Behold, she is your wife; how then could you say ‘She is my sister?’” And Yeˈṣaq said to him: “Because I said ‘Lest I die because of her.’”
And Abimelek said: “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
And Abimelek charged all his people, saying: “He who touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
And Yeˈṣaq sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. And Shema blessed him.
And the man became great, and grew more and more until he became very great.
And he had possessions of flocks, and possessions of herds, and a great household. And the Philistines envied him.
Now all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abˈram his father, the Philistines had stopped up, and filled with earth.
And Abimelek said to Yeˈṣaq: “Go from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
And Yeˈṣaq departed from there, and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.

And Yeˈṣaq dug again the wells of water, which the servants of Abˈram his father had dug, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abˈram. And he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
And Yeˈṣaq’s servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of spring water.
And the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Yeˈṣaq’s herdsmen, saying: “The water is ours.” And he called the name of the well ʿAshaq, because they oppressed his people.
And they dug another well, and they quarreled for that also, so he called the name of it Shiṭna.

And he removed from there, and they dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it, so he called the name of it Rabot, and he said: “For now Shema has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”
And he went up from there to Bir-shaba.

And Shema appeared to him that same night, and said: “I am the God of Abˈram your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abˈram’s sake.”
And he built an altar there, and invoked the name of Shema, and pitched his tent there. And there Yeˈṣaq’s servants dug a well.
Then Abimelek went to him from Gerar, and Aʾezat his friend, and Fi-kal the captain of his host.
And Yeˈṣaq said to them: “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me, and have sent me away from you?”
And they said: “We saw plainly that Shema was with you, so we said ‘Let there be an oath between us, between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you,
that you will do us no evil, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace. Now you are the blessed of Shema.’”
And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
And they arose in the morning, and swore one to another. And Yeˈṣaq sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
And the same day Yeˈṣaq’s servants came, and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him: “We have found water.”
And he called it Sheˈba; therefore the name of the city is Bir-shaba to this day.
And when Ishab was forty years old, he took for a wife Yaʾudet, the daughter of Baʾeri the Atite, and Bashamat, the daughter of Ayyalon the Hiwite.
And they were a source of grief to Yeˈṣaq and to Rubqa.
And when Yeˈṣaq was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Ishab his elder son, and said to him: “My son.” And he said to him: “Here I am.”
And he said: “Behold now, I am old, I don’t know the day of my death.
Now therefore, take, I pray, your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and hunt game for me.
And make me savoury food, such as I love, and you shall bring [it] to me, that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.”
And Rubqa heard Yeˈṣaq’s speech to Ishab his son. And Ishab went to the field to hunt game, [and] to bring [it].
And Rubqa spoke to Yāqob her son, saying: “Behold, I heard your father speak to Ishab your brother, saying:
‘Bring me game, and make me savoury food that I may eat, and bless you before Shema, before my death.’
Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.
Go now to the flock, and fetch me from there two good kids of goats, and I will make of them savoury food for your father, such as he loves.
And you shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
And Yāqob said to Rubqa his mother: “Behold, Ishab my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver, and you shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.”
And his mother said to him: “Upon me be your curse, my son. Only obey my voice, and go bring them to me.”
And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother. And his mother made savoury food, such as his father loved.
And Rubqa took the goodly garments of Ishab her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Yāqob her younger son.
And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck.
And she gave the savoury food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Yāqob.
And he came to his father, and said: “My father.” And he said: “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
And Yāqob said to his father: “I am Ishab your first-born. I have done as you told me. Rise, I pray you, sit and eat of my game, that your soul may bless me.”
And Yeˈṣaq said to his son: “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” And he said: “Because Shema your God granted me success."
And Yeˈṣaq said to Yāqob: “Come near, I pray you, that I may feel you, my son, [so I may know] whether you are really my son Ishab or not.”
And Yāqob went close to Yeˈṣaq his father, who felt him and said: “The voice is Yāqob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Ishab.”
And he did not recognise him, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Ishab’s hands. So he blessed him.
And he said: “Are you my very son Ishab?” And he said: “I am.”
And he said: “Bring [it] near to me, and I will eat of my son’s game, that my soul may bless you.” And he brought it near to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank.
And his father Yeˈṣaq said to him: “Come near now and kiss me, my son.”
And he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his clothes, and blessed him, and said: “See, the smell of my son is as the smell of the full field which Shema has blessed.
And God shall give you of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain, and new wine.

Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone that curses you, and blessed be everyone that blesses you.”
And as soon as Yeˈṣaq had finished blessing Yāqob, and Yāqob had scarcely left the presence of Yeˈṣaq his father, Ishab his brother came in from his hunt.
And he also made savoury food, and brought it to his father. And he said to his father: “Let my father rise, and eat of his son’s game, that your soul may bless me.”
And Yeˈṣaq his father said to him: “Who are you?” And he said: “I am your son, your first-born, Ishab.”
And Yeˈṣaq trembled exceedingly, and said: “Who then hunted game, and brought it to me, and I ate it all before you came, and have blessed him? And indeed he shall be blessed.”
And it came to pass, when Ishab heard the words of his father, that he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father: “Bless me, me also, O my father.”
And he said: “Your brother came with guile, and has taken away your blessing.”

And he said: “Rightly his name is called Yāqob, for he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright, and, behold, now he has taken away my blessing.” And he said: “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?”

And Yeˈṣaq answered and said to Ishab: “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants, and with grain and new wine I have sustained him. And what then shall I do for you, my son?”
And Ishab said to his father: “Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father.” And Ishab lifted up his voice, and wept.
And Yeˈṣaq his father answered and said to him: “Behold, of the fatness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and of the dew of heaven from above.
And by your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother, but when you shall become powerful, you shall shake his yoke from off your neck.”
And Ishab hated Yāqob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Ishab said in his heart: “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Yāqob.”
And the words of Ishab her elder son were told to Rubqa. So she sent and called Yāqob her younger son, and said to him: “Behold, your brother Ishab, comforts himself by planning to kill you.
Now therefore, my son, obey my voice, and rise, flee to Laban my brother, to Arran,
and stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away,
until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you, and fetch you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”

And Rubqa said to Yeˈṣaq: “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of At. If Yāqob takes a wife of the daughters of At, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will life be to me?”
And Yeˈṣaq called Yāqob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him: “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Kaˈnan.
Rise, go to Faddan-aram, to the house of Aftuwwel your mother’s father, and take a wife from there of the daughters of Laban your mother’s brother.
And may God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
and give you the blessing of Abˈram your father, to you, and to your offspring with you, to inherit the land of your so- journing, which Shema gave to Abˈram.”
And Yeˈṣaq sent away Yāqob. And he went to Faddan-aram to Laban, son of Aftuwwel the Aramean, the brother of Rubqa, Yāqob’s and Ishab’s mother.

Now Ishab saw that Yeˈṣaq had blessed Yāqob and sent him away to Faddan-aram, to take him a wife from there, [and that] as he blessed him they charged him, saying: “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Kaˈnan.”
And Yāqob had obeyed his father and his mother, and gone to Faddan-aram.
And Ishab saw that the daughters of Kaˈnan did not please Yeˈṣaq his father.
So Ishab went and took Maʾelat the daughter of Yishmaʾel, Abˈram’s son, the sister of Nabaʾot, to be his wife, besides the wives that he had.
And Yāqob went out from Bir-shaba, to go toward Arran.
And he came upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down to sleep in that place.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven. And behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
And behold, Shema stood above it, and said: “I am Shema, the God of Abˈram your father, and the God of Yeˈṣaq. The land on which you lie, I will give to you and to your offspring.

And your offspring shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south, and in you and in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
Behold, I am with you, and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you again to this land. For I will not leave you, until I have done what I have told you.”
And Yāqob awoke from his sleep, and said: “Surely Shema is in this place, and I did not know it,”
and he was afraid. And he said: “How dreadful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
And Yāqob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
And he called the name of that place Bit-el, but the name of the city was Luza at the first.
And Yāqob vowed a vow, saying: “If God will be with me, and will protect me on this journey that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothes to put on,
so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then Shema will be my God,
and this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, shall be God’s house, and of all that you shall give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
Then Yāqob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
And he looked, and behold, there was a well in the field, and, lo, three flocks of sheep were lying by it, for out of that well they watered the flocks. And a great stone was upon the well’s mouth.
And there all the shepherds were gathered, and they rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well’s mouth in its place.
And Yāqob said to them: “My brothers, where are you from?" And they said: “We are from Arran.”
And he said to them: “Do you know Laban the son of Naʾor?” And they said: “We know him.”
And he said to them: “Is it well with him?” And they said: “It is well. And, behold, Raʾel his daughter comes with the sheep.”
And he said to them: “Lo, it is yet high day; it is not time for the cattle to be gathered together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
And they said: “We cannot, until all the shepherds are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well’s mouth. Then we water the sheep.”
While he was still speaking with them, Raʾel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

And when Yāqob saw Raʾel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Yāqob went up, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
And Yāqob kissed Raʾel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
And Yāqob told Raʾel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rubqa’s son, and she ran and told her father.
And when Laban heard the news about Yāqob his sister’s son, he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him: “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” And he dwelt with him a month’s time.
And Laban said to Yāqob: “Because you are my brother, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?”
And Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Liyya, and the name of the younger was Raʾel.
And Liyya’s eyes were tender, but Raʾel was of beautiful form and fair to look upon.
And Yāqob loved Raʾel. And he said: “I will serve you seven years for Raʾel your younger daughter.”
And Laban said: “It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Dwell with me.”
And Yāqob served seven years for Raʾel, and they seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
And Yāqob said to Laban: “Bring me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
And in the evening he took Liyya his daughter, and brought her to him. And Yāqob went in to her.
And Laban gave Zilfa his handmaid to his daughter Liyya for a handmaid.
And in the morning, behold, it was Liyya. And he said to Laban: “What is this you have done to me? Behold, I have served with you for Raʾel! Why then have you beguiled me?”
And Laban said: “It is not so done in our place, to give the younger before the first-born.
Fulfill the week of this one, and I will give you the other also in return for serving me another seven years.”
And Yāqob did so, and fulfilled her week. And he gave him Raʾel his daughter for a wife.
And Laban gave to Raʾel his daughter Baˈla his handmaid to be her handmaid.
And he went in also to Raʾel, and he loved also Raʾel more than Liyya, and served with him another seven years.
And Shema saw that Liyya was hated, and he opened her womb, but Raʾel was barren.
And Liyya conceived, and bore a son, and she called his name Reʾuben, for she said: “Because Shema has looked upon my affliction, for now my husband will love me.”
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: “Because Shema has heard that I am hated, he has given me this son also.” And she called his name Sheˈmun.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore she called his name Libi.
And she conceived again, and bore a son, and said: “This time I will praise Shema.” Therefore she called his name Yeʾuda. Then she ceased bearing.
And when Raʾel saw that she bore Yāqob no children, Raʾel envied her sister. And she said to Yāqob: “Give me children, or else I shall die.”
And Yāqob’s anger was kindled against Raʾel, and he said: “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from your bowels the fruit of the womb?”
And she said: “Behold my maid-servant Baˈla, go in to her, that she may bear upon my blessing, and I also may obtain children by her.”
And she gave him Baˈla her handmaid for a wife, and Yāqob went in to her.
And Baˈla conceived, and bore Yāqob a son.
And Raʾel said: “God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.
And Baˈla Raʾel’s handmaid conceived again, and bore Yāqob a second son.
And Raʾel said: “With mighty wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and even have prevailed.” So she called his name Niftali.
When Liyya saw that she had ceased bearing, she took Zilfa her handmaid, and gave her to Yāqob for a wife.
And Zilfa Liyya’s hand-maid bore Yāqob a son.
And Liyya said: “By tidings!” So she called his name Gad.
And Zilfa Liyya’s handmaid bore Yāqob a second son.
And Liyya said: “Happy am I! For the daughters will call me happy.” So she called his name Asher.

And Reʾuben went out during the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Liyya. Then Raʾel said to Liyya: “Give me, I pray you, of your son’s mandrakes.”

And she said to her: “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? And would you take away my son’s mandrakes also?” And Raʾel said: “Therefore he shall lie with you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.”

And Yāqob came from the field in the evening, and Liyya went out to meet him, and said: “You must come in to me tonight, for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” And he lay with her that night.
And God listened to Liyya, and she conceived, and bore Yāqob a fifth son.
And Liyya said: “God has given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband.” So she called his name Yashishakar.
And Liyya conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Yāqob.
And Liyya said: “God has endowed me with a good dowry; now my husband will dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons.” So she called his name Zebulan.
And afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dina.
And God remembered Raʾel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.
And she conceived, and bore a son, and said: “God has taken away my reproach.”
So she called his name Yusef, saying: “May Shema add to me another son.”
And when Raʾel had borne Yusef, Yāqob said to Laban: “Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served with you, and let me go, for you know my service which I have served you.”
And Laban said to him: “If now I have found favour in your eyes, I have divined that Shema has blessed me because of you.”
And he said: “Name your wages, and I will give it.”
And he said to him: “You know how I have served you, and how your cattle have been with me.
For it was little which you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude; and Shema has blessed you because of me, and now when shall I provide for my own house also?”
And he said: “What shall I give you?” And Yāqob said: “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again shepherd your flock and keep it.

I will pass through all your flock today, removing from it every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. And [such] shall be my hire.

So shall my righteousness answer for me hereafter, when it shall come concerning my hire that is before you. Everyone that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that if found with me, shall be counted stolen.”
And Laban said: “And if not, let it be according to your words.”

And he removed that day the male goats that were striped and spotted, and all the male goats that were speckled and spotted, everyone that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons,

and he set three days’ journey between them and Yāqob, and Yāqob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks. [a] And the angel of God said to Yāqob in the dream, and he said: “Yāqob.” And [Yāqob] said: “Here I am.” [b] And he said: “Lift up now your eyes, and see, all the male goats which leap upon the flock are striped, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban had done to you. [c] I am the God of Bit-el, where you anointed a pillar, and where you vowed a vow to me. And now rise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your father and I will do you good.”
And Yāqob took rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond and of the plane-tree, and peeled white streaks in them, exposing the white which was in the rods.
And he set the rods which he had peeled before the flocks in the gutters, at the watering troughs, where the flocks came to drink; and they bred when they came to drink.
And the flocks bred before the rods, and the flocks brought forth striped, speckled, and spotted.
And Yāqob separated the lambs, and set before the flocks a striped ram and all the dark ones in Laban’s flock. And he put his own droves apart, and did not put them with Laban’s flock.
And it came to pass, whenever the stronger of the flock were breeding, that Yāqob laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that they might breed among the rods,
but when the flock were feeble, he did not put them in, so that the feebler were Laban’s and the stronger Yāqob’s.
And the man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, and maid-servants and men-servants, and camels and asses.
And he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying: “Yāqob has taken away all that was our father’s, and of that which was our father’s he has gotten all this glory.”
And Yāqob saw Laban’s countenance, and, behold, it is not toward him as before.
And Shema said to Yāqob: “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
And Yāqob sent and called Raʾel and Liyya to the field to his flock,
and said to them: “I see your father’s countenance, that it is not toward me as before, but the God of my father has been with me.
And you know that with all my power I have served your father.
And your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but Shema did not permit him to hurt me.
If he said ‘The speckled shall be your wages’, then all the flock bore speckled, and if he said ‘The striped shall be your wages’, then all the flock bore striped.
Thus Shema has taken away the cattle of your father, and give them to me.
And at the breeding time of the flock, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the male goats which leaped upon the flock were striped, speckled, and grizzled.
And the angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Yāqob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’
And he said, ‘Lift up now your eyes, and see, all the male goats which leap upon the flock are striped, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.
I am the God of Bit-el, where you anointed a pillar, and where you vowed a vow to me. And now rise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’”
And Raʾel and Liyya answered and said to him: “Is there left for us any portion or inheritance in our father’s house?
Behold, we are accounted by him as strangers! For he has sold us, and has also quite devoured our money.
For all the riches which Shema has taken away from our father, that is ours and our children’s. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.”
Then Yāqob rose, and set his wives and his sons on the camels.
And he drove away all his cattle, and all his substance which he had gathered, the cattle of his getting, which he had gathered in Faddan-aram, to go to Yeˈṣaq his father to the land of Kaˈnan.
Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Raʾel stole the household gods that were her father’s.
And Yāqob outwitted Laban the Aramean, in not telling him that he was fleeing.
So he fled with all that he had, and he arose, and passed over the river, and set his face toward the mountain of Gaˈlad.
And Laban was told on the third day that Yāqob had fled.
And he took his brothers with him, and pursued him for seven days, and he overtook him in the mountain of Gaˈlad.
And God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream of the night, and said to him: “Take heed not to speak to Yāqob either good or bad.”
And Laban came up to Yāqob. Now Yāqob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his brothers encamped in the mountain of Gaˈlad.
And Laban said to Yāqob: “What have you done that you have outwitted me, and carried away my two daughters as captives of the sword?
Why did you flee secretly, and steal away from me, and did not tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth, with singers, with tambourine and with harp;
and did not permit me to kiss my sons and my two daughters? Now you have done foolishly.
It is in the power of my hand to do you harm, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying: ‘Take heed not to speak to Yāqob either good or bad.’
And now, you have surely gone, because you longed greatly after your father’s house, [but] why have you stolen my gods?”
And Yāqob answered and said to Laban: “Because I was afraid, for I said ‘Lest you would take your two daughters from me by force.’
With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live. Before our brothers discern what of yours is with me, and take it to you.” For Yāqob did not know that Raʾel had stolen them.
And Laban went in and searched Yāqob’s tent, and into Liyya’s tent, and into the tent of the two hand-maids, but he did not find them. And he went out of Liyya’s tent, and entered into Raʾel’s tent.
Now Raʾel had taken the household gods, and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat upon them. And Laban felt about all the tent, but did not find them.
And she said to her father: “Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before you, for the manner of women is upon me.” And he searched, but did not find the household gods.
And Yāqob was angry, and berated Laban, and Yāqob answered and said to Laban: “What is my crime and what is my sin, that you have pursued me?
And whereas you have felt about all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set [it] here before my brothers and your brothers, that they may judge between us two.
It is twenty years that I have been with you; your ewes and your male goats have not cast their young, the rams of your flocks I have not eaten.
That which was torn of beasts I did not bring to you. I bore the loss of it of my hand, [whether] stolen by day or stolen by night.
[Thus] I was, in the day cold consumed me, and frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.
It is twenty years that I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

If the God of my father, the God of Abˈram, and the Fear of Yeˈṣaq, had not been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty-handed, with my affliction and with the labour of my hands. God saw and rebuked [you] last night.”

And Laban answered and said to Yāqob: “The daughters are my two daughters, and the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine. But what can I do this day to these my two daughters, or to their children who were born to them?
And now come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it be for a witness between you and me.”
And Yāqob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
And Yāqob said to his brothers: “Gather stones.” And they took stones, and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.
And Laban called it Yagar-shaʾeduta, but Yāqob called it Gal-ed.
And Laban said: “This heap is witness between me and you this day.” Therefore its name was called Gal-ed.
And the pillar, for he said: “Shema watch between you and me, when we are absent one from another.
If you afflict my two daughters, and if you take wives besides my two daughters, no seeing man is with us. God is witness between you and me.”
And Laban said to Yāqob: “Behold this heap, and behold the pillar, which you have cast between you and me.
This heap be witness, and the pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me to do harm.
The God of Abˈram, and the God of Naʾor judges between us, the God of Abˈram.” And Yāqob swore by the Fear of his father Yeˈṣaq.
And Yāqob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his brothers to eat bread, and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mountain.
And Laban rose early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. And Laban departed and returned to his place.
And Yāqob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
And Yāqob said when he saw them: “This is God’s host.” And he called the name of that place Manem.
And Yāqob sent messengers before him to Ishab his brother to the land of Shaʾer, the field of Edom.
And he commanded them, saying: “Thus you shall say to my lord Ishab, ‘Thus says your servant Yāqob, ‘I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed until now,
and I have oxen, and asses, and flocks, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favour in your sight.’”
And the messengers returned to Yāqob, saying: “We came to your brother Ishab, and moreover he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”
Then Yāqob was greatly afraid and was distressed. And he divided the people that were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into two companies,
and he said: “If Ishab comes to the one company, and smites it, then the company which is left will escape.”
And Yāqob said: “O God of my father Abˈram, and God of my father Yeˈṣaq, O Shema, who said to me ‘Return to your country, and to your kindred, and I will do you good,’

I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant, for with my staff I passed over this Yardan, and now I have become two companies.
Deliver me, I pray you, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Ishab, for I fear him, lest he come and strike me down, the mother with the children.
And you have said ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.’”
And he lodged there that night. And he took from what was at hand a present for Ishab his brother:
Two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
thirty milking camels and their calves, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses, and ten heasses.
And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants: “Pass over before me, and put a space between drove and drove.”
And he commanded the foremost, saying: “When Ishab my brother meets you, and asks you, saying: ‘Whose are you?’ and ‘Where are you going?’ and ‘Whose are these before you?’
you shall say, ‘They are your servant Yāqob’s. It is a present sent to my lord Ishab, and behold, he is also behind us.’”
And he commanded also the second, and also the third, and also all that followed the droves, saying: “On this manner you shall speak to Ishab, when you find him,

and you shall say, ‘Moreover, behold, your servant Yāqob is coming behind us. For he said, ‘I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me.’”
So the present passed over before him, and he himself lodged that night in the camp.
And he rose that night, and took his two wives, and his two hand-maids, and his eleven children, and passed over the ford of the Yibbaq.
And he took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over all that he had.
And Yāqob was left alone. And there a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.
And when he saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh. And the hollow of Yāqob’s thigh was strained, as he wrestled with him.
And he said: “Let me go, for the day breaks.” And he said: “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
And he said to him: “What is your name?” And he said: “Yāqob.”
And he said: “Your name shall no longer be called Yāqob, but Yishraʾel, for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
And Yāqob asked him, and said: “Tell me, I pray you, your name.” And he said: “Why is it that you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.
And Yāqob called the name of the place Fanuwwel: “for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
And the sun rose upon him as he passed over Fanuwwel, and he was limping upon his thigh.
Therefore the children of Yishraʾel do not eat the sinew of the hip which is upon the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Yāqob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.
And Yāqob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, Ishab was coming, and with him four hundred men. So he divided the children among Liyya, and Raʾel, and the two handmaids.
And he put the handmaids and their children in front, and Liyya and her children behind, and Raʾel and Yusef last.
And he himself passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
And Ishab ran to meet him and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him, and they wept.
And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children, and said: “Who are these with you?” And he said: “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”
Then the handmaids came near, they and their children, and bowed down.
And Liyya also and her children came near and bowed down. And afterward Yusef and Raʾel came near, and they bowed down.
And he said: “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” And he said: “To find favour in the sight of my lord.”
And Ishab said: “I have enough, my brother, and let what you have be yours.”

And Yāqob said: “No, I pray you, if now I have found favour in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, since as I have seen your face, as though I have seen the face of God, and you were pleased with me.
Take, I pray you, my gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” And he urged him, and he took it.
And he said: “Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before you.”
And he said to him: “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if I overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

Let my lord, I pray you, pass over before his servant, and I will lead on slowly, according to the pace of the walking [cattle] that is before me, and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Shaʾer.”
And Ishab said: “Let me now leave with you some of the folk that are with me.” And he said: “What need is there? let me find favour in the sight of my lord.”
So Ishab returned that day on his way to Shaʾer.
And Yāqob journeyed to Sakkot, and built himself a house, and made booths for his cattle. Therefore the name of the place is called Sakkot.
And Yāqob came in peace to the city of Ashkem, which is in the land of Kaˈnan, when he came from Faddan-aram, and encamped before the city.
And he bought the parcel of ground, where he had pitched his tent, from the children of Emor, Ashkem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.
And he erected there an altar, and called it Eleluwwi-Yishraʾel.
And Dina the daughter of Liyya, whom she bore to Yāqob, went out to meet with the daughters of the land.
And Ashkem the son of Emor the Ibbite, the prince of the land, saw her, and he took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.
And his soul cleaved to Dina the daughter of Yāqob, and he loved the maiden, and spoke kindly to the maiden.
And Ashkem spoke to his father saying: “Get me this maiden for a wife.”
Now Yāqob heard that he had defiled Dina his daughter. And his sons were with his cattle in the field, so Yāqob held his peace until they came.
And Emor the father of Ashkem went out to Yāqob to speak with him.

And the sons of Yāqob came in from the field when they heard of it, and the men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done an outrageous thing in Yishraʾel by lying with Yāqob’s daughter, for such a thing ought not to be done.
And Emor spoke with them, saying: “The soul of my son Ashkem longs for your daughter. I pray you, give her to him for a wife.
And make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
So you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell in it, [and] trade in it, and gain possessions in it.”
And Ashkem said to her father and to her brothers: “Let me find favour in your eyes, and what you shall say to me I will give.
Ask me so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as you say to me, but give me the maiden for a wife.”
And the sons of Yāqob answered Ashkem and Emor his father, and spoke with guile, because they had defiled Dina their sister,
and said to them: “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us.
Only by this will we consent to you, if you will be as we are, and circumcise every male among you,
then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves, and we will dwell with you, and we will be like one people.
But if you will not listen to us, and circumcise, then we will take our daughter, and we will be gone.”
And their words pleased Emor and Ashkem his son.
And the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Yāqob’s daughter. And he was honoured above all the household of his father.
And Emor and Ashkem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke with the men of their city, saying:

“These men are at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for, behold, the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters for ourselves for wives, and let us give them our daughters.
Only on this condition will the men consent to dwell with us, to become one people, by circumcising every male among us, as they are circumcised.
Behold, their cattle and their substance and all their beasts shall be ours! Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
And to Emor and to Ashkem his son all that went out of the gate of his city listened, and they circumcised every male, all that went out of the gate of his city.
And on the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons of Yāqob, Sheˈmun and Libi, Dina’s brothers, took each man his sword, and came upon the city safely, and killed all the males.
And they killed Emor and Ashkem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dina out of Ashkem’s house, and left.
And the sons of Yāqob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
And they took their flocks, and their herds, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field,
and all their wealth, and their little ones and their wives, they took captive and plundered all that was in the house.

And Yāqob said to Sheˈmun and Libi: “You have troubled me, making me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Kaˈnanites and the Ferizzites. And I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and attack me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.”
And they said: “As a whore they treated our sister!”
And God said to Yāqob: “Arise, go up to Bit-el, and dwell there, and make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from Ishab your brother.”
Then Yāqob said to his household and to all that were with him: “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.
And let us rise, and go up to Bit-el, and I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.”
And they gave Yāqob all the foreign gods which were in their hand, and the rings which were in their ears, and Yāqob hid them under the oak which was by Ashkem,
and they journeyed. And a terror of God was upon the cities that were around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Yāqob.
So Yāqob came to Luza, which is in the land of Kaˈnan—that is, Bit-el—he and all the people that were with him.
And he built there an altar, and called the place El-bit-el, because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from his brother.
And Dibbura Rubqa’s nurse died, and she was buried below Bit-el under the oak. And its name was called Alon-beket.
And God appeared to Yāqob again, when he came from Faddan-aram, and God blessed him.
And God said to him: “Your name is Yāqob. Your name shall not be called Yāqob any more, but Yishraʾel shall be your name.” And he called his name Yishraʾel.
And God said to him: “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations shall come from you, and kings shall come out of your loins.
And the land which I gave to Abˈram and Yeˈṣaq, to you I will give it, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”
And God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.
And Yāqob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. And he poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.
And Yāqob called the name of the place where God spoke with him, Bit-el.
And they journeyed from Bit-el. And when there was still some distance to come to Ifrata, Raʾel travailed, and she had hard labour.
And when she was in hard labour the midwife said to her: “Do not fear, for now you shall have another son.”
And as her soul was departing—for she was dying—she called his name Ban-uni, but his father called him Binyamem.
And Raʾel died, and was buried on the way to Ifrata—that is, Bit-lēm.
And Yāqob set up a pillar upon her grave. That is the Pillar of Raʾel’s grave to this day.
And Yishraʾel journeyed, and pitched his tent beyond Magdal-ʿadar.
And while Yishraʾel dwelt in that land, Reʾuben went and lay with Baˈla his father’s concubine. And Yishraʾel heard of it. Now the sons of Yāqob were twelve.
The sons of Liyya: Reʾuben, Yāqob’s first-born, and Sheˈmun, and Libi, and Yeʾuda, and Yashishakar, and Zebulan.
And the sons of Raʾel: Yusef and Binyamem.
And the sons of Baˈla, Raʾel’s handmaid: Dan and Niftali.
And the sons of Zilfa, Liyya’s handmaid: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Yāqob, that were born to him in Faddan-aram.
And Yāqob came to Yeˈṣaq his father to Mamri, to Qaryataʾarba—that is, Ibron—where Abˈram and Yeˈṣaq sojourned.
And the days of Yeˈṣaq were one hundred and eighty years.
And Yeˈṣaq expired, and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. And Ishab and Yāqob his sons buried him.
And these are the generations of Ishab—that is, Edom.
Ishab took his wives of the daughters of Kaˈnan: ʿAda the daughter of Ayyalon the Atite, and Elibama the daughter of ʿAne, the son of Ṣaˈbun the Ibbite,
and Maʾelat Yishmaʾel’s daughter, sister of Nabaʾot.
And ʿAda bore to Ishab Elifaz; and Maʾelat bore Rāwwel;
and Elibama bore Yewwash, and Yēllam, and Qara. These are the sons of Ishab, that were born to him in the land of Kaˈnan.

And Ishab took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the members of his household, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his property, which he had gathered in the land of Kaˈnan; and went from the land of Ka’nan away from his brother Yāqob.
For their substance was too great for them to dwell together; and the land of their sojournings could not bear them because of their cattle.
And Ishab dwelt in Mount Shaʾer; Ishab—that is, Edom.
And these are the generations of Ishab the father of the Edomites in Mount Shaʾer.
And these are the names of Ishab’s sons: Elifaz the son of ʿAda the wife of Ishab, Rāwwel the son of Maʾelat the wife of Ishab.
And the sons of Elifaz were Timan, and Amar, Ṣafu, and Gēttam, and Qenaz.
And Tamne was concubine to Elifaz Ishab’s son; and she bore to Elifaz ʿAmaleq. These are the sons of ʿAda, Ishab’s wife.
And these are the sons of Rāwwel: Nāt, and Zara, Shama, and Mizze. These were the sons of Maʾelat, Ishab’s wife.
And these were the sons of Elibama the daughter of ʿAne, the son of Ṣaˈbun, Ishab’s wife: And she bore to Ishab Yewwash, and Yēllam, and Qara.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Ishab. The sons of Elifaz the first-born of Ishab: chief of Timan, chief of Amar, chief of Ṣafu, chief of Qenaz,
chief of Gēttam, chief of ʿAmaleq; these are the chiefs that came of Elifaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of ʿAda.

And these are the sons of Rāwwel, Ishab’s son: chief of Nāt, chief of Zara, chief of Shama, chief of Mizze; these are the chiefs that came of Rāwwel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Maʾelat, Ishab’s wife.
And these are the sons of Elibama, Ishab’s wife: chief of Yewwash, chief of Yēllam, chief of Qara. These are the chiefs that came of Elibama the daughter of ʿAne, Ishab’s wife.
These are the sons of Ishab, and these are their chiefs: Ishab is Edom.
And these are the sons of Shaʾer the Arrite, the inhabitants of the land: Luṭan, and Shubal, and Ṣaˈbun, and ʿAne,
and Dishon, and Aṣar, and Dishan. These are the chiefs that came of the Arrites, the children of Shaʾer in the land of Edom.
And the children of Luṭan were Arri and Imam. And Luṭan’s sister was Tamne.
And these are the children of Shubal: Ilwan, and Maˈnat, and Ibal, Shabbu, and Unam.
And these are the children of Ṣaˈbun: Ayye, and ʿAne; this is ʿAne who found the Imem in the wilderness, as he fed the asses of Ṣaˈbun his father.
And these are the children of ʿAne: Dishon and Elibama the daughter of ʿAne.
And these are the children of Dishon: Imdan, and Ishban, Yitran, and Kirran.
And these are the children of Aṣar: Abˈlan, and Zuwwan, and Aqan.
And these are the children of Dishan: Ūṣ and Iddan.
These are the chiefs that came of the Arrites: chief of Luṭan, chief of Shubal, chief of Ṣaˈbun, chief of ʿAne,
chief of Dishon, chief of Aṣar, chief of Dishan. These are the chiefs that came of the Arrites, according to their chiefs in the land of Shaʾer.
And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yishraʾel.
And Bala the son of Būr reigned in Edom; and the name of his city was Dinabe.
And Bala died, and Yubab the son of Zara of Baṣra reigned in his stead.
And Yubab died, and Asham of the land of the Timanites reigned in his stead.
And Asham died, and Adad the son of Badad, who defeated the Madyanite in the field of Muwwab, reigned in his stead. And the name of his city was ʿAwwet.
And Adad died, and Shamla of Mashreqa reigned in his stead.
And Shamla died, and Shaʾol of Rabot-anˈnar reigned in his stead.
And Shaʾol died, and Bāl-ʿanan the son of ʿAkabor reigned in his stead.
And Bāl-ʿanan died, and Adad reigned in his stead. And the name of his city was Fū, and his wife’s name was Miṭabel, the daughter of Maṭrad, the daughter of Mi-zāb.
And these are the names of the chiefs that came of Ishab, according to their families, after their places, by their names: chief of Tamne, chief of Alwe, chief of Yatat,
chief of Elibama, chief of Ale, chief of Finan,
chief of Qenaz, chief of Timan, chief of Mabaṣer,
chief of Magˈdil, chief of Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their families in the land of their possession. This is Ishab, the father of the Edomites.
And Yāqob dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Kaˈnan.

These are the generations of Yāqob. Yusef, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. And he was a lad with the sons of Baˈla, and with the sons of Zilfa, his father’s wives. And Yusef brought a bad report of them to their father.
And Yishraʾel loved Yusef more than any other of his sons, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a coat of many colours.
But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his sons, they hated him, and could not speak peacefully to him.
And Yusef dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.
And he said to them: “Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed.
For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf rose, and also stood upright. And, behold, your sheaves gathered around about, and bowed down to my sheaf.”
And his brothers said to him: “Shall you indeed reign over us? Or shall you indeed have dominion over us?” And they hated him even more for his dreams, and for his words.
And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said: “Behold, I have dreamed another dream. And, behold, the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

And he told it to his father and to his brothers. And his father rebuked him, and said to him: “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I, and your mother, and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the earth before you?”
And his brothers envied him, but his father kept the saying in mind.
And his brothers went to feed their father’s flock in Ashkem.
And Yishraʾel said to Yusef: “Behold, your brothers are feeding the flock in Ashkem. Come, and I will send you to them.” And he said to him: “Here I am.”
And he said to him: “Go now, and see whether it is well with your brothers, and well with the flock, and bring me word back.” So he sent him out of the vale of Ibron, and he came to Ashkem.
And the man found him, and, behold, he was wandering in the field. And the man asked him, saying: “What are you seeking?”
And he said: “I am seeking my brothers. Tell me, I pray you, where they are feeding the flock.”
And the man said: “They have gone away, for I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Duten.’” And Yusef went after his brothers, and found them in Duten.
And they saw him far in the distance, and before he came near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.
And they said one to another: “Behold, this dreamer comes.
Come now, let us kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say about him, ‘An evil beast has devoured him,’ and we shall see what will become of his dreams.”
And Reʾuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said: “Let us not take his life.”
And Reʾuben said to them: “Shed no blood. Cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand upon him,” so that he might deliver him out of their hand, and restore him to his father.
And when Yusef came to his brothers, they stripped Yusef of his coat, the coat of many colours that was on him.
And they took [the coat], and cast him into the pit. And the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a caravan of Yishmaʾelites was coming from Gaˈlad, with their camels bearing gum and balm and myrrh, that were going to carry [their wares] down to Miṣrem.
And Yeʾuda said to his brothers: “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Yishmaʾelites, and let not our hand be upon him, for he is our brother, and our flesh.” And his brothers listened [to him].
And Madyanite traders passed by, and they drew and lifted Yusef out of the pit, and sold Yusef to the Yishmaʾelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Yusef to Miṣrem.
And Reʾuben returned to the pit, and behold, Yusef was not in the pit. And he tore his clothes.
And he returned to his brothers, and said: “The child is not there, and I, where shall I go?”
And they took Yusef’s coat, and killed a goat, and dipped the coat in the blood.
And they sent the coat of many colours, and they brought it to their father, and said: “This we have found. Recognise, we pray, whether it is your son’s coat or not?”
And he recognised it. And he said: “It is my son’s coat. An evil beast has devoured him. Yusef is surely torn to pieces.”
And Yāqob tore his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son for many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. And he said: “For I will go down to Sheol to my son mourning.” And his father wept for him.
And the Madyanites sold Yusef in Miṣrem to Fuṭifar, an officer of Faru, the captain of the guard.
And at that time Yeʾuda went down from his brothers, and turned to a certain ʿAdillamite, whose name was ʿAyyare.
And Yeʾuda saw there a daughter of a certain Kaˈnanite whose name was Shu. And he took her, and went in to her.
And she conceived, and bore a son. And she called his name Ar.
And she conceived again, and bore a son. And she called his name Unan.
And she yet again bore a son. And called his name Shila. And it was in Kaziba that she bore him.
And Yeʾuda took a wife for Ar his first-born, and her name was Tamar.
And Ar, Yeʾuda’s first-born, was wicked in the sight of Shema. And Shema killed him.
And Yeʾuda said to Unan: “Go in to your brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”
And Unan knew that the offspring would not be his, and when he went into his brother’s wife he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give offspring to his brother.
And what he did was evil in the sight of Shema, and he killed him also.

Then Yeʾuda said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: “Remain a widow in your father’s house, until Shila my son grows up,” for he said: “Lest he also die, like his brothers.” And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.
And over the course of time Shu’s daughter, the wife of Yeʾuda, died. And Yeʾuda was comforted, and went up to his sheep-shearers to Timna, he and his friend ʿAyyare the ʿAdillamite.
And Tamar his daughter-in-law was told, saying: “Behold, your father-in-law goes up to Timna to shear his sheep.”

And she took off her widow’s garments, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Inem, which is by the way to Timna, for she saw that Shila was grown up, and she was not given to him for a wife.
When Yeʾuda saw her, he thought she was a whore, for she had covered her face.

And he turned to her by the way, and said: “Come, I pray you, and let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said: “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
And he said: “I will send you a kid of the goats from the flock.” And she said: “Will you give me a pledge, until you send it?”
And he said: “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said: “Your signet and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” And he gave [them] to her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.
And she rose, and went away, and took off her veil from her, and put on her widow’s garments.
And Yeʾuda sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the ʿAdillamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand, but he could not find her.
Then he asked the men of the place, saying: “Where is that prostitute, that was at Inem by the wayside?” And they said: “There has been no prostitute here.”
And he returned to Yeʾuda, and said: “I have not found her. And also the men of the place said, ‘There has been no prostitute here.’”
And Yeʾuda said: “Let her take it, lest we be put to shame. Behold, I sent this kid, and you have not found her.”

And about three months later Yeʾuda was told, saying: “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the whore, and moreover, behold, she is with child by whoredom.” And Yeʾuda said: “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”

When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying: “By the man, whose these are, I am with child.” And she said: “Recognise, I pray you, whose these are, the signet, and the cord, and the staff.”
And Yeʾuda recognised them, and said: “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to Shila my son.” And he did not know her again.
And when the time of her labour came, behold, twins were in her womb.
And when she was in labour, one of them put out a hand. And the midwife took it and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying: “This one came out first.”
And as he drew back his hand, behold, his brother came out. And she said: “What a breach you breached over us.” Therefore she called his name Faraṣ.
And afterward came out his brother, with the scarlet thread upon his hand. And she called his name Zara.
And Yusef was brought down to Miṣrem. And Fuṭifar, an officer of Faru, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the Yishmaʾelites, that had brought him down there.
And Shema was with Yusef, and he was a prosperous man, and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master saw that Shema was with him, and that Shema caused all that he did to prosper in his hand.
And Yusef found favour in his master’s sight, and he attended him, and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put in his hand.

And from the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, Shema blessed the Egyptian’s house for Yusef’s sake. And the blessing of Shema was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Yusef’s hand, and he did not know anything that was with him, except the bread which he ate. And Yusef was of beautiful form and fair to look upon.
And after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Yusef, and she said: “Lie with me,”
but he refused. And he said to his master’s wife: “Behold, my master knows nothing that is with me in his house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.
He is not greater in this house than I, neither has he kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”
And as she spoke to Yusef day by day, he did not listen to her, to lie by her, to be with her.
But one such day, when Yusef went into the house to do his work in the house, and none of the men of the house were there in it,
she caught him by his garments, saying: “Lie with me.” And he left his garments in her hand, and fled, and got out.
And when she saw that he had left his garments in her hand, and fled and got out,
she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying: “See, he has brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.
And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments in my hand, and fled, and got out.”
And she laid up his garments by her, until his master came home.
And she spoke to him according to these words, saying: “The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me.
And as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments by me, and fled out.”
And when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying: “After this manner your servant did to me,” his anger was kindled.
And Yusef’s master took him, and put him in the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined. And he was there in the prison.
But Shema was with Yusef, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed to Yusef’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison. And whatever they did there, he was the one who did it.
The keeper of the prison did not look to anything that was under his hand, because Shema was with him. And all that he did, Shema made prosper.
And after these things the butler of the king of Miṣrem and his baker offended their lord the king of Miṣrem.
And Faru was angry with his two officers, with the chief of the butlers, and with the chief of the bakers.
And he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison, the place where Yusef was confined.
And the captain of the guard charged Yusef with them, and he ministered to them. And they remained for some time in custody.

And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Miṣrem, who were confined in the prison.
And Yusef came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and, behold, they were troubled.
And he asked Faru’s officers that were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying: “Why do you look so sad today?”
And they said to him: “We have dreamt a dream, and there is none that can interpret it.” And Yusef said to them: “Behold, interpretations belong to God. Tell them to me, I pray you.”
And the chief butler told his dream to Yusef, and said to him: “In my dream, behold, a vine was before me.
And on the vine there were three branches. And it was as a bud, its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
And Faru’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and pressed them into Faru’s cup, and gave the cup into Faru’s hand.”
And Yusef said to him: “This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days.
Within three days Faru shall lift up your head and restore you to your office. And you shall give Faru’s cup into his hand, in the manner you had formerly done when you were his butler.
Only remember me, when it is well with you, and show me kindness, I pray you, and mention me to Faru, and bring me out of this house.
For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted favourably, he said to Yusef: “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
And in the uppermost basket there was all manner of baked food for Faru, but the birds did eat them upon the basket upon my head.”
And Yusef answered and said: “This is its interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
Within three days Faru shall lift up your head from you, and shall hang you on the tree. And the birds shall eat your flesh from you.”
And on the third day, which was Faru’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and lifted up the head of the chief butler and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the chief butler to his butlership again, and he gave the cup into Faru’s hand.
And he hanged the chief baker, as Yusef had interpreted to them.
Yet the chief butler did not remember Yusef, but forgot him.
And at the end of two full years Faru dreamed. And, behold, he stood by the river,
and, behold, there came up out of the river seven cows, fair and fat-fleshed. and they fed in the reed-grass.
And, behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the river, ugly and lean-fleshed, and stood by the other cows on the bank of the river.
And the ugly and lean-fleshed cows ate up the seven fair and fat cows. And Faru awoke,
and he slept and dreamed a second time. And, behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, fat and good.
And, behold, seven ears, thin and blasted by the east wind, sprung up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed up the seven fat and full ears. And Faru awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

And in the morning his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Miṣrem and all its wise men. And Faru told them his dreams, but there was none that could interpret them to Faru.
Then the chief butler spoke to Faru, saying: “I remember my offenses today.
Faru was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker.
And we dreamed a dream on the same night, I and he, we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

And there was with us there a young Hebrew, a servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him [our dreams], and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he interpreted.
And as he interpreted to us, so it was: me he restored to my office, and him he hanged.”
Then Faru sent and called Yusef, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. And he shaved himself, and changed his clothes, and came in to Faru.
And Faru said to Yusef: “I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it. And I have heard it said of you, that lo, you hear a dream and you interpret it.”
And Yusef answered Faru, saying: “Without God Faru’s peace will not be answered.”
And Faru spoke with Yusef: “In my dream, and behold, I stood upon the bank of the river.
And behold, there came up out of the river seven cows, fat-fleshed and fair, and they fed in the reed-grass.
And, behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly and lean-fleshed, such as I had never seen as foul in all the land of Miṣrem.
And the lean and ugly cows ate the seven first and fat cows.
And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly as at the beginning. So I awoke,
and I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up upon one stalk, full and good.
And, behold, seven ears withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears. And I told it to the magicians, but there was none that could explain it to me.”
And Yusef said to Faru: “The dream of Faru is one. What God is about to do I shall explain to Faru:
The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream is one.
And the seven lean and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
That is the thing which I spoke to Faru. What God is about to do I shall show to Faru.
Behold, there will come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Miṣrem,
and there shall arise after them seven years of famine, and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Miṣrem, and the famine shall consume the land.
And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine and afterward, for it shall be very grievous.
And the dream was repeated for Faru, twice, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it about.
Now therefore let Faru select a discerning and wise man, and set him over the land of Miṣrem.
And let Faru do [this], and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Miṣrem in the seven plenteous years.
And let him gather all the food of the seven good years that are coming, and lay up grain under the hand of Faru for food in the cities, and let them keep [it].
And the food shall be a reserve for the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Miṣrem, so that the land shall not perish through the famine.”
And the thing was good in the eyes of Faru, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Faru said to his servants: “Can we find such as this, a man in whom the spirit of God is?”
And Faru said to Yusef: “Since God has shown you all of this, there is none so discerning and wise as you.
You shall be over my house, and according to your word shall all my people be ruled; only in the throne will I be greater than you.”
And Faru said to Yusef: “See, I have set you over all the land of Miṣrem.”
And Faru took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it upon Yusef’s hand, and arrayed him in garments of fine linen, and put a gold chain around his neck.
And he made him ride in the second chariot which he had; and appointed a herald before him. And he set him over all the land of Miṣrem.
And Faru said to Yusef: “I am Faru, and without you no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Miṣrem.”
And Faru called Yusef’s name “he revealed my secrets,” and he gave him for a wife Esenet, the daughter of Fuṭifara priest of An. And Yusef went out over the land of Miṣrem.
And Yusef was thirty years old when he stood before Faru king of Miṣrem. And Yusef went out from the presence of Faru, and went throughout all the land of Miṣrem.
And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.

And he gathered up all the food [during] the seven years in which there was plenty in the land of Miṣrem, and laid up the food in the cities. The food of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in it.
And Yusef laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very plentifully, until he left off numbering; for it was without number.
And to Yusef were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Esenet, the daughter of Fuṭifara priest of An, bore to him.
And Yusef called the name of the first-born Manashi, “For,” [he said:] “God has made me forget my toil, and all my father’s house.”
And the name of the second he called Ifrem, “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
And the seven years of plenty that were in the land of Miṣrem came to an end.
And the seven years of the famine began to come, according to that which Yusef had said. And there was the famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Miṣrem there was bread.
And when all the land of Miṣrem was famished, the people cried to Faru for bread. And Faru said to all the Egyptians: “Go to Yusef, and what he says to you, you shall do.”
And the famine was over the face of all the earth, and Yusef opened all the store-houses, and sold grain to the Egyptians. And the famine was severe in the land of Miṣrem.
And all [the inhabitants of] the lands came to Miṣrem to Yusef to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
And Yāqob saw that there was grain in Miṣrem, and Yāqob said to his sons: “Why are you afraid?”
And he said: “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Miṣrem. Go down to that place, and buy for us from there, that we may live and not die.”
And Yusef’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Miṣrem.
But Binyamem, Yusef’s brother, Yāqob did not send with his brothers, for he said: “Lest harm befall him.”
And the sons of Yishraʾel came to buy among those that came, for the famine was in the land of Kaˈnan.
And Yusef was the governor over the land, and he was the one who sold to all the people of the land. And Yusef’s brothers came, and bowed down to him with their faces to the earth.

And Yusef saw his brothers, and he knew them, but made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly with them. And he said to them: “Where do you come from?” And they said: “From the land of Kaˈnan to buy food.”
And Yusef knew his brothers, but they did not know him.
And Yusef remembered the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and said to them: “You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
And they said to him: “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
We are all one man’s sons. We are honest. Your servants are not spies.”
And he said to them: “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
And they said: “We your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Kaˈnan. And behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more.”
And Yusef said to them: “It is as I spoke to you, saying, You are spies.
By this you shall be tested. By the life of Faru, you shall not go from this place, unless your youngest brother comes here.

Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and you shall be confined, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else, by the life of Faru surely you are spies.” And they said: “The lad cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.”
And he put them all together into custody for three days.
And Yusef said to them on the third day: “Do this and live, [for] I fear God.
If you are honest men, let the one of your brothers be confined in your prison-house, and you go, and carry grain for the famine of your houses,
and bring your youngest brother to me, so your words will be verified, and you shall not die.” And they did so.
And they said one to another: “In truth we are guilty concerning our brother since we saw the distress of his soul when he begged us, and we would not hear. Therefore all this distress came upon us.”
And Reʾuben answered them, saying: “Behold, I spoke to you, saying: ‘Do not sin against the child!’ But you would not listen. Therefore now comes a reckoning for his blood here.”
