And they came to the valley of Ishkol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they carried [it] on a pole between two [of them]; and of the pomegranates and of the figs [they also took].
That place was called the Valley of Ishkol, because of the cluster which the children of Yishraʾel cut down from there.
And they returned from spying out the land at the end of forty days.

And they went and came to Mushi and to Ārron and to all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, to the wilderness of Farran, to Kadesh. And they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
And they told him, and said: “We came to the land to which you sent us. It flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
However, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified, and very great. And moreover, we saw the children of Enaq there.

ʿAmaleq dwells in the land of the south, and the Atite, and the Ibbite, and the Yebusite, and the Emarite dwell in the hill country. And the Kaˈnanite dwells by the sea, and along the side of the Yardan.”
And Kilab quieted the people before Mushi, and said to him: “Let us go up at once and occupy it, for we are well able to overcome it.”
But the men that went up with him said: “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.”

And they brought the children of Yishraʾel a bad report of the land which they had spied out, saying: “The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people that we saw in it are men of great stature.

And there we saw the Nefilem, the sons of Enaq, who come of the Nefilem, and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.” [a] And the children of Yishraʾel murmured in their tents, and said: “Because Shema hates us, he has brought us out of the land of Miṣrem, to deliver us into the hand of the Emarites, to destroy us. [b] Where are we going up while our brothers have made our heart to melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and more numerous than we are, the cities are great and fortified up to heaven, and moreover we have seen the sons of the Enaqem there.’” [c] And Mushi said to the children of Yishraʾel: “Do not be in dread or afraid of them. [d] Shema your God who goes before you, he himself will fight for you, just as he did for you in Miṣrem before your eyes, [e] and in the wilderness, where you have seen how Shema your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place. [f] Yet, behold, in spite of this thing, you do not believe in Shema your God, [g] who goes before you in the way to seek you out a place to encamp, in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.”
And all the congregation raised a loud cry; and the people wept that night.

And all the children of Yishraʾel murmured against Mushi and against Ārron, and the whole congregation said to them: “Would that we had died in the land of Miṣrem or would that we had died in this wilderness!
Why is Shema bringing us into this land, so that we fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Behold, it would be better for us to return to Miṣrem!”
And they said one to another: “Let us choose a leader and go back to Miṣrem.”
Then Mushi and Ārron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel.
And Yeʾusha the son of Non and Kilab the son of Yefanni, who were among those who scouted the land, tore their clothes,
and they spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, saying: “The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceeding good land.
If Shema delights in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us, a land which flows with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against Shema. And do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us. The [defence of their] idols is removed from over them, and Shema is with us. Do not fear them.”
But all the congregation said to stone them with stones. And the glory of Shema appeared in the tent of meeting to all the children of Yishraʾel.
And Shema said to Mushi: “How long will this people despise me? And how long will they not believe in me, in spite of the signs which I have wrought among them?
I will strike them with the pestilence and disinherit them, and I will make of you and of your father’s house a nation greater and mightier than they.”
And Mushi said to Shema: “Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for you brought up this people in your might from among them,

and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, O Shema, are in the midst of this people, for you, Shema, are seen face to face, and your cloud stands over them, and you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
Now if you kill this people as one man, then the nations which have heard your fame will speak, saying,
‘Because Shema was not able to bring this people into the land which he swore to them, he killed them in the wilderness.’
And now, I pray you, let my lord’s power be great as you have spoken, saying,

‘Shema is slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth, forgiving iniquity, and transgression, and sin, and the innocent—he will clear him, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the children’s children, to the third and the fourth generation.’
Pardon, I pray you, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your lovingkindness, just as you have forgiven this people, from Miṣrem until now.”
And Shema said: “I have pardoned according to your words,
but truly, as I live, and as the glory of Shema shall fill all the earth,
because all those men that have seen my glory and my signs which I wrought in Miṣrem and in the wilderness, yet have put me to the test these ten times and have not obey my voice,
they shall not see the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. And none of those who despised me shall see it.
But my servant Kilab, because he had a different spirit, and has followed me fully, him I will bring into the land into which he went, and his offspring shall possess it.
Now the ʿAmaleqite and the Kaˈnanite dwell in the valley. Turn tomorrow, and set out into the wilderness by the way to the sea of Sof.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi and to Ārron, saying:
“How long shall this evil congregation murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Yishraʾel, which they murmur against me.
Say to them, ‘As I live, says Shema, what you have spoken in my hearing, so I will do to you.
Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness, and all of your number, numbered from twenty years old and up, who have murmured against me,
not one shall come into the land where I swore that I would make you dwell, except for Kilab the son of Yefanni and Yeʾusha the son of Non.
But your little ones, who you said would become a plunder, them I will bring in, and they shall know the land which you have rejected.
But as for you, your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
And your children shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your faithlessness, until your dead bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, for every day a year, shall you bear your iniquities, forty years, and you shall know my displeasure.
I, Shema, have spoken. Surely this I will do to all this evil congregation, who are gathered together against me; in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.’”
And the men whom Mushi sent to spy out the land, who returned and caused all the congregation to murmur against him by bringing up a bad report against the land,
those men that did bring up a bad report of the land, died by the plague before Shema.
Of those men who went to spy out the land only Yeʾusha the son of Non and Kilab the son of Yefanni remained alive.
And Mushi told these words to all the children of Yishraʾel, and the people mourned greatly.

And they rose early in the morning and went up to the heights of the hill country, saying: “Here we are. And we will go up to the place which Shema has promised, for we have sinned.” [a] And Shema said to Mushi: “Say to them, ‘Do not go up or fight, for I am not in your midst, lest you be defeated before your enemies.’”
And Mushi said: “Why now are you transgressing the commandment of Shema, when that will not succeed?
Do not go up, for Shema is not in your midst, lest you be defeated before your enemies.
For there the ʿAmaleqite and the Kaˈnanite are before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following Shema, Shema will not be with you.”
But they presumed to go up to the heights of the hill country, although neither the ark of the covenant of Shema nor Mushi departed out of the camp.

Then the ʿAmaleqite and the Kaˈnanite who lived in that hill country came down against them and chased them as bees do, and struck them and beat them down, as far as Irma, and they returned to the camp.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land of your habitations, which I give to you,

and you make an offering by fire to Shema, a burned offering, or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or a freewill offering, or in your set feasts, to make a sweet savour to Shema, of the herd or of the flock,
then he who offers his offering shall offer to Shema a meal offering of a tenth part [of an ephah] of fine flour mingled with the fourth part of a hin of oil,
and wine for the drink offering, the fourth part of a hin, you shall prepare with the burned offering, or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.
Or for a ram, you shall prepare for a meal offering two tenth parts [of an ephah] of fine flour mingled with the third part of a hin of oil,
and for the drink offering you shall offer the third part of a hin of wine, a sweet savour to Shema.
And when you prepare a bull for a burned offering, or for a sacrifice to accomplish a vow or for peace offerings to Shema,
then he shall offer with the bull a meal offering of three tenth parts [of an ephah] of fine flour mingled with half a hin of oil,
and you shall offer for the drink offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, a sweet savour to Shema.
Thus shall it be done for each bull, or for each ram, or for each of the male lambs, or of the kids.
According to their number that you shall prepare, so shall you do to everyone according to their number.
Every native shall do these things after this manner, in offering an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema.
And if a stranger sojourns with you, or anyone who may be among you throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema, as you do, so he shall do.
O the assembly! There shall be one statute for you and for the stranger that sojourns [with you], a statute forever throughout your generations; as you are, so shall the sojourner be before Shema.
One law and one ordinance shall be for you and for the stranger that sojourns with you.’”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land to which I bring you,
and when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall offer up a heave offering to Shema.
Of the first of your dough you shall offer up a cake for a heave offering; as the heave offering of the threshing-floor, so shall you heave it.
Of the first of your dough you shall give to Shema a heave offering throughout your generations.
And when you shall err and not observe all these commandments which Shema has spoken to Mushi,
all that Shema has commanded you by Mushi, from the day that Shema gave commandment, and onward throughout your generations,

then it shall be, if it was done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, all the congregation shall offer one young bull for a burned offering, a sweet savour to Shema, with its meal offering, and its drink offerings, according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, and they shall be forgiven, for it was an error, and they have brought their offering, an offering made by fire to Shema, and their sin offering before Shema, for their error.
And all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel shall be forgiven, and the stranger that sojourns among them, because the whole people was involved in the error.
And if one person sins unwittingly, then he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for the soul that errs, when he sins unwittingly, before Shema, to make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
You shall have one law for him that does anything unwittingly, for him that is native among the children of Yishraʾel, and for the stranger that sojourns among them.
But the soul that does anything with a high hand, whether he is native or a sojourner, blasphemes Shema, and that soul shall be cut off from among his peo- ple.
Because he has despised the word of Shema and has broken his commandments, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.’”
And while the children of Yishraʾel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Mushi and Ārron and to all the congregation.
And they put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
And Shema said to Mushi: “The man shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”
And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him to death with stones as Shema commanded Mushi.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and tell them to make fringes on the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and put a cord of blue on the fringe of each border.

And they shall be fringes for you to look at them and remember all the commandments of Shema, and do them, and not to follow after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you used to play the whore,
that you may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God.
I am Shema your God who brought you out of the land of Miṣrem to be your God. I am Shema your God.”
Now Qara, the son of Yaˈṣar, the son of Qāt, the son of Libi, and Datan and Abiram, the sons of Ilyab, and Ūn, the son of Falat, the son of Reʾuben, took [men],
and they rose up before Mushi, with certain of the children of Yishraʾel, two hundred and fifty princes of the congregation, called to the assembly, men of reputation.

And they assembled themselves together against Mushi and against Ārron, and said to them: “You have gone too far, for all the congregation are holy, everyone of them, and Shema is among them. Why then do you lift yourselves above the assembly of Shema?”
And when Mushi heard it, he fell on his face.
And he spoke to Qara and to all his company, saying: “In the morning Shema will show who is his, and the holy he will bring near to him. The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him.
Do this: Take censers, Qara and all his company,
and put fire in them and put incense on them before Shema tomorrow, and the man whom Shema chooses, he [shall be] holy. You have gone too far, sons of Libi.”
And Mushi said to Qara: “Hear now, you sons of Libi:

Is it a small thing for you that the God of Yishraʾel has separated you from the congregation of Yishraʾel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle of Shema, to stand before the congregation to minister to them,
and that he has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Libi with you? And would you seek the priesthood also?
Therefore you and all your company have gathered together against Shema, and Ārron. What is he that you murmur against him?”
And Mushi sent to call Datan and Abiram, the sons of Ilyab, and they said: “We will not come up.
Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, that you must make yourself also a prince over us?
Moreover you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields or vineyards. Will the eyes of these men be put out? We will not come up.”
And Mushi was very angry, and said to Shema: “Do not respect their offering. I have not taken one of their precious things from them, and I have not harmed one of them.”
And Mushi said to Qara: “Be present, you and all your company before Shema, you and they and Ārron, tomorrow.
And let everyone of you take his censer and put incense on them, and everyone of you bring before Shema his censer, two hundred and fifty censers; you also, and Ārron, each his censer.”
And they took every man his censer, and put fire in them, and laid incense on them, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Mushi and Ārron.
And Qara assembled all the congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of Shema appeared to all the congregation.
And Shema spoke to Mushi and to Ārron, saying:
“Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.”
And they fell on their faces and said: “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from about the dwellings of Qara, Datan, and Abiram.’”
And Mushi rose and went to Datan and Abiram, and the elders of Yishraʾel followed him.
And he spoke to the congregation, saying: “Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their sins.”

So they got away from the dwellings of Qara, Datan, and Abiram, on every side, and Datan and Abiram came out, and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives, and their sons, and their little ones.
And Mushi said: “Hereby you shall know that Shema has sent me to do all these works, for [I have] not [done them] of my own mind.
If these men die the common death of all men, or if they are visited after the visitation of all men, then Shema has not sent me.

But if Shema creates something new, and the ground open its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you shall know that these men have despised Shema.”
And as he finished speaking all these words, the ground that was under them split apart.
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and all the men that belonged to Qara and all their goods.
So they, and all that belonged to them, went down alive into Sheol, and the earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
And all Yishraʾel that were round about them fled at their cry, for they said: “Lest the earth swallow us up.”
And fire came out from Shema and devoured the two hundred and fifty men who offered the incense.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Tell Elāzar the son of Ārron the priest to take up the censers out of the blaze, and scatter the fire far and wide, for they are holy.

As for the censers of these men who have sinned at the cost of their lives, make them into hammered plates for a covering of the altar, for they offered them before Shema; therefore they are holy, and they shall be a sign to the children of Yishraʾel.”
And Elāzar the son of Ārron the priest took the bronze censers, which those who were burned had offered, and they hammered them out as a covering for the altar,

to be a reminder to the children of Yishraʾel, so that no outsider, who is not of the descendants of Ārron, should come near to burn incense before Shema, lest he be like Qara and as his company, as Shema said to him through Mushi.
But on the next day all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel murmured against Mushi and against Ārron, saying: “You have killed the people of Shema.”
And when the congregation had assembled against Mushi and against Ārron, they looked toward the tent of meeting, and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of Shema appeared.
And Mushi and Ārron came to the front of the tent of meeting,
and Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Get away from the midst of this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.” And they fell on their faces.

And Mushi said to Ārron: “Take your censer, and put fire in it from off the altar, and lay incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from Shema; the plague has begun.”
And Ārron took [it] as Mushi said, and ran into the midst of the assembly, and behold, the plague had begun among the people. And he put on the incense, and made atonement for the people.
And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
Now they that died by the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in the matter of Qara.
And Ārron returned to Mushi to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague was stopped.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and take from them rods, one for each father’s house, from all their princes according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write every man’s name on his rod,
and write Ārron’s name on the rod of Libi, for there shall be one rod for the head of each fathers’ house.
And you shall lay them up in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
And the rod of the man whom I choose shall bud. Thus I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Yishraʾel, which they murmur against you.”
And Mushi spoke to the children of Yishraʾel, and all their princes gave him rods, for each prince one, according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Ārron was among their rods.
And Mushi laid up the rods before Shema in the tent of the testimony.
And on the next day, Mushi went into the tent of the testimony, and behold, the rod of Ārron for the house of Libi had budded and put forth buds, and produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.
And Mushi brought out all the rods from before Shema to all the children of Yishraʾel, and they looked, and took every man his rod.
And Shema said to Mushi: “Put back the rod of Ārron before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the children of rebellion that you may make an end of their murmurings against me, lest they die.”
And Mushi did as Shema commanded him; so he did.
And the children of Yishraʾel spoke to Mushi, saying: “Behold, we perish, we are undone, we are all undone.
Every relative that comes near to the tabernacle of Shema shall be killed. Are we all to perish?”
And Shema said to Ārron: “You and your sons and your father’s house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.

And your brothers also, the tribe of Libi, the tribe of your father, bring near with you, that they may be joined to you, and minister to you, but you and your sons with you shall be before the tent of the testimony.
And they shall keep your charge, and the charge of all the tent, but they shall not come near to the vessels of the sanctuary and to the altar, lest they, and you, die.
And they shall be joined to you, and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent, and an outsider shall not come near to you.
And you shall keep the charge of the sanctuary and the charge of the altar, that there may never again be wrath on the children of Yishraʾel.
And I, behold, I have taken your brothers the Libites from among the children of Yishraʾel. They are a gift to you, given to Shema, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for all that concerns the altar, and for that which is within the veil; and you shall serve. I give you the priesthood as a service of a gift, and the outsider that comes near shall be put to death.”

And Shema spoke to Ārron: “And I, behold, I have given you the charge of my heave offerings, all the consecrated things of the children of Yishraʾel. I have given them to you and to your sons as a portion forever.

This shall be yours of the most holy things, [reserved] from the fire: every offering of theirs, every meal offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every guilt offering of theirs, which they offer to me, shall be most holy for you and for your sons.
In the most holy [place] shall you eat of it; every male shall eat of it; it shall be holy to you.

And this is yours: the heave offering of their gift, all the wave offerings of the children of Yishraʾel. I have given them to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a portion forever; everyone that is clean in your house shall eat it.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the first-fruits of them which they give to Shema, to you I have given them.
The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to Shema, shall be yours; everyone that is clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted in Yishraʾel shall be yours.

Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh which they offer to Shema, both of man and of beast shall be yours; nevertheless the first-born of man you shall redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts you shall redeem.
And take as its redemption price, from a month old and up, according to your estimation, for five shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.

But the firstling of a cow, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and shall burn their fat for an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema.
And their flesh shall be yours, as the wave-breast and as the right thigh it shall be yours.

All the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Yishraʾel offer to Shema, I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before Shema to you and to your offspring with you.”
And Shema said to Ārron: “You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Yishraʾel.
And to the children of Libi, behold, I have given all the tithe in Yishraʾel for an inheritance, in return for their service which they serve, the service of the tent of meeting.
And the children of Yishraʾel shall no more come near the tent of meeting, lest they bear sin and die.

But the Libites shall do the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity. [It shall be] a statute forever throughout your generations, and among the children of Yishraʾel they shall have no inheritance.

For the tithe of the children of Yishraʾel which they offer as a heave offering to Shema, I have given it to the Libites for an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Yishraʾel they shall have no inheritance.’”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:

“Moreover, you shall speak to the Libites and say to them, ‘When you take of the children of Yishraʾel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritances, then you shall offer up a heave offering of it for Shema, a tithe of the tithe.
And your heave offerings shall be reckoned to you as though it were the grain of the threshing-floor, and as the fullness of the winepress.
Thus you also shall offer a heave offering to Shema of all your tithes which you receive of the children of Yishraʾel. And from it you shall give Shema’s heave offering to Ārron the priest.
Out of all your gifts you shall offer every heave offering of Shema; from each its best part is to be consecrated.
Therefore you shall say to them, ‘When you heave from it the best of it, then it shall be reckoned to the Libites as the increase of the threshing-floor, and as the increase of the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your reward in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
And you shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have heaved from it the best of it. And you shall not profane the holy things of the children of Yishraʾel, lest you die.’”
And Shema spoke to Mushi and to Ārron, saying:

“This is the statute of the law which Shema has commanded, saying, ‘Tell the children of Yishraʾel to bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish, and upon which a yoke has never come.
And you shall give her to Elāzar the priest, and she shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered before him.
And Elāzar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.
And the heifer shall be burned in his sight. Her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall be burned.
And the priest shall take cedarwood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the fire burning the heifer.
Then the priest shall wash his clothes and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp; and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
And he who burns her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the evening.

And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel for a water for impurity; it is a sin offering.

And he who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. And it shall be to the children of Yishraʾel and to the stranger that sojourns among them for a statute forever.
He that touches the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.
He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean, but if he does not purify himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he shall not be clean.

Whoever touches a dead person, the body of a man that has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of Shema, and that soul shall be cut off from Yishraʾel; because the water for impurity was not sprinkled on him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is still upon him.
And this is the law when a man dies in a tent: Everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent shall be unclean seven days.
And every open vessel, which has no covering and a cord upon it, is unclean.
And whoever in the open field touches one who was killed with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
And for the unclean they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering, and running water they shall add in a vessel.

And a clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water and sprinkle it on the tent, and on the vessels, and on the persons who were there, and on whoever touched the bone or the slain or the dead or the grave.

And the clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. And on the seventh day he shall purify him, and he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean in the evening.

But the man that shall be unclean and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of Shema; the water for impurity has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
And it shall be a statute forever to you, and he who sprinkles the water for impurity shall wash his clothes, and he who touches the water for impurity shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the soul that touches it shall be unclean until evening.’”
And the children of Yishraʾel, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Ṣen in the first month, and the people abode in Kadesh. And Maryam died there, and was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation, and they assembled themselves together against Mushi and against Ārron.
And the people quarreled with Mushi, and spoke, saying: “Would that we had died when our brothers died before Shema!
And why have you brought the assembly of Shema into this wilderness, that we should die there, we and our cattle?
And why have you made us come up out of Miṣrem to bring us to this evil place? It is no place for grain, or figs, vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”
And Mushi and Ārron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and fell on their faces, and the glory of Shema appeared to them.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:

“Take the rod and assemble the congregation, you and Ārron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, so that it gives its water. And you shall bring them water out of the rock. So you shall give the congregation and their cattle drink.”
And Mushi took the rod from before Shema, as he commanded him.
And Mushi and Ārron gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said to them: “Hear now, you rebels, shall we bring you water out of this rock?”
And Mushi lifted up his hand, and struck the rock with his rod twice, and water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their cattle drank.

And Shema said to Mushi and Ārron: “Because you did not believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Yishraʾel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”

These are the waters of Meriba, because the children of Yishraʾel quarreled with Shema, and he was sanctified in them. [a] And Mushi said: “O Lord Shema, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such works and mighty acts as yours? [b] Let me go over, I pray you, and see the good land that is beyond the Yardan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.” [c] And Shema said to Mushi: “Let it suffice you. Speak no more to me of this matter. [d] Get up to the top of Affasga and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and behold with your eyes, for you shall not go over this Yardan. [e] But charge Yeʾusha the son of Non and encourage him and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you shall see.” [f] And Shema spoke to Mushi saying: “You have circled this mountain long enough. Turn northward, [g] and command the people, saying ‘You are about to pass through the border of your brothers the children of Ishab, who dwell in Shaʾer, and they will be afraid of you. So take good heed to yourselves. [h] Do not contend with them, for I will not give you a possession of their land. No, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Shaʾer to Ishab for a possession. [i] You shall purchase food from them for money, that you may eat, and you shall also buy water from them for money, that you may drink.”
And Mushi sent messengers from Qadesh to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Yishraʾel, ‘You know all the travail that has befallen us.
How our fathers went down into Miṣrem, and we dwelt in Miṣrem a long time, and the Egyptians dealt harshly with us, and our fathers.
And when we cried to Shema, he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Miṣrem, and behold, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your border.

Let us pass, I pray you, through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, neither will we drink water of a cistern. We will go along the king’s highway. We will not turn aside to the right hand or to the left, until we have passed your territory.’”
And Edom said to him: “You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.”

And the children of Yishraʾel said to him: “We will go up by the highway, and if we drink of your water, I and my cattle, then I will pay the price of it. Let me only pass through on my feet, nothing more.”
And he said: “You shall not pass through.” And Edom came out against him with many men, and with a strong hand.
Thus Edom refused to give Yishraʾel passage through his territory, so Yishraʾel turned away from him.
And they journeyed from Kadesh, and the children of Yishraʾel, the whole congregation, came to Mount Ar.
And Shema spoke to Mushi and Ārron in Mount Ar, by the border of the land of Edom, saying:
“Ārron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Yishraʾel, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meriba.
Take Ārron and Elāzar his son and bring them up to Mount Ar,
and you will strip Ārron of his garments and put them on Elāzar his son, and Ārron shall be gathered [to his people], and shall die there.”
And Mushi did as Shema commanded and he brought him up to Mount Ar in the sight of all the congregation.
And Mushi stripped Ārron of his garments and put them on Elāzar his son, and Ārron died there on the top of the mountain, and Mushi and Elāzar came down from the mountain.
And when all the congregation saw that Ārron was dead, all the house of Yishraʾel wept for Ārron thirty days.
And the Kaˈnanite, the king of ʿArad, who dwelt in the south, heard that Yishraʾel came by the way of the scouts, and he fought against Yishraʾel, and took some of them captive.
And Yishraʾel vowed a vow to Shema, and said: “If you will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.”
And Shema listened to the voice of Yishraʾel and delivered up the Kaˈnanites into his hand, and they utterly destroyed them and their cities. So the name of the place was called Irma.
And they journeyed from Mount Ar by the way to the sea of Sof to go around the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.

And the people spoke against God and against Mushi: “Why have you brought us out of Miṣrem to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and there is no water, and our soul loathes this worthless bread.”
And Shema sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, so that many people of Yishraʾel died.
And the people came to Mushi, and said: “We have sinned, because we have spoken against Shema and against you. Pray to Shema that he take away the serpents from us.” And Mushi prayed for the people.
And Shema said to Mushi: “Make a fiery [serpent], and set it on the pole. And everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
And Mushi made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole. And if a serpent had bit any man, he would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And the children of Yishraʾel journeyed, and encamped in Abbot.

And they journeyed from Abbot, and encamped at Ayyi-aʾibrem, in the wilderness which is before Muwwab, toward the sunrise. [a] And Shema said to Mushi: “Do not harass Muwwab or contend with them, for I will not give you of his land for a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Loṭ for a possession.”

From there they journeyed, and encamped in the valley of Zarad.>— — [a] And Shema spoke to Mushi saying: [b] “You are this day to pass over Ar, the border of Muwwab. And when you come near [the border of] the children of ʿAmmon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you of the land of the children of ʿAmmon for a possession, because I have given it to the children of Loṭ for a possession.”

And they journeyed from the valley of Zarad, and encamped on the other side of the Arenan, which is by the wilderness that comes out of the border of the Emarites, for the Arenan is the border of Muwwab, between Muwwab and the Emarites.
Therefore it is said in the book of the Wars of Shema: “Waʾeb in Sufa, and the valleys of the Arenan,
which he caused them to inherit, and which extends toward the dwelling of a city, and leans to the border of Muwwab.”
And from there [they journeyed] to Bir, that is the well of which Shema said to Mushi: “Gather to me the people together, and I will give them water.”
Then Yishraʾel sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The well, which the princes dug, which the nobles of the people delved, with the scepter, and with their staves.” From the wilderness [they went] to Mattana,
and from Mattana to Nēlliʾel, and from Nēlliʾel to Bamot,

and from Bamot-aggiyya that is in the field of Muwwab, to the top of Affasga, which looks down upon the desert. [a] And Shema said to Mushi: “Rise up, take your journey and pass over the valley of the Arenan. Behold, I have given into your hand Siyyon the Emarite, king of Ishbon, and his land. Begin to possess it and contend with him in battle. [b] This day begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples who are under the whole heaven, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of you.”
And Yishraʾel sent messengers to Siyyon king of the Emarites with words of peace, saying:

“Let me pass through your land. I will go by the king’s highway. I will not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. I will not turn aside into field or into vineyard. [a] You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat, and give me water for money, that I may drink. Only let me pass through on my feet, [b] as the children of Ishab that dwell in Shaʾer, and the Muwwabites that dwell in Ar, did to me.”

And Siyyon would not allow Yishraʾel to pass through his territory. And Shema said to Mushi: “Behold, I have begun to deliver up Siyyon and his land before you. Begin to take possession, that you may inherit his land.” Siyyon gathered all his people together and went out against Yishraʾel into the wilderness, and came to Yēṣṣa, and he fought against Yishraʾel.

And Yishraʾel defeated him and his sons and all his people with the edge of the sword, and they possessed his land from the Arenan to the Yibbaq, as far as to the children of ʿAmmon, for the border of the children of ʿAmmon was strong.
And Yishraʾel took all these cities. And Yishraʾel dwelt in all the cities of the Emarites, in Ishbon, and in all its towns.
For Ishbon was the city of Siyyon the king of the Emarites, and it is he who had fought against the former king of Muwwab and taken all his land out of his hand, as far as the Arenan.
Therefore the ballad singers who come to Ishbon say: “Let the city of Siyyon be built and established.
For a fire has gone out of Ishbon, a flame from the city of Siyyon. It has devoured until Muwwab, the lords of the high places of the Arenan.
Woe to you, Muwwab! You are undone, O people of Kamosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to the Emarite king, Siyyon.
We have caused desolation [from] Ishbon to Dibon, and we set on fire Midabe until Anafa.”
Thus Yishraʾel dwelt in the cities of the Emarites.
And Mushi sent to spy out Yāzzer. And they took its towns, and they drove out the Emarites that were there.
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Ūg the king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Idri.

And Shema said to Mushi: “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, and all his people, and his land. And you shall do to him as you did to Siyyon, king of the Emarites, who dwelt at Ish-bon.”
So they defeated him and all his people, until there was no one left him remaining, and they possessed his land.
And the children of Yishraʾel journeyed and encamped in the plains of Muwwab beyond the Yardan at Yariyyu.
And Balaq the son of Ṣibbor saw all that Yishraʾel had done to the Emarites.
And Muwwab was in great dread of the people because they were many. And Muwwab was distressed because of the children of Yishraʾel.

And Muwwab said to the elders of Madyan: “Now will this horde lick up all that is round about us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.” And Balaq the son of Ṣibbor was king of Muwwab at that time.

And he sent messengers to Baˈlam the son of Būr, the interpreter, which is by the river, to the land of the children of ʿAmmon, to call him, saying: “Behold, a people has come out from Miṣrem. And behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they are dwelling opposite me.

Come now, I pray you, curse this people for me, for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land, for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
And the elders of Muwwab and the elders of Madyan departed with their fees for divination in their hand. And they came to Baˈlam, and spoke to him the words of Balaq.
And he said to them: “Lodge here tonight, and I will bring back word to you, as Shema shall speak to me.” And the princes of Muwwab stayed with Baˈlam.
And God came to Baˈlam, and said: “What men are these with you?”
And Baˈlam said to God: “Balaq the son of Ṣibbor, king of Muwwab, has sent [them] to me, [saying],
‘Behold, a people has come out from Miṣrem, and it covers the face of the earth. Come now, curse them for me. Perhaps I shall be able to fight against them, and shall drive them out.’”
And God said to Baˈlam: “You shall not go with them and you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.”
And Baˈlam rose in the morning and said to the princes of Balaq: “Go to your land, for Shema refuses to let me go with you.”
And the princes of Muwwab rose, and they went to Balaq, and said: “Baˈlam refuses to come with us.”
And Balaq sent princes once again, more numerous and more honourable than they.
And they came to Baˈlam, and said to him: “Thus says Balaq the son of Ṣibbor, ‘Let nothing, I pray you, hinder you from coming to me,
for I will promote you to very great honour, and whatever you say to me I will do. Come therefore, I pray you, curse this people for me.’”
And Baˈlam answered and said to the servants of Balaq: “Even if Balaq gives me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go beyond the word of Shema my God, to do less or more.
Now therefore, I pray you, tarry here tonight also, that I may know what more Shema will say to me.”
And the angel of God came to Baˈlam at night, and said to him: “If the men have come to call you, rise, go with them, but only the word which I speak to you, that shall you do.”
And Baˈlam rose in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Muwwab.
And Shema’s anger was kindled because he went, and the angel of Shema placed himself in the way to oppose him. Now he was riding on his ass, and his two servants were with him.

And the ass saw the angel of Shema standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand. And the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field. And Baˈlam struck the ass, to turn her into the way.
Then the angel of Shema stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side.
And the ass saw the angel of Shema, and she was pressed to the wall and pressed Baˈlam’s foot against the wall. And he struck her again.
And the angel of Shema went further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right or to the left.
And the ass saw the angel of Shema, and she lay down under Baˈlam. And Baˈlam’s anger was kindled, and he struck the ass with his staff.
And Shema opened the mouth of the ass, and she said to Baˈlam: “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
And Baˈlam said to the ass: “Because you have mocked me. I wish I had a sword in my hand, for then I would kill you.”
And the ass said to Baˈlam: “Behold, I am your ass, on which you have ridden all your life long to this day! Was I ever accustomed to doing so to you?” And he said: “No.”
Then Shema opened the eyes of Baˈlam, and he saw the angel of Shema standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand, and he bowed down, and fell on his face.
And the angel of Shema said to him: “Why have you struck your ass these three times? Behold, I have come forth to oppose you because your way is bad before me.
And the ass saw me and turned aside from before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, surely now I would have killed you and saved her life.”
And Baˈlam said to the angel of Shema: “I have sinned, for I did not know that you stood in the way against me. Now therefore, if it displeases you, I will go back again.”
And the angel of Shema said to Baˈlam: “Go with the men, but only the word that I shall speak to you, that shall you keep to speak.” So Baˈlam went with the princes of Balaq.
And when Balaq heard that Baˈlam had come, he went out to meet him to the City of Muwwab, which is on the border of the Arenan, at the extremity of the border.
And Balaq said to Baˈlam: “Behold, I earnestly sent to you to call you! Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honour you?”
And Baˈlam said to Balaq: “Lo, I have come to you! Have I now any power at all to speak anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that I shall keep to speak.”
And Baˈlam went with Balaq, and he brought him to Qaryat-iṣot.
And Balaq sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent to Baˈlam and to the princes who were with him.
And in the morning, Balaq took Baˈlam and brought him up to Bamot-bāl, and he saw from there the utmost part of the people.
And Baˈlam said to Balaq: “Make for me here seven altars and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
And Balaq did as Baˈlam had spoken, and Balaq and Baˈlam offered on every altar a bull and a ram.
And Baˈlam said to Balaq: “Stand by your burned offerings and I will go. Perhaps God will come to meet me and will tell me what he shows me, and I will tell you.” And he went hidden.
And the angel of God found Baˈlam, and he said to him: “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.”
And the angel of Shema put a word in Baˈlam’s mouth and said: “Return to Balaq, and thus you shall speak.”
And he returned to him, and lo, he was standing by his burned offerings, he and all the princes of Muwwab.
And he took up his parable, and said: “From Aram has Balaq brought me, the king of Muwwab from the mountains of the East: ‘Come, curse me Yāqob, and come, defy Yishraʾel.’
How shall I curse, whom God has not cursed? And how shall I defy, whom Shema has not defied?
For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I praise him. Lo, a people dwells alone and shall not be reckoned among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Yāqob or number the fourth part of Yishraʾel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!”
And Balaq said to Baˈlam: “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them altogether.”
And he answered and said: “Behold, I must take heed to speak that which Shema puts in my mouth!”

And Balaq said to him: “Come, I pray you, with me to another place, [so that] you may see them. You shall see only the utmost part of them, and shall not see them all, and curse them for me from there.”
And he took him into Shadi-ṣabbem to the top of Affasga, and built seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
And he said to Balaq: “Stand by your burned offerings, while I call here.”
And the angel of Shema called Baˈlam and put a word in his mouth and said: “Return to Balaq and thus you shall speak.”
And he came to him, and lo, he was standing by his burned offerings, and the princes of Muwwab with him. And Balaq said to him: “What has Shema spoken?”
And he took up his parable and said: “Rise up, Balaq, and hear; listen to me, son of Ṣibbor.
God is not a man, that he should lie, neither the son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
Behold, I have received [a command] to bless. I have blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
I have not beheld iniquity in Yāqob, nor have I seen perverseness in Yishraʾel. Shema his God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
God who brings them out of Miṣrem is like the horns of a wild ox for them.
Surely there is no augur with Yāqob, neither is there anyone who practices divination with Yishraʾel. Now it shall be said of Yāqob and of Yishraʾel, ‘What has God wrought!’
Behold, the people rises up as a lioness, and as a lion does he lift himself up. He shall not lie down until he eats of the prey and drinks the blood of the slain.”
And Balaq said to Baˈlam: “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.”
But Baˈlam answered and said to Balaq: “Behold, I told you, saying, ‘Whatever thing God speaks, that I must do!’
And Balaq said to Baˈlam: “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.
And Balaq took Baˈlam to the top of Fūr, which overlooks the desert.
And Baˈlam said to Balaq: “Build me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
And Balaq did as Baˈlam had spoken, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
And when Baˈlam saw that it pleased Shema to bless Yishraʾel, he did not go, as at the other times, to meet with the augurs, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
And Baˈlam lifted up his eyes and he saw Yishraʾel dwelling according to their tribes, and the spirit of God came upon him.
And he took up his parable, and said: “The oracle of Baˈlam the son of Būr, the oracle of the man whose eye is open,
who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down but having [his] eye open.
How goodly are your tents, O Yāqob, and your encampments, O Yishraʾel!
Like valleys they are spread out, like gardens by the river-side, like tents which Shema has pitched, like cedar trees beside the waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Gog, and his kingdom shall be exalted.

God who has brought him out of Miṣrem is like the horns of a wild ox for them. He shall eat up the nations, his adversaries, and shall break their bones in pieces and strike [them] through with his arrows.
He crouches, he lies down as a lion and as a lioness. Who shall rouse him up? Blessed be everyone that blesses you, and cursed be everyone that curses you.”

And Balaq’s anger was kindled against Baˈlam, and he struck his hands together. And Balaq said to Baˈlam: “I called you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times.
Therefore now flee to your place. I thought to promote you to great honour, but lo, Shema has kept you back from honour.”
And Baˈlam said to Balaq: “Behold, I spoke to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,
‘If Balaq would give me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go beyond the word of Shema, to do either good or bad of my own mind. What Shema speaks to me, that I will speak!’
And now, behold, I go to my people. Come, and I will let you know what this people shall do to your people in the latter days.”
And he took up his parable, and said: “The oracle of Baˈlam the son of Būr, the oracle of the man whose eye is open,
the oracle of him who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and having his eyes open.

I see him, but not now; I praise him, but not near. There shall come forth a star out of Yāqob, and a scepter shall rise out of Yishraʾel. He shall strike through the corners of Muwwab, and the head of all the children of Shat.
And Edom shall be a possession, Ishab also, his enemies, shall be a possession, while Yishraʾel shall triumph.
And out of Yāqob shall one have dominion and shall destroy the remnant from the city.”
And he looked on ʿAmaleq and took up his parable, and said: “ʿAmaleq was the first of the nations, but his latter end is to perish forever.”
And he looked on the Qenite, and took up his parable, and said: “Strong is your dwelling-place, and your nest is set in the rock.
Nevertheless Qen shall be wasted until your return from Ashor.”
And he took up his parable, and said: “Woe to him who will be counted with its name. God
shall bring them out of the hand of Kittem, [and] they shall afflict Ashor, and shall afflict Ebar, and he also shall perish forever.”
And Baˈlam rose and went and returned to his place, and Balaq also went his way.
And Yishraʾel abode in Shiṭṭem, and the people began to play the whore with the daughters of Muwwab.
They called the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down to their gods.
And [some] of the children of Yishraʾel joined themselves to Bāl-fūr. And the anger of Shema was kindled against Yishraʾel.
And Shema said to Mushi: “Command, and the people who joined themselves to Bal-fūr shall be killed, that the fierce anger of Shema may turn away from Yishraʾel.”
And Mushi said to the judges of Yishraʾel: “Everyone of you kill his men who have joined themselves to Bāl-fūr.”

And, behold, one of the children of Yishraʾel came and brought to his brothers a Madyanite woman in the sight of Mushi and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And when Fiˈnas the son of Elāzar, the son of Ārron the priest, saw it, he rose from the midst of the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
And he went after the man of Yishraʾel into the chamber and thrust both of them through, the man of Yishraʾel and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Yishraʾel.
And those that died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:

“Fiˈnas the son of Elāzar, the son of Ārron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yishraʾel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I did not consume the children of Yishraʾel in my jealousy.
Therefore say, ‘Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace,
and it shall be to him and to his offspring after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the children of Yishraʾel.’”
Now the name of the slain man of Yishraʾel, who was slain with the Madyanite woman, was Zamri the son of Sillu, a prince of a father’s house among the Sheˈmunites.
And the name of the Madyanite woman that was slain was Kazbet, the daughter of Ṣor, who was the head of the people of a father’s house in Madyan.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Harass the Madyanites and strike them,

for they have harassed you with their wiles, with which they have beguiled you in the matter of Fūr and in the matter of Kazbet, the daughter of the prince of Madyan, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Fūr.”
And after the plague.
Shema spoke to Mushi and to Elāzar the son of Ārron the priest, saying:
“Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, from twenty years old and up, by their fathers’ houses, all that are able to go out to war in Yishraʾel.”
And Mushi and Elāzar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu, saying:
“[Take the sum of the people] from twenty years old and up, as Shema commanded Mushi and the children of Yishraʾel that came out of the land of Miṣrem.
Reʾuben, the first-born of Yishraʾel, and the sons of Reʾuben: [of] Inok, the family of the Inokites; of Fillu, the family of the Filluites;
of Iṣron, the family of the Iṣronites; of Karmi, the family of the Karmites.
These are the families of the Reʾubenites, and they that were numbered of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
The sons of Fillu: Ilyab.

And the sons of Ilyab: Namuwwel, Datan, and Abiram. These are the Datan and Abiram, who were called of the congregation, who gathered against Mushi and against Ārron in the company of Qara, when they gathered against Shema,
and the earth opened its mouth, and the earth swallowed them up, when that company died, when the fire devoured Qara and two hundred and fifty men. And they became a sign.
Notwithstanding, the sons of Qara did not die.
The sons of Sheˈmun after the families of the Sheˈmunites: of Namuwwel, the family of the Namuwwelites; of Yamen, the family of the Yamenites; of Yaken, the family of the Yakenites;
of Zara, the family of the Zaraites; of Shaʾol, the family of the Shaʾolites.
These are the families of the Sheˈmunites, twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The sons of Gad after their families: of Ṣaˈfun, the family of the Ṣaˈfunites; of Iggi, the family of the Iggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites;
of Ezni, the family of the Eznites; of Iddi, the family of the Iddites;
of Arbaddi, the family of the Arbaddites; of Arballi, the family of the Arballites.
These are the families of Gad according to those that were numbered of them, forty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Yeʾuda: Ar and Unan; and Ar and Unan died in the land of Kaˈnan.
And the sons of Yeʾuda after their families were: of Shila, the family of the Shilanites; of Faraṣ, the family of the Faraṣites; of Zara, the family of the Zaraites.
And the sons of Faraṣ were: of Iṣron, the family of the Iṣronites; of Amuwwel, the family of the Amuwwelites.
These are the families of Yeʾuda according to those that were numbered of them, seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The sons of Yashishakar after their families: of Tula, the family of the Tulaites; of Fuwwa, the family of the Fuwwaites;
of Yeshob, the family of the Yeshobites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Yashishakar according to those that were numbered of them, sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The sons of Zebulan after their families: of Sarad, the family of the Saradites; of Alon, the family of the Alonites; of Yēllaʾel, the family of the Yēllaʾelites.
These are the families of Zebulan according to those that were numbered of them, sixty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Yusef after their families: Manashi and Ifrem.
The sons of Manashi: of Maker, the family of the Makerites; and Maker begot Gaˈlad: [of Gaˈlad], the family of the Gaˈladites.
These are the sons of Gaˈlad: [of] ʿĀyyazar, the family of the ʿĀyyazarites; and [of] Alaq, the family of the Alaqites;
and [of] Ishruwwal, the family of the Ishruwwalites; and [of] Ashkem, the family of the Ashkemites;
and [of] Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and [of] ʿAfar, the family of the ʿAfarites.
And Ṣalaˈfad the son of ʿAfar had no sons, but daughters, and the names of the daughters of Ṣalaˈfad were Maʾela, and Niyya, Igla, Milka, and Tirṣa.
These are the families of Manashi according to those that were numbered of them, fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
And these are the sons of Ifrem after their families: of Shutala, the family of the Shutalaites; of Bakar, the family of the Bakarites; of Tām, the family of the Tāmites.
These are the sons of Shutala: of Eden, the family of the Edenites.
These are the families of the sons of Ifrem according to those that were numbered of them, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Yusef after their families.
The sons of Binyamem after their families: of Bala, the family of the Balaites; of Ashˈbil, the family of the Ashˈbilites; of Aʾiram, the family of the Aʾiramites;
of Shufam, the family of the Shufamites; of Ufam, the family of the Ufamites;
of Erad, the family of the Eradites; of Nēmman, the family of the Nēmmanites.
These are the sons of Binyamem after their families, and those that were numbered of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.
And these are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuwwam, the family of the Shuwwamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.
All the families of the Shuwwamites, and those that were numbered of them were sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The sons of Asher after their families: of Yamne, the family of the Yamnites; of Yashbi, the family of the Yashbites; of Barye, the family of the Baryites;
of Abar, the family of the Abarites; of Malˈkil, the family of the Malˈkilites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher was Shara.
These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those that were numbered of them, fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The sons of Niftali after their families: of Yeṣṣaʾel, the family of the Yeṣṣaʾelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites;
of Yaṣar, the family of the Yaṣarites; of Shillom, the family of the Shillomites.
These are the families of Niftali according to their families, and those that were numbered of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
These are they that were numbered of the children of Yishraʾel, six hundred and one thousand and seven hundred and thirty.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“To these you shall divide the land for an inheritance according to the number of names.

To the more [numerous] you shall give the more inheritance, and to the less [numerous] you shall give the less inheritance; to everyone according to those that were numbered of him shall his inheritance be given.
Notwithstanding, one shall divide the land by lot; according to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
According to the lot one shall divide their inheritance between the larger and the smaller.”
And these are those who were numbered of the Libites after their families: of Girshon, the family of the Girshonites; of Qāt, the family of the Qātites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.

These are the families of the sons of Libi: the family of the Libnites, and the family of the Ibronites, and the family of the Mēllites, and the family of the Qaraites, and the family of the Mushites. And Qāt begot ʿAmram.
And the name of ʿAmram’s wife was Yukabed the daughter of Libi, who was born to Libi in Miṣrem. And she bore to ʿAmram Ārron and Mushi, and Maryam their sister.
And to Ārron were born Nadab, and Abiyyu, Elāzar, and Itamar.
And Nadab and Abiyyu died when they offered alien fire before Shema.

And those who were numbered of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and up, for they were not numbered among the children of Yishraʾel, because there was no inheritance given them among the children of Yishraʾel.
These are they that were numbered by Mushi and Elāzar the priest, who numbered the children of Yishraʾel in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu.
But among these there was not a man of those who were numbered by Mushi and Ārron the priest, who numbered the children of Yishraʾel in the wilderness of Sini.
For Shema had said of them: “They shall surely be put to death in the wilderness. And there was no man left of them, except Kilab the son of Yefanni and Yeʾusha the son of Non.

Then drew near the daughters of Ṣalaˈfad, the son of ʿAfar, the son of Gaˈlad, the son of Maker, the son of Manashi, of the families of Manashi the son of Yusef; and these are the names of his daughters: Maʾela, and Niyya, Igla, Milka, and Tirṣa.
And they stood before Mushi and before Elāzar the priest and before the princes and all the congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, saying:

“Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company of those who gathered themselves together against Shema in the company of Qara, but our father died in his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession of an inheritance among the brothers of our father.”
And Mushi brought their cause before Shema.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“The daughters of Ṣalaˈfad are right. You shall give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and you shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them.
And you shall speak to the children of Yishraʾel, saying, ‘If a man dies and has no son, then you shall give his inheritance to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his kin that is near to him from his family, and he shall possess him; and it shall be to the children of Yishraʾel a statute [and] ordinance, as Shema commanded Mushi.’”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying: “Get up into this Mount Aʾibrem and behold the land which I have given to the children of Yishraʾel.
And when you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people as Ārron your brother was gathered,

because you rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Ṣen, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the waters before their eyes.” (These are the waters of Maribat-qadesh in the wilderness of Ṣen.)
And Mushi spoke to Shema, saying:
“Let Shema, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
who may go out before them and who may come in before them, and who may lead them out and who may bring them in, that the congregation of Shema may not be as sheep which have no shepherd.”
And Shema said to Mushi: “Take Yeʾusha the son of Non, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay your hand upon him,
and set him before Elāzar the priest and before all the congregation, and give him a charge in their sight.
And you shall put of your honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel may obey.

And he shall stand before Elāzar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before Shema. At his word he shall go out, and at his word he shall come in, both he, and all the children of Yishraʾel with him, the whole congregation.”
And Mushi did as Shema commanded him, and he took Yeʾusha, and set him before Elāzar the priest, and before all the congregation,

and he laid his hand on him, and gave him a charge, as Shema spoke by Mushi. [a] And he said to him: “Your eyes have seen what Shema your God has done to these two kings. So shall Shema do to all the kingdoms into which you are going over. You shall not fear them, [b] for it is Shema your God who fights for you”.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Command the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘My offering, my food for offering made by fire of a sweet savour to me, shall you observe to offer to me in its due seasons.’
And you shall say to them, ‘This is the fire which you shall offer to Shema: male lambs a year old without blemish, two day by day, for a continual burned offering.
The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer at twilight;
and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of oil.
It is a continual burned offering, which was ordained in Mount Sini for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire to Shema.
And its drink offerings shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb. In the holy [place] shall you pour out a drink offer- ing of strong drink to Shema.
And the other lamb you shall offer at twilight. As the meal offering of the morning and as its drink offerings you shall offer it, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema.
And on the Sabbath day two male lambs a year old without blemish, and two tenth parts [of an ephah] of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with oil, and its drink offerings.
This is the burned offering of every Sabbath, besides the continual burned offering and their drink offerings.
And in the beginnings of your months you shall offer a burned offering to Shema: two young bulls, and one ram, seven male lambs a year old without blemish;

and three tenth parts [of an ephah] of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with oil, for each bull, and two tenth parts [of an ephah] of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with oil, for the one ram;
and a tenth part [of an ephah] of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal offering to every lamb; for a burned offering of a sweet savour, an offering made by fire to Shema.

And their drink offerings [shall be] half a hin of wine for each bull, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for each lamb. This is the burned offering of every month throughout the months of the year.
And one male goat for a sin offering to Shema; it shall be offered besides the continual burned offering, and their drink offerings.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is Shema’s Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month shall be a feast. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
In the first day shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no servile work,
but you shall offer an offering made by fire, a burned offering to Shema: two young bulls, and one ram, and seven male lambs a year old; they shall be to you without blemish;
and their meal offering, fine flour mingled with oil; three tenth parts [of an ephah] shall you offer for a bull, and two tenth parts for the ram;
and a tenth part [of an ephah] [you shall offer] for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these besides the burned offering of the morning, which is for a continual burned offering.

After this manner you shall daily offer, for seven days, the food of the offering made by fire, of a sweet savour to Shema. It shall be offered besides the continual burned offering, and their drink offerings.
And on the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no servile work.
In the day of the first-fruits, when you offer a new meal offering to Shema in your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no servile work,
but you shall offer a burned offering, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema: two young bulls, and one ram, seven male lambs a year old; they shall be to you without blemish;
and their meal offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts [of an ephah] for each bull, and two tenth parts [of an ephah] for the one ram,
and a tenth part [of an ephah] for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat, for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
Besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering, you shall offer them; they shall be to you without blemish, and their drink offerings.
And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no servile work. It is a day of blowing of trumpets to you.
And you shall offer a burned offering for a sweet savour to Shema: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without blemish;
and their meal offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts [of an ephah] for the bull, and two tenth parts [of an ephah] for the ram,
and a tenth part [of an ephah] for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

besides the burned offering of the new moon, and its meal offering, and the continual burned offering and its meal offering, and its drink offerings, according to their ordinance, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire to Shema.
And on the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation, and you shall afflict your souls, and you shall do no manner of work,
but you shall offer a burned offering to Shema for a sweet savour: one young bull, and one ram, seven male lambs a year old; they shall be to you without blemish;
and their meal offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts [of an ephah] for the bull and two tenth parts [of an ephah] for the one ram,
and a tenth part [of an ephah] for every lamb of the seven lambs;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the sin offering of atonement and the continual burned offering and its meal offering, and its drink offerings.
And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no servile work, and you shall keep a feast to Shema seven days.
And you shall offer a burned offering, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema, thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old; they shall be to you without blemish;
and their meal offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts [of an ephah] for every bull of the thirteen bulls, and two tenth parts [of an ephah] for each ram of the two rams,
and a tenth part [of an ephah] for every lamb of the fourteen lambs and their drink offerings;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering and its drink offerings.
And on the second day [you shall offer] twelve young bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish;
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offerings.
And on the third day eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering and its drink offerings.
And on the fourth day ten bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offerings.
And on the fifth day nine bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering, and its meal offering and its drink offerings.
And on the sixth day eight bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering, and its drink offerings.
And on the seventh day seven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
and one male goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering and its drink offerings.
And on the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly; you shall do no servile work,
but you shall offer a burned offering, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour to Shema: one bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without blemish,
and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the ordinance,
and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the continual burned offering and its meal offering and its drink offerings.

These you shall offer to Shema in your set feasts, besides your vows and your freewill offerings, for your burned offerings, and for your meal offerings, and for your drink offerings, and for your peace offerings.”
And Mushi told the children of Yishraʾel according to all that Shema commanded Mushi.
