And Mushi spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Yishraʾel saying: “This is the thing which Shema has commanded:
When a man vows a vow to Shema, or swears an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his words; he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
Also when a woman vows a vow to Shema and binds herself by a bond, being in her father’s house, in her youth,

and her father hears her vows and her bonds by which she has bound her soul, and her father remains silent to her, then all her vows shall stand, and her bonds by which she has bound her soul shall stand.

But if her father diligently opposes her on the day that he hears, none of her vows or of her bonds by which she has bound her soul shall stand. And Shema will forgive her because her father opposed her.
And if she is married to a husband, while her vows are upon her or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound her soul,
and her husband hears it and remains silent to her on the day that he hears it, then all her vows shall stand, and her bonds by which she has bound her soul shall stand.

But if her husband opposes her on the day that he hears it, then he shall make void her vows which are upon her or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound her soul. And Shema will forgive her.
But the vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound her soul, shall stand against her.
And if she vowed in her husband’s house or bound her soul by a bond with an oath,
and her husband heard it and remains silent to her and does not oppose her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her bonds by which she bound her soul shall stand.

But if her husband made them null and void on the day that he heard them, then whatever proceeded out of her lips concerning her vows or concerning the bond of her soul, shall not stand. Her husband has made them void. And Shema will forgive her.
Every vow and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish or her husband may make void.

But if her husband remains silent to her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows or all her bonds, which are upon her; he has established them because he remained silent to her on the day that he heard them.
But if he shall make them null and void after that he heard them, then he shall bear his iniquity.”
These are the statutes which Shema commanded Mushi between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter, being in her youth, in her father’s house.
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Avenge the children of Yishraʾel on the Madyanites and afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”
And Mushi spoke to the people, saying: “Arm men from among you for the war, that they may go against Madyan to execute Shema’s vengeance on Madyan.
Of every tribe a thousand, throughout all the tribes of Yishraʾel, shall you send to the war.”
So there were provided, out of the thousands of Yishraʾel, a thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
And Mushi sent them, a thousand of every tribe, to the war, them and Fiˈnas the son of Elāzar the priest, to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.
And they warred against Madyan as Shema commanded Mushi, and they killed every male.
And they killed the kings of Madyan with the rest of their slain: Uwwi, and Raqqam, and Ṣor, and Ūr, and Reba, the five kings of Madyan. Also Baˈlam the son of Būr they killed with the sword.
And the children of Yishraʾel took captive the women of Madyan and their little ones; and all their cattle, and all their flocks, and all their goods, they took as plunder.
And all their cities in the places where they dwelt, and all their encampments, they burned with fire.
And they took all the spoil and all the booty, both of man and of beast.

And they brought the captives and the booty and the spoil to Mushi, and to Elāzar the priest, and to all the congregation of the children of Yishraʾel, to the camp on the plains of Muwwab, which are by the Yardan at Yariyyu.
And Mushi and Elāzar the priest and all the princes of the congregation went forth to meet them outside the camp.
And Mushi was angry with the officers of the army, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, who had come from the service in the war.
And Mushi said to them: “Why did you let all the women live
here? These caused the children of Yishraʾel, through the counsel of Baˈlam, to commit trespass against Shema in the matter of Fūr, and so the plague came among the congregation of Shema.
Now therefore, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.
But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him keep alive for yourselves.
And you, encamp outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed any person and whoever has touched any slain, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.

And every garment, and anything made of skin, and all work of goats’ [hair], and anything made of wood, you shall purify.” [a] And Mushi said to Elāzar the priest: “Say to the men of war who went to the battle, ‘This is the statute of the law which Shema has commanded: [b] Only the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the iron, and the tin, and the lead, [c] everything that can stand the fire, you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean. Nevertheless it shall be purified with the water for impurity. And whatever cannot stand the fire, you shall pass through the water. [d] And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean. And afterward you shall come into the camp.”
And Elāzar the priest said to the men of war who went to the battle: “This is the statute of the law which Shema has commanded Mushi:
Only the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the iron, and the tin, and the lead,

everything that can stand the fire, you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean. Nevertheless it shall be purified with the water for impurity. And whatever cannot stand the fire, you shall pass through the water.
And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean. And afterward you shall come into the camp.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Take the sum from the booty that was taken, both of man and of beast, you and Elāzar the priest and the heads of the fathers’ [houses] of the congregation,
and divide the booty into two parts, between the warriors who went out to battle and all the congregation.
And levy a tribute to Shema of the men of war who went out to battle, one soul of five hundred, of the persons and of the oxen and of the asses and of the flocks, of all the cattle.
Take it from their half and give it to Elāzar the priest for Shema’s heave offering.

And from the children of Yishraʾel’s half you shall take one drawn out of every fifty, of the persons, and of the oxen, and of the asses, and of the flocks, of all the cattle, and give them to the Libites who keep the charge of the tabernacle of Shema.”
And Mushi and Elāzar the priest did as Shema commanded Mushi.
Now the booty over and above the plunder which the men of war took was six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep,
and seventy-two thousand oxen,
and sixty-one thousand asses,
and thirty-two thousand persons of the women that had not known a man by lying with him.
And the half, which was the portion of those who went to war, was in number three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep.
And Shema’s tribute of the sheep was six hundred and seventy-five.
And the oxen were thirty-six thousand, of which Shema’s tribute was seventy-two.
And the asses were thirty thousand five hundred, of which Shema’s tribute was sixty-one.
And the persons were sixteen thousand, of which Shema’s tribute was thirty-two persons.
And Mushi gave the tribute, which was Shema’s heave offering, to Elāzar the priest, as Shema commanded Mushi.
And of the children of Yishraʾel’s half, which Mushi divided from that of the men who had gone to war.
Now the congregation’s half was three hundred and thirty and seven thousand five hundred sheep,
and thirty-six thousand oxen,
and thirty thousand five hundred asses,
and sixteen thousand persons.

And Mushi took from the children of Yishraʾel’s half one drawn out of every fifty, of man and of beast, and gave them to the Libites, who kept the charge of the tabernacle of Shema, as Shema commanded Mushi.
And the officers who were over the thousands of the army, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, came near to Mushi,
and they said to Mushi: “Your servants have counted the men of war who are under our charge, and there is not a man missing from us.
And we have brought Shema’s offering, what each man found, articles of gold, armlets, and bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and beads to make atonement for our souls before Shema.”
And Mushi and Elāzar the priest received from them the gold, all wrought articles.
And the gold of the heave offering that they offered up to Shema, from the captains of thousands and from the captains of hundreds was sixteen thousand and seven hundred and fifty shekels.
(The men of war had taken plunder, every man for himself.)
And Mushi and Elāzar the priest received the gold from the captains of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the children of Yishraʾel before Shema.

Now the children of Reʾuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashi had a very great multitude of cattle, and when they saw the land of Yāzzer and the land of Gaˈlad, that behold, the place was a place for cattle,
the children of Gad and the children of Reʾuben and the half-tribe of Manashi came and spoke to Mushi and to Elāzar the priest and to the princes of the congregation, saying:
“ʿAṭṭirot, and Dibon, and Yāzzer, and Nimra, and Ishbon, and Alela, and Shabbema, and Nabbu, and Būn,
the land which Shema struck down before the congregation of Yishraʾel is a land for cattle, and your servants have cattle.”
And they said: “If we have found favour in your sight, give this land to your servants for a possession and do not bring us over the Yardan.”
And Mushi said to the children of Reʾuben and to the children of Gad and to the half-tribe of Manashi: “Shall your brothers go to the war, and you shall sit here?
And why will you discourage the heart of the children of Yishraʾel from going over into the land which Shema has given them?
Your fathers did this, when I sent them from Qadesh-birna to see the land.
For when they went up to the valley of Ishkol and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the children of Yishraʾel from going into the land which Shema had given them.
And Shema’s anger was kindled on that day, and he swore, saying,
‘Surely none of the men that came up out of Miṣrem, from twenty years old and up, shall see the land which I swore to Abˈram, to Yeˈṣaq, and to Yāqob, because they have not wholly followed me,
except for Kilab the son of Yefanni the Qenazite and Yeʾusha the son of Non, because they have wholly followed Shema.’
And Shema’s anger was kindled against Yishraʾel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the sight of Shema was consumed.
And behold, you have risen up in your fathers’ stead, a brood of sinful men, to increase still more the fierce anger of Shema toward Yishraʾel.
For if you turn away from following him, he will yet again make them wander in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.”
And they came near to him, and said: “We will build sheepfolds here for our cattle, and cities for our little ones,

but we ourselves will take up arms, ready to go before the children of Yishraʾel, until we have brought them to their place, and our little ones shall dwell in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our houses until the children of Yishraʾel have inherited every man his inheritance.
For we will not inherit with them on the other side of the Yardan and beyond, because our inheritance has fallen to us on this side of the Yardan to the east.”
And Mushi said to them: “If you will do this thing, and if you will take up arms to go before Shema to the war,
and every armed man of you will pass over the Yardan before Shema, until he has driven out his enemies from before him,
and the land is subdued before Shema, then after that you shall return and be guiltless toward Shema and toward Yishraʾel, and this land shall be for you a possession before Shema.
But if you will not do so, behold, you have sinned against Shema, and be sure your sins will find you out.
Build cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do that which has proceeded out of your mouth.”
And the children of Reʾuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashi spoke to Mushi, saying: “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our little ones, and our wives, and our flocks, and all our cattle shall be there in the cities of Gaˈlad,
but your servants will pass over, every man that is armed for war, before Shema to battle, as my lord says.”
So Mushi gave command concerning them to Elāzar the priest and to Yeʾusha the son of Non and to the heads of the fathers’ [houses] of the tribes of the children of Yishraʾel.

And Mushi said to them: “If the children of Reʾuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashi will pass with you over the Yardan, every man that is armed to battle, before Shema, and the land shall be subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gaˈlad for a possession,
but if they will not pass over with you armed, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Kaˈnan.”
And the children of Reʾuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashi answered, saying: “As Shema has said to your servants, so we will do.
We will pass over armed before Shema into the land of Kaˈnan, and the possession of our inheritance [shall remain] with us beyond the Yardan.”

And Mushi gave to them, to the children of Reʾuben and to the children of Gad and to the half-tribe of Manashi the son of Yusef, the kingdom of Siyyon king of the Emarites and the kingdom of Ūg king of Bashan, a land, according to its cities with [their] borders, the cities of the land round about.
And the children of Gad built Dibon, and ʿAṭṭirot, and ʿArˈʿar,
and ʿAṭṭirot-shabbem, and Yāzzer, and they expanded it,
and Bet-nimra, and Bet-arran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
And the children of Reʾuben built Ishbon, and Alela, and Qaryatem,
and Nabbu, and Bālmon, encircled there, and Shabbema, and they gave the names to the cities which they built.
And the children of Maker the son of Manashi went to Gaˈlad, and took it, and dispossessed the Emarites that were in it.
And Mushi gave Gaˈlad to Maker the son of Manashi, and he settled in it.
And Yaʾer the son of Manashi went and took Uwwatem, and called them Uwwat-yaʾer.
And Naba went and took Qenat and its villages, and called it Naba, after his own name.
These are the journeys of the children of Yishraʾel, when they went out of the land of Miṣrem by their hosts under the hand of Mushi and Ārron.
And Mushi wrote their starting places according to their journeys by the commandment of Shema, and these are their journeys according to their starting places.

And they journeyed from Rāmses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the children of Yishraʾel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all their first-born, whom Shema had struck down among them. Upon their gods also Shema executed judgments.
And the children of Yishraʾel journeyed from Rāmses and encamped in Sakkot.
And they journeyed from Sakkot and encamped in Atem, which is in the edge of the wilderness.
And they journeyed from Atem and they settled at Fi-aʾirat, which is before Bāl-ṣafon, and they encamped before Magdal.
And they journeyed from Fiaʾirat and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Atem and encamped in Mirra.
And they journeyed from Mirra, and came to Ilem. And in Ilem were twelve springs of water, and seventy palm trees. And they encamped there.
And they journeyed from Ilem and encamped by the sea of Sof.
And they journeyed from the sea of Sof and encamped in the wilderness of Sen.
And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sen and encamped in Difqa.
And they journeyed from Difqa and encamped in Illesh.
And they journeyed from Illesh, and encamped in Refidem, where there was no water for the people to drink.
And they journeyed from Refidem and encamped in the wilderness of Sini.
And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sini and encamped in Qabarot-attawwa.
And they journeyed from Qabarot-attawwa and encamped in Aṣirot.
And they journeyed from Aṣirot and encamped in Ritma.
And they journeyed from Ritma, and encamped in Rimmon-faraṣ.
And they journeyed from Rimmonfaraṣ and encamped in Lebuna.
And they journeyed from Lebuna and encamped in Rissa.
And they journeyed from Rissa and encamped in Qēllata.
And they journeyed from Qēllata and encamped in Mount Ashfar.
And they journeyed from Mount Ashfar and encamped in Aridda.
And they journeyed from Aridda and encamped in Maqēllat.
And they journeyed from Maqēllat and encamped in Teʾat.
And they journeyed from Teʾat and encamped in Tirra.
And they journeyed from Tirra and encamped in Matiqa.
And they journeyed from Matiqa and encamped in Ashmuna.
And they journeyed from Ashmuna and encamped in Masirot.
And they journeyed from Masirot, and encamped in Bani-yaqan.
And they journeyed from Bani-yaqan and encamped in Mount Aggidgeda.
And they journeyed from Mount Aggidgeda and encamped in Yeṭibta.
And they journeyed from Yeṭibta and encamped in Ebirna.
And they journeyed from Ebirna and encamped in Iṣṣiyyon-gebar.
And they journeyed from Iṣṣiyyongebar and encamped in the wilderness of Ṣen—that is, Kadesh.
And they journeyed from Qadesh and encamped in Mount Ar, on the edge of the land of Edom.

And Ārron the priest went up Mount Ar at the command of Shema and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Yishraʾel had come out of the land of Miṣrem, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
And Ārron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Ar.
And the Kaˈnanite, the king of ʿArad, who dwelt in the south in the land of Kaˈnan, heard of the coming of the children of Yishraʾel.
And they journeyed from Mount Ar and encamped in Ṣalamuna.
And they journeyed from Ṣalamuna and encamped in Finan.
And they journeyed from Finan and encamped in Abbot.
And they journeyed from Abbot and encamped in Ayyi-aʾibrem, in the territory of Muwwab.
And they journeyed from Ayyem and encamped in Dibon-gad.
And they journeyed from Dibon-gad and encamped in Alamon-adbalatima.
And they journeyed from Alamon-adbalatima and encamped in the mountains of Aʾibrem, before Nabbu.
And they journeyed from the mountains of Aʾibrem and encamped in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu.
And they encamped by the Yardan, from Betayyashimot as far as Ebel-shiṭṭem in the plains of Muwwab.
And Shema spoke to Mushi in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘When you pass over the Yardan into the land of Kaˈnan,
then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured [stones], and destroy all their molten images, and demolish all their high places,
and you shall take possession of the land, and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.

And you shall inherit the land by lot according to your families. To the more [numerous] you shall give the more in- heritance, and to the less [numerous] you shall give the less inheritance. Wherever the lot falls to any man, that shall be his. According to the tribes of your fathers shall you inherit.

But if you will not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those of them whom you let remain shall be as pricks in your eyes, and as thorns in your sides, and they shall trouble you in the land where you dwell.
And as I thought to do to them, so I will do to you.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Command the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land of Kaˈnan (this is the land that shall fall to you for an inheritance, the land of Kaˈnan according to its borders),
then your south side shall be from the wilderness of Ṣen along by the side of Edom, and your south border shall be from the end of the Salt Sea on the east.
And your border shall turn south of Mala-ʿaqrabbem, and pass along to Ṣen, and its end shall be south of Qadesh-birna. And it shall go on to Aṣar-adar, and pass along to ʿAṣamuna.
And the border shall turn from ʿAṣamuna to the brook of Miṣrem, and its end shall be at the sea.
And your western border shall be: The great sea shall set up the border. This shall be your western border.
And this shall be your northern border: from the great sea you shall draw a line to Mount Ar.
And from Mount Ar you shall draw a line to the entrance of Amet, and its end shall be the border at Ṣared.
And the border shall go to Zifrinna, and its end shall be at Aṣar-inan. This shall be your northern border.
And you shall draw a line for your eastern border from Aṣar-inan to Ashfema.
And the border shall go down from Ashfema to Arebiˈla, on the east side of Ain. And the border shall go down and shall reach to the side of the sea of Kinnaret on the east.
And the border shall go down to the Yardan, and its end shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its borders round about.”
And Mushi commanded the children of Yishraʾel, saying: “This is the land which you shall inherit by lot, which Shema has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half- tribe.

For the tribe of the children of Reʾuben according to their fathers’ houses and the tribe of the children of Gad according to their fathers’ houses have received their inheritance, and also the half-tribe of Manashi.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Yardan at east of Yariyyu, toward the sunrise.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“These are the names of the men that shall divide the land to you for inheritance: Elāzar the priest and Yeʾusha the son of Non.
And you shall take one prince of every tribe to divide the land for inheritance.
And these are the names of the men: Of the tribe of Yeʾuda, Kilab the son of Yefanni.
Of the tribe of the children of Sheˈmun, Shamuwwel the son of ʿAmmiyyod.
Of the tribe of Binyamem, Ildad the son of Kislan.
Of the tribe of the children of Dan a prince, Beqi the son of Yigli.
Of the children of Yusef: Of the tribe of the children of Manashi a prince, Aˈnil the son of Ibbod.
And of the tribe of the children of Ifrem a prince, Qamuwwel the son of Shifṭan.
And of the tribe of the children of Zebulan a prince, Eliṣafan the son of Farenak.
And of the tribe of the children of Yashishakar a prince, Filˈṭil the son of ʿIzzan.
And of the tribe of the children of Asher a prince, Āyyod the son of Shalmi.
And of the tribe of the children of Niftali a prince, Fadaʾel the son of ʿAmmiyyod.
These are they whom Shema commanded to divide the inheritance to the children of Yishraʾel in the land of Kaˈnan.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu, saying:
“Command the children of Yishraʾel to give to the Libites from the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in, and pasture-land for the cities round about them you shall give to the Libites.
And the cities they shall have to dwell in and their pasturelands shall be for their cattle and for their substance and for all their beasts.
And the pasturelands of the cities which you shall give to the Libites shall be from the wall of the city outward one thousand cubits round about.

And you shall measure outside the city, on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, the city being in the middle. This shall be to you the pasturelands of the cities.
And the cities which you shall give to the Libites, they shall be the six cities of refuge which you shall give for the murderer to flee to, and besides them you shall give forty-two cities.
All the cities which you shall give to the Libites shall be forty-eight cities, them and their pasturelands.

And concerning the cities which you shall give from the possession of the children of Yishraʾel, from the larger [tribes] you shall take many, and from the smaller [tribes] you shall take few; each according to his inheritance which he inherits shall give of his cities to the Libites.”
And Shema spoke to Mushi, saying:
“Speak to the children of Yishraʾel, and say to them, ‘When you pass over the Yardan into the land of Kaˈnan,
then you shall appoint cities to be cities of refuge for you, that the murderer that kills any person unwittingly may flee there.
And the cities shall be to you for refuge from the avenger, that the murderer shall not be put to death until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
And the cities which you shall give shall be for you six cities of refuge.
You shall give three cities beyond the Yardan, and three cities you shall give in the land of Kaˈnan; they shall be cities of refuge.
For the children of Yishraʾel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them, these six cities shall be a refuge, that anyone who kills any person unwittingly may flee there.
But if he struck him with an instrument of iron, so that he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
And if he struck him with a stone that could cause death in hand, and he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
And if he struck him with a weapon of wood that could cause death in hand, and he died, he is a murderer. The murderer shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of blood shall himself put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.
And if he pushed him out of hatred, or hurled [something] at him, lying in wait, so that he died,
or in enmity struck him with his hand so that he died, he that struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer, the avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.
But if he pushes him suddenly without enmity, or hurled something at him without lying in wait,
or with any stone that could cause death, and without seeing him dropped it on him, so that he died, and he was not his enemy and did not seek his harm,
then the congregation shall judge between the murderer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.

And the congregation shall deliver the murderer from the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to his city of refuge to which he had fled, and he shall dwell in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the murderer shall at any time go beyond the border of his city of refuge to which he fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the murderer, he shall not be guilty of blood.
Because he must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest, but after the death of the high priest the murderer may return to the land of his possession.
And these things shall be for a statute of ordinance to you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the evidence of witnesses. But a single witness shall not be accepted for a sentence of death.
Moreover, you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer, who is guilty of death, but he shall surely be put to death.
And you shall take no ransom for him who has fled to his city of refuge, that he may return to dwell in the land before the death of the high priest.
So you shall not pollute the land which you inhabit, for blood, it pollutes the land, and no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, but by the blood of him who shed it.
And you shall not defile the land which you inhabit, in the midst of which I dwell, for I Shema dwell in the midst of the children of Yishraʾel.’”

And the heads of the fathers’ [houses] of the families of the children of Gaˈlad, the son of Maker, the son of Manashi, of the families of the sons of Yusef, came near and spoke before Mushi and before the princes, the heads of the fathers’ [houses] of the children of Yishraʾel.

And they said: “Shema commanded my lord to give the land for inheritance by lot to the children of Yishraʾel, and my lord commanded by Shema to give the inheritance of Ṣalaˈfad our brother to his daughters.

And if they are married to any of the sons of the [other] tribes of the children of Yishraʾel, then their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers, and it will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they shall belong. So it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.

And when the jubilee of the children of Yishraʾel comes, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they shall belong, so their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.”
And Mushi commanded the children of Yishraʾel according to the word of Shema, saying: “The tribe of the sons of Yusef is right.
This is the thing which Shema commands concerning the daughters of Ṣalaˈfad, saying, ‘Let them marry whom they think best, only into the families of the tribe of their father they shall be married.
So no inheritance of the children of Yishraʾel shall be removed from one tribe to another, for the children of Yishraʾel shall hold on everyone to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And every daughter that possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yishraʾel shall be wife to one of the families of the tribe of her father, so that the children of Yishraʾel may possess every man the inheritance of his fathers.
So no inheritance shall be removed from one tribe to another tribe, for the tribes of the children of Yishraʾel shall hold on everyone to his own inheritance.’”
As Shema commanded Mushi, so did the daughters of Ṣalaˈfad.
And Maʾela, and Niyya, Igla, Milka, and Tirṣa, the daughters of Ṣalaˈfad, were married to the sons of their father’s brothers.
They were married into the families of the sons of Manashi the son of Yusef, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
These are the commandments and the ordinances which Shema commanded by Mushi to the children of Yishraʾel in the plains of Muwwab by the Yardan at Yariyyu.
These are the words which Mushi spoke to all Yishraʾel beyond the Yardan, in the wilderness in the ʿAraba, opposite Sof, between Farran and Atfal and Libban and Aṣirot and Di-zāb.
It is eleven daysʼ [journey] from Ureb by the way of Mount Shaʾer to Qadesh-birna.
And in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Mushi spoke to the children of Yishraʾel, according to all that Shema had given him in commandment to them,
after he had struck Siyyon the king of the Emarites, who dwelt in Ishbon, and Ūg the king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ishtarot, at Idri.
Beyond the Yardan, in the land of Muwwab, Mushi undertook to write this law, saying:
“Shema our God spoke to us in Ureb, saying, ʻYou have stayed long enough in this mountain.

Turn and take your journey, and go to the hill country of the Emarites, and to all their dwellers in the ʿAraba, in the hill country and in the lowland [and] in the south and by the seacoast, the land of the Kaˈnanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Farat.
Behold, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land which I swore to your fathers, to Abˈram, to Yeˈṣaq, and to Yāqob, to give to their offspring after them.
And I spoke to you at that time, saying, ʻI am not able to bear you alone.
Shema your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are today as numerous as the stars of heaven.
Shema, the God of your fathers, will make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you, as he has promised you!
How can I alone bear your encumbrance, your burden, and your strife?
Take wise, and understanding, and experienced men, according to your tribes, and I will make them heads over you.ʼ
And you answered me, and said, ʻThat which you have spoken of doing is good.ʼ

So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and experienced men, and made them heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, according to your tribes.
And I charged your judges at that time, saying, ʻHear [the cases] between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the sojourner that is with him.

You shall not be partial in judgment. You shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is Godʼs. And the case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.ʼ
And I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do. >— —

And we journeyed from Ureb, and went through all that great and terrible wilderness which you saw, on the way to the hill country of the Emarites, as Shema our God commanded us. And we came to Qadesh-birna.
And I said to you, ʻYou have come to the hill country of the Emarites, which Shema our God gives us.
Behold, Shema your God has set the land before you. Go up, take possession, as Shema, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not fear or be dismayed.ʼ

And you came near to me everyone of you and said, ʻLet us send men before us, so that they may make the land beloved by us, and bring us word again of the way by which we must go up, and the cities into which we shall come.ʼ
And the thing pleased me well. And I took twelve men of you, one man for every tribe.
And they turned and went up into the hill country, and came to the valley of Ishkol, and spied it out.
And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down to us, and brought us word again and said, ʻIt is a good land which Shema our God gives us.ʼ
Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of Shema your God.
And you murmured in your tents and said, ʻBecause Shema hates us, he has brought us out of the land of Miṣrem, to deliver us into the hand of the Emarites, to destroy us.

Where are we going up while our brothers have made our heart to melt, saying, ʻThe people are greater and more numerous than we are, the cities are great and fortified up to heaven, and moreover we have seen the sons of the Enaqem there.’
Then I said to you, ʻDo not be in dread or afraid of them.
Shema your God who goes before you, he himself will fight for you, just as he did for you in Miṣrem before your eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you have seen how Shema your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place.ʼ
Yet, behold, in spite of this thing, you did not believe in Shema your God,
who goes before you in the way to seek you out a place to encamp, in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
And Shema heard the voice of your words and was angered, and he swore saying,
‘Surely not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore [to give] to your fathers,
except Kilab the son of Yefanni. He shall see it, and to him and to his children I will give the land on which he has trodden, because he has wholly followed Shema.ʼ
Shema was angry with me also for your sakes, saying, ʻYou also shall not go in there.
Yeʾusha the son of Non, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Encourage him, for he shall cause Yishraʾel to inherit it.
Moreover your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your children, they shall go in there, and to them I will give it, and they shall possess it.
But as for you, turn, and take your journey into the wilderness in the direction of the sea of Sof.ʼ

Then you answered, and said to me, ʻWe have sinned against Shema our God. We will go up and fight against him, just as Shema our God commanded us.ʼ And everyone of you fastened his weapons of war, and thought it easy to go up into the hill country.
And Shema said to me, ʻSay to them, ʻDo not go up or fight, for I am not in your midst, lest you be defeated before your enemies.’
So I spoke to you, and you did not listen, but you rebelled against the commandment of Shema your God, and were presumptuous and went up into the hill country.
And the ʿAmaleqite and the Kaˈnanite that dwelt in that hill country, came out against you, and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Shaʾer, as far as Irma.
And you returned and wept before Shema, but Shema did not listen to your voice or gave ear to you.
So you remained at Qadesh many days according to the days that you remained [there].
Then we turned and journeyed into the wilderness in the direction of the sea of Sof, as Shema told me. And we circled Mount Shaʾer many days.
And Shema spoke to me, saying,
ʻYou have circled this mountain long enough. Turn northward,
and command the people, saying, ʻYou are about to pass through the border of your brothers the children of Ishab, who dwell in Shaʾer, and they will be afraid of you. So take good heed to yourselves.
Do not contend with them, for I will not give you a possession of their land. No, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Shaʾer to Ishab for a possession.
You shall purchase food from them for money, that you may eat, and you shall also buy water from them for money, that you may drink.ʼ

For Shema your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your going through this great wilderness. These forty years Shema your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing. [a] And I sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, [b] ʻLet me pass, I pray you, through your land. I will not pass through field or vineyard, neither will we drink water of a cistern. We will go along the kingʼs highway. We will not turn aside to the right hand or to the left, until we have passed your territory.ʼ [c] And He said, ʻYou shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.ʼ

So we went on, away from our brothers the children of Ishab, who dwell in Shaʾer, away from the ʿAraba road from Ayyalat and Iṣṣiyyon-gebar. And we turned and went in the direction of the wilderness of Muwwab.
And Shema said to me, ʻDo not harass Muwwab or contend with him, for I will not give you of his land for a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Loṭ for a possession.’
(The Imem dwelt there formerly, a people great and many, and tall as the Enaqem.
But the Muwwabites call them Imem.

The Arrites also dwelt in Shaʾer formerly, but the children of Ishab dispossessed them, and God destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their stead, as Yishraʾel did to the land of his possession, which Shema gave to them.)
ʻAnd now rise up, take your journey and get over the brook Zarad.ʼ And we went over the brook Zarad.

And the days in which we came from Qadesh-birna until we went over the brook Zarad were thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of war was consumed from the midst of the camp, as Shema had sworn to them.
Moreover the hand of Shema was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp, until they were consumed.
So when all the men of war were consumed and were dead from among the people,
Shema said to me, saying,
ʻYou are this day to pass over Ar, the border of Muwwab.

And when you come near [the border of] the children of ʿAmmon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you of the land of the children of ʿAmmon for a possession, because I have given it to the children of Loṭ for a possession.
(That also is accounted a land of Refaʾem. Refaʾem dwelt there formerly, but the ʿAmmonites call them Zamzamem,
a people great and many, and tall as the Enaqem, but Shema destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their stead,
as he did for the children of Ishab that dwell in Shaʾer when he destroyed the Arrites from before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their stead even to this day.
And the Ibbem that dwelt in Aṣirem as far as ʿAzza, the Kaftarrem that came out of Kaftar destroyed them and dwelt in their stead.)

ʻRise up, take your journey and pass over the valley of the Arenan. Behold, I have given into your hand Siyyon the Emarite, king of Ishbon, and his land. Begin to possess it and contend with him in battle.
This day begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples who are under the whole heaven, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of you.
And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Qadamot to Siyyon king of Ishbon with words of peace, saying,
ʻLet me pass through your land. I will go along by the king’s highway; I will not turn aside neither to the right hand nor to the left.
You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat, and give me water for money, that I may drink. Only let me pass through on my feet,
as the children of Ishab that dwell in Shaʾer, and the Muwwabites that dwell in Ar, did to me, until I shall pass over the Yardan into the land which Shema our God gives us.ʼ
But Siyyon king of Ishbon would not let us pass by him, for Shema your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into your hand, as at this day.
And Shema said to me, ʻBehold, I have begun to deliver up Siyyon the Emarite, king of Ishbon, and his land before you. Begin to take possession, that you may inherit his land.ʼ
Then Siyyon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Yēṣṣa.
And Shema our God delivered him up before us, and we struck down him and his sons and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time and completely devoted to destruction all his cities, the women and the little ones, without leaving him any remaining.
Only the cattle we took for plunder to ourselves, with the spoil of the cities which we had taken.

From ʿArˈʿar, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arenan, and [from] the city that is in the valley, as far as to Gaˈlad, there was not a city too high for us. Shema our God delivered up all into our hands.
Only to the land of the children of ʿAmmon no hand drew near, [that is] the river Yibbaq and the cities of the hill country and whatever Shema our God had forbidden us.
Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan, and Ūg the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Idri.

And Shema said to me, ʻDo not fear him, for I have delivered him and all his people and his land into your hand, and you shall do to him as you did to Siyyon king of the Emarites, who dwelt at Ishbon.ʼ
So Shema our God delivered into our hand Ūg also, the king of Bashan, and all his people, and we struck him down until none was left remaining.
And we took all his cities at that time—there was not a city which we did not take from them—sixty cities, all the region of Argab, the kingdom of Ūg in Bashan.
All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides the great many unwalled towns.
And we devoted them to destruction, as we did to Siyyon king of Ishbon, completely devoting to destruction every city, with the women and the little ones.
But all the cattle and the spoil of the cities we took for plunder to ourselves.
And we took the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Emarites that were beyond the Yardan, from the valley of the Arenan to Mount ʿArmon
(the Ṣidonites call ʿArmon Sharen, and the Emarites call it Shinner),
all the cities of the plain and all Gaˈlad and all Bashan, to Silka and Idri, cities of the kingdom of Ūg in Bashan.

For only Ūg king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Refaʾem. Behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron. It is in Ribbat-bani-ʿammon! Nine cubits was its length, and four cubits its breadth, after the cubit of a man!

And this land we took for possession at that time: from ʿArˈʿar, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arenan, and half the hill country of Gaˈlad, and its cities, I gave to the Reʾubenites and to the Gadites.
And the rest of Gaˈlad, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Ūg, that is, all the region of Argab, I gave to the half-tribe of Manashi. (All that [portion] of Bashan is called the land of Refaʾem.
And Yaʾer the son of Manashi took all the region of Argab, to the border of the Gishurites and the Makkeites, and called them—that is, Bashan—after his own name, Uwwat-yaʾer, to this day.)
And I gave Gaˈlad to Maker.

And to the Reʾubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gaˈlad as far as the valley of the Arenan, the middle of the valley, and [its] border, as far as over the river Yibbaq, which is the boundary of the children of ʿAmmon;
the ʿAraba also, and the Yardan, and [its] border, [from] Amkinnaret as far as the sea of the ʿAraba, the Salt Sea, under Ashadotaffasga on the east.
And I commanded you at that time, saying, ʻShema your God has given you this land to possess. You shall pass over armed before your brothers the children of Yishraʾel, all the men of valour.
But your little ones and your wives and your cattle—I know that you have much cattle—shall abide in your cities which I have given you,

until Shema gives rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also possess the land which Shema your God gives them beyond the Yardan. Then you shall return every man to his possession which I have given you.ʼ
And I commanded Yeʾusha at that time, saying, ʻYour eyes have seen what Shema has done to these two kings. So shall Shema do to all the kingdoms into which you are going over.
You shall not fear them, for it is Shema your God who fights for you.ʼ —
And I besought Shema at that time, saying,
ʻO Lord Shema, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such works and mighty acts as yours?
Let me go over, I pray you, and see the good land that is beyond the Yardan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.ʼ
But Shema was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. And Shema said to me, ʻLet it suffice you. Speak no more to me of this matter.
Get up to the top of Affasga and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and behold with your eyes, for you shall not go over this Yardan.
But charge Yeʾusha, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you shall see.ʼ
So we abode in Giyya opposite Bet-fūr.
And now, O Yishraʾel, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances which I teach you, to do them, that you may live and go in and possess the land which Shema, the God of your fathers, gives you.
You shall not add to the word which I command you today, neither shall you diminish from it, that you may keep the commandments of Shema your God which I command you.
Your eyes have seen what Shema did because of Bāl-fūr, for all the men that followed Bāl-fūr, Shema your God has destroyed them from your midst.
But you that did cleave to Shema your God are alive everyone of you this day.
See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as Shema my God commanded me, that you should do so in the land which you are going into to take possession of it.

Keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples that shall hear all these statutes, and say, ʻSurely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.ʼ
For what great nation is there, that has a god so near to them as Shema our God is whenever we call upon him?
And what great nation is there, that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

Only take heed to yourself and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes saw, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life, but make them known to your children and your childrenʼs children.

The day that you stood before Shema your God in Ureb when Shema said to me, ʻGather the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.ʼ
And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven, [with] darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
And Shema spoke to you out of the midst of the fire. You heard the voice of words, but you saw no form, nothing but a voice.
And he declared to you his covenant which he commanded you to perform, the ten commandments, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
And Shema commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land which you go over to possess.
Take then good heed to yourselves, for you saw no manner of form on the day that Shema spoke to you in Ureb out of the midst of the fire,
lest you act corruptly, and make yourselves a graven image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
the likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth,

and lest you lift up your eyes to heaven, and when you see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, you be drawn away and worship them and serve them, [things] which Shema your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.
But Shema has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Miṣrem, to be to him a people of inheritance, as at this day.
Furthermore, Shema was angry with me because of you, so that I should not go over the Yardan, and that I should not go into the good land which Shema your God gives you for an inheritance.
For I must die in this land. I must not go over the Yardan, but you shall go over and possess that good land.
Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of Shema your God, which he made with you, and make a graven image in the form of anything which Shema your God has forbidden you.
For Shema your God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.

When you shall beget children and childrenʼs children, and you shall have been long in the land and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image in the form of anything, and shall do that which is evil in the sight of Shema your God, to provoke him to anger,

I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall soon utterly perish from off the land which you are going over the Yardan to take possession of it. You will not prolong your days in it, but shall utterly be destroyed.
And Shema will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations, where Shema shall lead you away.
And there you shall serve gods, the work of menʼs hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
But from there you shall ask after Shema your God, and you shall find him, when you seek after him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in tribulation, and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days you shall return to Shema your God and obey his voice.
For Shema your God is a merciful God. He will not fail you or destroy you or forget the covenant of your fathers which he swore to them.

For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven to the other, whether there has been [any such thing] as this great thing is, or has been heard like it.
Did ever a people hear the voice of a living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?

Or has God attempted to go and take him a nation from the midst of [another] nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great sights, according to all that Shema your God did for you in Miṣrem before your eyes?
To you it was shown, that you might know that Shema is God. There is none else besides him.
Out of heaven he let you hear his voice, that he might instruct you, and upon earth he let you see his great fire, and you heard his words out of the midst of the fire.
And because he loved your fathers, therefore he chose their descendant after them and brought you out with his presence and with his great power, out of Miṣrem,
to drive out nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as at this day.
Know therefore this day, and lay it to your heart, that Shema is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath. There is none else.

And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments, which I command you this day, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which Shema your God gives you forever.”
Then Mushi set apart three cities beyond the Yardan in the east,
that the murderer might flee there, anyone that kills his neighbour unwittingly, and did not hate him in time past, and in fleeing to one of these cities he might live:
Buṣar in the wilderness, in the plain country, for the Reʾubenites, and Rimot in Gaˈlad for the Gadites, and Gulan in Bashan for the Manashites.
And this is the law which Mushi set before the children of Yishraʾel:
These are the testimonies, the statutes and the ordinances, which Mushi spoke to the children of Yishraʾel when they came out of Miṣrem,
beyond the Yardan, in Giyya opposite Bet-fūr, in the land of Siyyon king of the Emarites, who dwelt at Ishbon, whom Mushi and the children of Yishraʾel struck down when they came out of Miṣrem.
And they took his land in possession, and the land of Ūg king of Bashan, the two kings of the Emarites, who were beyond the Yardan to the east.
From ʿArˈʿar, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arenan, as far as Mount Shiyyon—that is, ʿArmon,
and all the ʿAraba beyond the Yardan eastward as far as the sea of the ʿAraba, the Salt Sea, under Ashadot-affasga.
And Mushi called to all Yishraʾel and said to them: “Hear, O Yishraʾel, the statutes and the ordinances which I speak in your hearing this day, that you may learn them, and be careful to do them.
Shema our God made a covenant with us in Ureb.
Shema did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, who are all of us here alive this day.
Shema spoke with you face to face in the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
as I stood between Shema and you at that time, to show you the words of Shema, for you were afraid because of the fire, and did not go up into the mountain, saying,
ʻI am Shema your God, who brought you out of the land of Miṣrem, out of the house of bondage.

A You shall have no other gods before me. You shall not make yourself a graven image, or any likeness [of anything] that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.
You shall not worship nor serve them, for I, Shema your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me,
and showing lovingkindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
B You shall not take the name of Shema your God in vain, for Shema will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.
C Observe the Sabbath day, for it is holy, as Shema your God commanded you.
Six days you shall labour, and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Shema your God. In it you shall not do any work: you, or your son, or your daughter, [or] your man-servant, or your maid-servant, [or] your ox, or your ass, or any of your cattle, or your stranger that is within your cities, that your man-servant and your maid-servant may rest as well as you.

And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Miṣrem, and Shema your God brought you out from there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore Shema your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
D Honour your father and your mother, as Shema your God commanded you, that your days may be long, and that it may go well with you in the land which Shema your God gives you.
E You shall not kill. F You shall not commit adultery. G You shall not steal. H You shall not bear false witness against your neighbour.

I You shall not covet your neighbourʼs house, neither shall you covet your neighbourʼs wife, his field, his man-servant, or his maid-servant, his ox, or his ass, or anything that is your neighbourʼs. J [a] And when Shema your God shall bring you into the land of the Kaˈnanite to which you are entering to take possession of it, [b] you shall set up large stones, and plaster them with plaster. [c] And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this law. [d] And when you have passed over the Yardan, you shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, in [Mount] Ārgarizem. [e] And there you shall build an altar to Shema your God, an altar of stones; you shall lift up no iron tool upon them. [f] You shall build an altar to Shema your God of unhewn stones, and you shall offer burned offerings on it to Shema your God. [g] And you shall sacrifice peace offerings, and shall eat there. And you shall rejoice before Shema your God. [h] That mountain beyond the Yardan, behind the way of the setting of the sun, in the land of the Kaˈnanites who live in the ʿAraba, op- posite Galgal, beside Alon-mura, opposite Ashkem.ʼ

These words Shema spoke to all your assembly in the mountain out of the midst of the fire, [with] darkness, cloud, and thick darkness, [with] a great voice, and he added no more. And he wrote them upon two tablets of stone, and gave them to me.
And when you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes, and your elders,

and you said, ʻBehold, Shema our God has shown us his glory, and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire. We have seen this day that God does speak with man, and he lives.
Now therefore why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of Shema our God any more, then we shall die.
For who is there of all flesh, that has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and has still lived?
Go near and hear all that Shema our God shall say, and you will speak to us all that Shema our God will speak to you, and we will hear it and do it.ʼ

And Shema heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me. And Shema said to me, ʻI have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. They have well said all that they have spoken.
Oh that there were such a heart in them, that they would fear me, and keep my commandments always, that it might be well with them, and with their children forever!
Go say to them, ʻReturn to your tents.ʼ
But you, stand here by me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which you shall teach them, that they may do them in the land which I give them to possess.ʼ
You shall be careful to do therefore as Shema your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
You shall walk in all the way which Shema your God has commanded you, that you may live, and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which you shall possess.
Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Shema your God commanded to teach you, that you might do them in the land to which you go over to possess,

that you might fear Shema your God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you today, you and your son and your sonʼs son, all the days of your life, and that your days may be long.

Hear therefore, O Yishraʾel, and be careful to do [it], that it may be well with you, and that you may increase mightily, as Shema, the God of your fathers, has promised you, [in] a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, O Yishraʾel: Shema our God is one Shema.
And you shall love Shema your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
And these words which I command you this day shall be upon your heart.
And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in the house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.
And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hands, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
And you shall write them upon the door-posts of your houses and upon your gates.
And it shall be, when Shema your God shall bring you into the land which he swore to your fathers, to Abˈram, to Yeˈṣaq, and to Yāqob, to give you, great and goodly cities which you did not build,
houses full of all good things which you did not fill, cisterns hewn out, which you did not hew, vineyards and olive-trees which you did not plant, and you shall eat and be full,
then take heed lest you forget Shema your God who brought you out of the land of Miṣrem, out of the house of bondage.
You shall fear Shema your God, and him you shall serve, and shall swear by his name.
You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples that are round about you,
for Shema your God in your midst is a jealous God, lest the anger of Shema your God be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the face of the earth.
You shall not try Shema your God, as you tried [him] in Massa.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of Shema your God, and his testimonies and his statutes, which he has commanded you.
And you shall do that which is right and good in the sight of Shema your God, that it may be well with you and that you may go in, and possess the good land which Shema swore to your fathers,
to thrust out all your enemies from before you, as Shema has spoken.
And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ʻWhat mean the testimonies, the statutes and the ordinances, which Shema our God has commanded you?ʼ
then you shall say to your son, ʻWe were Faruʼs slaves in Miṣrem, and Shema brought us out of Miṣrem with a mighty hand,
and Shema showed signs and wonders, great and grievous, against Miṣrem, against Faru and against all his house, before our eyes,
and he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in to give us the land which Shema swore to our fathers.
And Shema commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Shema our God for our good always, and that he might preserve us alive, as at this day.
And it shall be righteousness to us, if we be careful to do all this commandment before Shema our God, as he has commanded us.ʼ

When Shema your God brings you into the land which you are entering to take possession of it, and casts out many nations before you, the Atite, and the Girgeshite, and the Emarite, and the Kaˈnanite, and the Ferizzite, and the Ibbite, and the Yebusite, seven nations greater and mightier than you,
and when Shema your God delivers them up before you, and you strike them down, then you must utterly destroy them. You shall make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
You shall not make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give to his son, or his daughter you shall not take to your son.
For he will turn away your son from following me, that he may serve other gods, and the anger of Shema will be kindled against you, and he will destroy you quickly.
But thus you shall deal with them: You shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and hew down their Asherim, and burn their graven images with fire.
For you are a holy people to Shema your God, and Shema your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession above all peoples that are upon the face of the earth.
Shema did not set his love upon you or choose you because you were more in number than any people, for, oh, you were the fewest of all peoples,

but because Shema loves you, and because he would keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, has Shema brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Faru king of Miṣrem.
Know therefore that Shema your God he is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and lovingkindness with those who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
and repays those who hate him while they are living, by destroying them. He will not be slack with them who hate him. He will repay them while they are living.
You shall therefore keep the commandment, the statutes and the ordinances, which I command you this day, to do them.
And because you listen to these ordinances and keep and do them, Shema your God will keep with you the covenant and the lovingkindness which he swore to your fathers.

And he will love you, and bless you, and multiply you. He will also bless the fruit of your body and the fruit of your ground, your grain, your new wine, and your oil, the increase of your cattle, and the young of your flock, in the land which Shema swore to your fathers to give you.
You shall be blessed above all peoples. There shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle.
And Shema will take away from you all sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Miṣrem which you know, will he put upon you, but will lay them upon all those who hate you.
And you shall consume all the peoples that Shema your God shall deliver to you. Your eye shall not pity them, neither shall you serve their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
If you shall say in your heart, ʻThese nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?ʼ
you shall not be afraid of them, [but] you shall well remember what Shema your God did to Faru and to all Miṣrem,

the great trials which your eyes saw, the signs, and the wonders, and the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, whereby Shema your God brought you out, so shall Shema your God do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
Moreover Shema your God will send the hornet among them, until they that are left and hide themselves perish from before you.

You shall not be in dread of them, for Shema your God is in your midst, a great and terrible God. those nations from before you little by little. You may not consume them at once, lest the beasts of the field increase upon you.
But Shema your God will deliver them up before you and will throw them into great confusion, until he destroys them.
And he will deliver their kings into your hand, and you shall make their name perish from under heaven. No man shall be able to stand before you, until you have destroyed them.

The graven images of their gods you shall burn with fire. You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, or take it for yourselves, lest you be ensnared by it, for it is abominations to Shema your God.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest it, and you shall utterly abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.
All the commandment which I command you this day you shall be careful to do, that you may live and multiply, and go in and possess the land which Shema swore to your fathers.

And you shall remember all the way which Shema your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not.

And he humbled you and let you hunger and fed you with manna, which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, that he might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds out of the mouth of Shema does man live.
Your clothing did not wear out upon you, and your feet did not swell these forty years.
And you shall consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so Shema your God disciplines you.
And you shall keep the commandments of Shema your God, to walk in his ways and to fear him.
For Shema your God brings you to a good and broad land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and springs, flowing in valleys and hills;
a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig-trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive-trees and honey,
a land in which you shall eat bread without scarceness, you shall not lack anything in it, a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you may dig copper.
And you shall eat and be full, and you shall bless Shema your God for the good land which he has given you.
Take heed lest you forget Shema your God in not keeping his commandments and his ordinances and his statutes, which I command you this day,
lest when you have eaten and are full and have built goodly houses and dwelt [in them],
and when your herds and your flocks multiply, and your silver and your gold is multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Shema your God, who brought you out of the land of Miṣrem, out of the house of bondage,
who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, [with its] fiery serpents, scorpions, and thirsty ground where there was no water, who brought you water out of the rock of flint,
who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, that he might humble you and test you, to do you good in the end.
[Beware lest] you say in your heart, ʻMy power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth.ʼ

But you shall remember Shema your God, for it is he that gives you power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he swore to your fathers to Abˈram, to Yeˈṣaq and to Yāqob, as at this day.
And it shall be, if you shall forget Shema your God and walk after other gods and serve them and worship them, I testify against you this day that you shall surely perish.
As the nations that Shema makes to perish before you, so shall you perish, because you would not obey the voice of Shema your God.
Hear, O Yishraʾel: You are to pass over the Yardan this day, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourself, cities great and fortified up to heaven,
a people great and tall, the sons of the Enaqem, whom you know and of whom you have heard said ʻWho can stand before the sons of Enaq?ʼ

Know therefore this day that Shema your God is he who goes over before you as a devouring fire. He will destroy them and he will bring them down before you. So shall you drive them out and make them perish quickly, as Shema has spoken to you.

Do not say in your heart, after Shema your God has thrust them out before you, saying, ʻFor my righteousness Shema has brought me in to possess this land,ʼ whereas for the wickedness of these nations Shema does drive them out before you.

Not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land, but for the wickedness of these nations Shema is driving them out before you, and that he may establish the word which he swore to your fathers, to Abˈram, to Yeˈṣaq, and to Yāqob.
Know therefore that Shema your God does not give you this good land to possess for your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember and do not forget how you provoked Shema your God to wrath in the wilderness. From the day that you went out of the land of Miṣrem until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against Shema.
Also in Ureb you pro- voked Shema to wrath, and Shema was angry with you to destroy you.

When I went up into the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which Shema made with you, then I abode in the mountain forty days and forty nights. I neither ate bread nor drank water.

And Shema delivered to me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words which Shema spoke to you in the mountain out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly.
And at the end of forty days and forty nights Shema gave me the two tablets of the covenant.

And Shema said to me, ʻArise, get down quickly from here, for your people that you have brought out of Miṣrem have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them. They have made themselves a molten calf.ʼ
Furthermore Shema spoke to me, saying, ʻI have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
Let me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. And I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they.ʼ
So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
And I looked, and behold, you had sinned against Shema your God. You had made yourselves a molten calf. You had turned aside quickly out of the way which Shema had commanded you.
And I took hold of the two tablets and cast them out of my two hands and broke them before your eyes.

And I fell down before Shema as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I neither ate bread nor drank water, because of all your sins which you sinned in doing that which was evil in the sight of Shema to provoke him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure which Shema was wroth against you to destroy you. But Shema listened to me that time also.
And Shema was very angry with Ārron, [wanting] to destroy him, and I prayed for Ārron also at the same time.

And I took your sins, the calf which you had made, and burned it with fire and stamped it, grinding it very small, until it was as fine as dust, and I cast the dust of it into the brook that descended out of the mountain.
And at Tebara and at Massa and at Qabarot-attawwa you provoked Shema to wrath.

And when Shema sent you from Qadesh-birna, saying, ʻGo up and possess the land which I have given you,ʼ then you rebelled against the commandment of Shema your God, and you did not believe him or obey his voice.
You have been rebellious against Shema from the day that he knew you.
So I fell down before Shema the forty days and forty nights that I fell down, because Shema had said he would destroy you.

And I prayed to Shema, and said, ʻO Lord Shema, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, that you have redeemed through your greatness, that you have brought out of Miṣrem with your mighty hand.
Remember your servants, Abˈram, Yeˈṣaq, and Yāqob. Do not look to the stubbornness of this people, or to their wickedness or to their sin,

lest the people of the land from which you brought us out say, ʻBecause Shema was not able to bring them into the land which he promised to them, and because he hated them, he has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.ʼ
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, which you brought out from Miṣrem by your great power and by your outstretched arm.ʼ
At that time Shema said to me, ʻHew two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to me on the mountain and make an ark of wood.
And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.ʼ
So I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tablets of stone like the first, and went up on the mountain, having the two tablets in my hand.
And he wrote on the tablets, as at the first writing the ten commandments which Shema spoke to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly, and Shema gave them to me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark which I had made, and there they are, as Shema commanded me.
And the children of Yishraʾel journeyed from Masirot, and encamped in Bani-yaqan.

From there they journeyed and encamped in Aggidgeda. From there they journeyed and encamped in Yeṭibta, a land of brooks of water. From there they journeyed and encamped in Ebirna. From there they journeyed and encamped in Iṣṣiyyon-gebar. From there they journeyed and encamped in the wilderness of Ṣen—that is, Kadesh. From there they journeyed and encamped in Mount Ar. And Ārron died there, and he was buried there. And Elāzar his son ministered in the priestʼs office in his stead.
At that time Shema set apart the tribe of Libi to bear the ark of the covenant of Shema, to stand before Shema to minister to him and to bless in his name, to this day.
Therefore Libi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers; Shema is his inheritance, as Shema your God said to him.
And I stayed on the mountain, as at the first time, forty days and forty nights, and Shema listened to me that time also, and Shema was unwilling to destroy you.
And Shema said to me, ʻArise, take your journey before this people, and they shall go in and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give to them.ʼ

And now, Yishraʾel, what does Shema your God require of you, but to fear Shema your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Shema your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commandments of Shema your God and his statutes, which I command you this day for your good?
Behold, to Shema your God belongs heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is in it.
Only Shema had a delight in your fathers to love them, and he chose their offspring after them, you above all peoples, as at this day.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be stiff-necked no more.
For Shema your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and terrible God, who is not partial and takes no bribe.
He executes justice for the orphan and widow, and loves the sojourner, giving him food and clothing.
Love therefore the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Miṣrem.
You shall fear Shema your God, and him you shall serve, and to him you shall cleave, and by his name you shall swear.
He is your praise, and he is your God, that has done for you these great and terrible things which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down to Miṣrem seventy persons, and now Shema your God has made you as the stars of heaven for multitude.
Therefore you shall love Shema your God and keep his charge, his ordinances and his commandments and his statutes always.
And know this day, for [I speak] not with your children, that have not known and that have not seen the chastisement of Shema your God, his greatness, and his mighty hand and his outstretched arm,
his signs, and his works, which he did in the midst of Miṣrem to Faru and to all his land,

and what he did to the army of Miṣrem, to their horses, and to their chariots; how he made the water of the sea of Sof flow over them as they pursued after you, and how Shema has destroyed them to this day,
and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place,

and what he did to Datan and Abiram, the sons of Ilyab, the son of Reʾuben; how the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up and all the men that appertained to Qara, and their house-holds and their tents, and every living thing that followed them in the midst of all Yishraʾel.
But your eyes have seen all the great work of Shema which he did.
